stories.Headline: Trump administration plans to designate over two dozen AI firms as national champions
stories.Summary:
The Trump administration plans to designate over two dozen artificial intelligence firms as national champions. This initiative aims to help these American companies expand overseas and compete against Chinese technology firms. The Wall Street Journal reported these plans on Sunday, November 16, 2026. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is expected to unveil the selected companies, possibly within one week. The administration intends to use this label to mark the government picking favorite industry players.

The list includes Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Anthropic, among more than twenty-four other firms. Selected companies may receive federal financing, government support for overseas operations, and faster export license reviews. This builds on the American AI Exports Program established by Executive Order 14320 on July 23, 2025. The Commerce Department noted that industry-led groups submitted 78 applications under this program by July 2026. US chips and AI models will be bundled into packages to counter rivals like Huawei.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Nvidia needs a dramatic shakeup and should seek an external leadership candidate. Bessent told Fox News that the board must look outside the company for a new leader. He demanded answers within ten days regarding the company's compliance culture and adherence to US export restrictions. President Trump has publicly defended Jensen Huang despite intensified scrutiny over foreign intelligence concerns and personal relationships. The administration views these companies as flag-bearers for a strategic industry with a shared mission.

Critics argue that Nvidia contributing over 26 million dollars to Trump-related projects raises potential conflicts of interest. This spending includes a 25 million dollar pledge toward the White House ballroom, according to reports. Rivals like AMD and OpenAI are affected because only one company is reportedly on track for the title. These competitors may push for similar recognition or for limits on a single company's policy weight. Foreign governments and businesses are the intended customers for the integrated American AI technology packages.

Nvidia committed 1 billion dollars to the Genesis Mission, a federal program involving fourteen different government agencies. This was the largest industry pledge, exceeding AMD's 500 million dollars and OpenAI's 200 million dollar commitment. Total industry commitments to the mission exceed 2.4 billion dollars to support energy, health, and space research. On October 8, 2026, President Trump awarded Jensen Huang the National Medal of Science at a summit. US manufacturing pledges of 500 billion dollars over four years starting in 2025 linked to Huang.

President Trump will travel to Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit on November 18 and 19. He is expected to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping during this trip to discuss trade and technology. The articles leave open whether the champion designation will be formalized and what specific benefits will attach. It remains unclear if the White House will continue backing Huang if the current scrutiny intensifies further. The company has not publicly confirmed a successor after reportedly approaching Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas.

stories.Headline: Microsoft unveils six specialized AI models at Ignite to rival OpenAI and Anthropic on cost
stories.Summary:
Microsoft unveiled six specialized AI models at its Ignite conference in San Francisco on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, and its executives pitched them as cheaper alternatives to OpenAI and Anthropic. Judson Althoff, CEO of Microsoft's commercial business, said anything possible in Claude or ChatGPT could be done better with Copilot and for less. Jacob Andreou, Microsoft's executive vice president of Copilot, said Anthropic and OpenAI force compromise on power and collaboration with simplified viewers and editors. Microsoft AI released a new batch of its own MAI models built to compete with OpenAI and Anthropic for a fraction of the price. CEO Satya Nadella announced on the same stage that OpenAI's GPT-6.2, released Tuesday morning, is now available in Microsoft Foundry.

The lineup includes MAI Code 2, available in GitHub Copilot starting Tuesday, which Microsoft says delivers 96% of the coding performance of Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the price on benchmarks Microsoft chose. Microsoft also introduced MAI Cyber 2. Andreou backed the pitch with a chart of estimated monthly costs per business user, including subscription and usage fees, putting Copilot at $30 for an everyday AI user against $81 for ChatGPT and $205 for Claude. For advanced users of each company's agent tools, it showed $96 for Copilot, $149 for ChatGPT and $299 for Claude, with most of the Claude figure estimated usage charges on top of Anthropic's $20 enterprise seat. The numbers come from research Microsoft commissioned and paid for from GigaOm, based on testing Microsoft ran in October on modeled workloads, and reflect enterprise pricing that adds usage charges to a per-seat fee rather than the flat monthly subscriptions individuals pay.

Althoff said simply that anything you can do in Claude or ChatGPT, you can do better with Copilot and for less. Andreou said Anthropic and OpenAI have embraced documents, slides and spreadsheets, but their simplified viewers and editors force compromise on power and collaboration. Andreou said the full versions of Word, Excel and PowerPoint inside Copilot are included in the subscription, which means Copilot is the only way to draft a PowerPoint presentation without spinning a meter. A Microsoft spokesperson, discussing a separate report on workplace AI costs, said AI is not just a technological trend but a transformative tool that, if adopted wisely, can yield significant returns. The same spokesperson said seeing AI as a long-term investment rather than a short-term solution can shift the narrative around its costs.

The pitch comes as Anthropic expands into Microsoft's core business, having introduced new Claude-based tools for spreadsheets and whiteboards last week that compete more directly with Office. Anthropic is expected to make its IPO this week, putting new scrutiny on its financials and long-term growth prospects. Anthropic's Claude for Microsoft 365 lets people use Claude inside Office apps for tasks such as sorting email and creating slide decks, but the product has less than a tenth as many weekly users as the paid version of Copilot in Office, The Information reported Monday citing internal Microsoft data. Andreou is one of the executives who see that as a sign Microsoft can keep customers from switching, the report said. Microsoft is a partner and investor in both OpenAI and Anthropic and sells their AI models to its own customers, yet another role was on full display during the keynote: competitor.

The Microsoft report on workplace AI costs points out that AI can reduce labor costs through automation, optimize decision-making and enhance customer engagement. It says startups in the retail sector can use AI-driven analytics to predict customer behavior, stock inventory more efficiently and trim unnecessary costs, and that AI chatbots handle routine inquiries so human staff can address more complex issues. It warns that implementation often comes with upfront expenses from software licensing fees to new hardware, that personnel may need training, and that ongoing maintenance and updates add to the total cost of ownership. It notes compatibility is a significant challenge for small businesses with limited technological infrastructure, since integrating AI may demand custom setups and a reassessment of current technology stacks. It adds that data privacy concerns are critical because fines and reputational damage from breaches or misuse could outweigh potential gains, and it advises owners to define goals, set a realistic budget and remain adaptable.

Nadella kicked off Microsoft Ignite with an Outlook outage mea culpa, saying the company has work to do. Microsoft still sells OpenAI's and Anthropic's models alongside its own MAI lineup. The articles leave open how the six specialized models are named beyond MAI Code 2 and MAI Cyber 2, and what the remaining models do. They leave open how Anthropic's expected IPO prices and what its filings will show. They leave open whether the GigaOm cost estimates will be independently verified, and how customers will respond to Microsoft competing with the partners whose models it sells.

stories.Headline: India, the US and eight other nations sign a declaration to protect AI supply chains
stories.Summary:
India, the United States, and eight other nations signed a joint declaration to safeguard artificial intelligence supply chains on November 15, 2026. This agreement was signed during a meeting of the founders of the US-led Pax Silica initiative. US Under Secretary of State for Economic Affairs Jacob Helberg convened the retreat in San Francisco. The nations aim to treat the protection of these supply chains as a shared endeavour. This move comes amid growing competition with China in the field of emerging technology.

The San Francisco Declaration on the Secure Foundations of Enduring Prosperity involves Australia, India, Israel, Japan, South Korea, Qatar, Singapore, the UAE, and the UK. It defines sensitive technologies as goods, software, knowledge, components, inputs, and means of production used in AI supply chains. Critical infrastructure includes ports, terminals, transport, communications, logistics networks, information technology, and digital platforms. The agreement proposes five working groups covering pro-innovation policy frameworks, SI adoption, supply chain cooperation, security hubs, and resilience. The US government now refers to artificial intelligence as super intelligence, or SI, following an executive order by President Donald Trump.

The US State Department issued a statement saying that economic security is fundamental to national security. They stated that no nation can secure the foundations of the SI era alone. The department noted that prosperity will only be as durable as the underlying infrastructure and supply chains. By agreeing on what to protect, the participants are laying foundations for partner nations to innovate and grow. The statement added that the coalition is now cementing shared principles into a working partnership with a common baseline.

The declaration notes that sensitive technologies could provide military advantages or create undue economic leverage if misused or transferred without authorization. It warns that hostile control or unauthorized exposure of data flowing through critical systems could cause significant harm. The signatories believe AI resilience is best achieved through diversified, trusted supply chains and building trusted capabilities. They called for protecting private investment and ensuring a level playing field for innovation and growth. India is affected as it seeks to expand domestic manufacturing in semiconductors while reducing reliance on foreign sources.

The US announced the Pax Silica initiative in December of last year to secure supply chains for silicon and other minerals. These materials are essential for semiconductor production, which supports artificial intelligence and other advanced technological industries. The framework aims to build secure and resilient supply chains for critical minerals, semiconductors, and AI infrastructure. The San Francisco Declaration marks a new phase for Pax Silica less than a year after its launch. This multilateral platform allows India to coordinate with other economies on critical infrastructure and AI supply chains.

The participants will now establish the five proposed working groups to carry their common purpose into common practice. These groups will focus on policy frameworks, sector adoption, stack cooperation, security hubs, and general resilience. The nations will cooperate on the enforcement of policies to protect infrastructure from undue access, influence, or control. The articles do not state when these specific working groups will begin their official operations. They also leave open the specific details of how the nations will coordinate their respective enforcement policies.

stories.Headline: Google expands access to Genie 4 world model and launches Tasks AI assistant in India
stories.Summary:
Google began rolling out its Genie 4 AI world model more widely on November 18, 2026, Jay Peters reported for The Verge at 6:36 PM UTC. The model was initially released to trusted testers late last month, according to the article. Google says Genie 4 can generate more realistic virtual experiences. It is now available to eligible AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie. The Verge published the story under its Tech section on the same day.

The rollout follows Google's separate launch of its agentic AI assistant Tasks, formerly Gemini Sparks, to users in India, Inc42 reported on November 17, 2026. Josh Woodward, vice-president of Google Labs and the Gemini app, said the feature lets users assign tasks including making calls, booking appointments, comparing products and completing purchases. The service comes bundled for free with Google's new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model. Woodward said the update was rolling out free of charge for hundreds of millions of people across the US, Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia and India. Tasks was reportedly initially launched to select testers in May as Gemini Spark, an agentic AI helper, and was subsequently expanded to US-based subscribers of the Google AI Ultra tier.

Woodward said in a blog post that Gemini can draw on information already available within Google services, including Gmail, Calendar, Maps, Photos, files and payment cards, to carry out tasks on a user's behalf. He said Gemini can call businesses, wait through hold periods, identify available appointment slots and add bookings to a user's calendar. Under the hood, Gemini uses the agent payments protocol, AP2, to enable Tasks to make purchases online. Google said it plans to integrate the universal commerce protocol, UCP, into Gemini to further streamline the checkout experience. Google also said it is working with American Express, Mastercard and Visa to enable tokenised card transactions via Tasks, though it did not specify whether those partnerships extend to India.

Inc42 reported that India's inclusion in the initial rollout gives Google a large market to test consumer adoption of the personal AI assistant. Google has invited app developers to join its Connected Apps Platform, which could let Indian consumer, fintech, travel tech and foodtech brands build task-based third-party integrations with the assistant. Inc42 said adoption will depend on the availability of supported merchants, payment methods and third-party apps in the country, and that there appears to be no clarity on this front. The article said the launch is part of a broader wave of big tech giants rolling out personal AI assistants to capture the masses. It noted that in September, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg showcased Meta's offering called Muse, which allows an AI agent to send emails, fill forms, make plans and even make purchases autonomously.

Inc42 said OpenAI had earlier introduced Dots, which can draft board meeting decks, conduct background research and handle multi-step project management. It said xAI has also been developing Grok Bot, which sees cleaning up sales records and processing invoices as potential uses for agents. Microsoft is also pursuing agents built on OpenClaw, which can function as digital teammates, according to the article. The article said Emergent, better known for its vibe-coding platform, launched Wingman, an autonomous agent that handles routine actions and seeks approval before taking bigger steps. Inc42 also said that from Meta's Muse to OpenAI's Dots, a growing wave of big tech giants are rolling out personal AI assistants.

The Verge article listed other stories published on November 18, 2026, including one on Grand Theft Auto VI, one on Nvidia's rise and one on Instagram letting users edit stories after posting. It also listed a leaked Lenovo Legion Go Beam handheld, a piece on tech lawsuits defining 2026, and the first Nvidia RTX Spark mini PCs launching from Asus, Dell and MSI. The Verge article carried a most-popular item saying Satya Nadella says he is AGI-pilled now, and another on an Outlook outage at Microsoft. It also included an item saying Nvidia does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. The Verge piece ended with a comments section that was still loading.

Inc42 said Google could be looking to expand the role of AI assistants beyond answering questions to embedding them in daily life, unlike Gemini's Chat, which only generates responses to a user's queries. The article said Tasks goes one step further and enables the chatbot to perform basic functions. It said the features could make Gemini Tasks a channel for online shopping, bill payments and routine purchases. Inc42's page also displayed subscription offers for its Inc42 Plus membership, including a three-year plan at ₹29,999 reduced to ₹7,999, a two-year plan at ₹19,999 reduced to ₹5,999 and a one-year plan at ₹9,999 reduced to ₹3,499. The article did not say when Tasks would reach merchants or payment partners in India.

stories.Headline: US stocks fall as Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO amid spying allegations
stories.Summary:
Wall Street indices closed sharply lower on Monday, November 16, 2026, due to broad selloffs. Investors reacted to the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang following allegations of an affair. This event soured enthusiasm for artificial intelligence stocks and increased stakes for upcoming corporate events. The market faced jitters ahead of Nvidia earnings and an initial public offering for Anthropic. These combined factors led to a significant decline across the three major United States indices.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 739.38 points, or 1.41 per cent, to 51,608.17. The S&P 500 dropped 145.08 points, or 1.92 per cent, to 7,416.59, while the Nasdaq fell 626.51 points. The Nasdaq Composite ended at 24,509.76, representing a 2.49 per cent loss, and confirming a market correction. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index tumbled 5.3 per cent, and Nvidia shares slid by 4.1 per cent. The Trump administration issued a new rule restricting China's access to the best AI chips from Nvidia.

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh stated that new technologies will have a significant impact on the economy. He noted scenarios ranging from rising growth to higher unemployment if investment returns prove to be disappointing. Jensen Huang said he would be honored to return if the board decided it served the shareholders. He admitted to making serious mistakes and falling below the standards expected of the company's top leader. However, the Nvidia board and chairman stated they have no plans to reinstate Huang as the CEO.

Ross Mayfield of Baird noted that investors are probing other corners of the equity market instead of panic-selling. Chipmakers Intel and Micron both dropped over 7 per cent, while server maker Dell fell by 7 per cent. Super Micro Computer fell 6.9 per cent, and hyperscalers Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta slid between 2.4 and 4.1 per cent. CoreWeave dipped 6.1 per cent and Nebius dropped 7.6 per cent, affecting various firms in the technology sector. Many employees, investors, and business partners reportedly called for the return of the former chief executive officer.

The SOX index was up 106.6 per cent year-to-date in mid-June, but 2026 gains fell to 43 per cent. The Nasdaq reached an all-time closing high on October 6 before falling more than 10 per cent recently. San Francisco AI startup insiders hold a combined 1.2 trillion dollars in equity, according to a Bloomberg analysis. At the Anthropic IPO midpoint, the average employee's equity is valued at 72 million dollars in total value. Nvidia's worst week since April 2025 followed the scandal, with 900 billion dollars in value vanishing quickly.

Analysts expect Nvidia to report revenue of 109.10 billion dollars and a 90.4 per cent year-on-year earnings jump. Federal Open Market Committee minutes due Wednesday may offer clues before next month's interest rate decision by the Fed. Markets price a 95.7 per cent likelihood of a 25-basis-point rate hike in December, per CME FedWatch. Nvidia has hired Heidrick and Struggles to help find a new CEO to replace the departed Jensen Huang. The articles leave open whether President Donald Trump and Xi Jinping will reach agreements during their expected meeting.

stories.Headline: Palo Alto Networks agrees to buy Applied Compute in a $4.5 billion all-stock deal
stories.Summary:
Palo Alto Networks said in a Wednesday Nov. 18 press release that it plans to acquire Applied Compute, a platform for post-training and inference of open-weight models, in an all-stock transaction valued at $4.5 billion. The company announced the deal alongside its fiscal first quarter 2027 results. Palo Alto Networks is a global AI security firm. Applied Compute co-founder and CEO Yash Patil will become Palo Alto Networks' co-chief AI officer after the close of the transaction. Applied Compute's AI research team will join Palo Alto Networks.

The transaction is expected to close during Palo Alto Networks' fiscal third quarter of 2027, which runs from February to April, subject to regulatory clearance and other customary closing conditions. The deal will add Applied Compute's platform and AI research team to help enterprises adopt AI securely, whether they choose open-weight models, closed frontier models or both. Applied Compute will continue to serve AI-native companies, digital natives and large enterprises. Palo Alto Networks reported revenue of $3.44 billion versus $3.31 billion expected, up 39% from $2.47 billion a year ago. Adjusted earnings per share were $1.05 versus 97 cents expected.

Chairman and CEO Nikesh Arora said every enterprise is going to run a mix of open and closed models, and every one of those models needs to be secured. Arora said Applied Compute has built the best post-training and inference platform Palo Alto Networks has seen, and its research team is exceptional. Patil said Applied Compute was built with an exceptional team of AI researchers and engineers to make it easy for any company to train, serve and improve proprietary models. Patil said joining Palo Alto Networks will put security at the center of all its products and accelerate traction with the world's largest organizations. Arora said on the earnings call that if it works, the deal will dwarf the ability the company has in cybersecurity.

Arora said on the call that open-weight models had grown from under 5% of token traffic to more than 60% over the past year, without saying where the figure came from. JP Morgan analyst Brian Essex asked Arora about customer demand. Arora said deterministic security controls cannot anticipate every scenario an agent is going to conduct, and enterprises building AI applications will have to train a supervisory AI model at the same time. Sanchit Vir Gogia, chief analyst at Greyhound Research, said most failures in AI applications happen at runtime, through prompts, tools and permissions, whoever trained the model.

Applied Compute said in a Nov. 2 blog post that it was founded less than 18 months ago and has grown from zero to $100 million in annualized revenue run rate during that time. PYMNTS reported Tuesday Nov. 17 that Applied Compute is one of the training partners Nvidia relies on to help enterprises tailor open models with their own data, which feeds demand for Nvidia compute. The Information reported Nov. 4 that Palo Alto Networks had made four acquisitions this year and was in talks to acquire Clutch Security for around $500 million. The deal follows Palo Alto's $25 billion purchase of CyberArk, which added identity security to its platform. Palo Alto has sold model-agnostic protection through Prisma AIRS since 2025.

CFO Dipak Golechha said on the call that Palo Alto plans to build its own compute capacity, with spending mostly going to GPUs and servers and a smaller share for the facilities that house them. Golechha said Palo Alto will continue to source from its cloud partners and add dedicated capacity over time. Arora said the company aims for more than 100 megawatts of compute in the next three to five years. Palo Alto expects adjusted earnings per share of $4.26 to $4.30 and revenue of $14.52 billion to $14.57 billion for fiscal year 2027. Net income totaled $482 million, or 57 cents per share, up from $334 million, or 47 cents per share, a year ago.

stories.Headline: Trump administration considers requiring US firms to disclose use of Chinese AI models
stories.Summary:
The Trump administration is considering a plan to force American firms to disclose their use of Chinese AI models. This effort was reported by Reuters on November 18, 2026, citing three people familiar with the matter. The administration wants to discourage reliance on this technology without imposing new restrictions that could anger Beijing. Officials hope to reduce the use of Chinese AI through a name and shame campaign. This approach aligns with a broader anti-regulation stance on artificial intelligence within the current government.

The Treasury Department and the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy discussed the plan for companies like Airbnb. Airbnb uses the Qwen model from Alibaba to power its AI customer service agent for its users. Under this proposal, companies would be required to post their use of Chinese AI models on their websites. The plan targets open-weight models, which make core components available for anyone to download and adapt. These models include DeepSeek, Qwen, and Kimi, which was developed by the company known as Moonshot AI.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in July that the administration could sanction Chinese AI firms for intellectual property theft. He specifically mentioned the distillation process, where smaller models are trained using the output of larger American models. OSTP director Michael Kratsios said in April that China steals intellectual property from US labs on an industrial scale. The Chinese embassy in Washington stated that politicizing technology stifles global advances and they will safeguard Chinese businesses. The White House, the Treasury Department, and Alibaba did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Representative John Moolenaar of Michigan welcomed the report, calling disclosure an important step in managing potential risks. Representative Andrew Garbarino of New York joined Moolenaar in launching a congressional investigation into Chinese AI use in 2026. They sent letters to Airbnb, DoorDash, and Anysphere, the maker of the AI coding tool called Cursor. DoorDash uses Kimi for internal tasks, and Anysphere's Composer 2 model was built on a version of Kimi. SpaceX is also affected because it bought Anysphere, though the company did not respond to comment requests.

Chinese open-weight models are popular because they are cheaper than proprietary tools from US labs OpenAI and Anthropic. In October, Chinese models were the three most popular by token usage on the marketplace platform called OpenRouter. The US government itself used an Alibaba model on a website to search federal regulations despite FBI accusations. Concerns grew after reports of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang having an affair with an alleged spy for China. This situation highlighted unpunished cases where Nvidia AI chips were smuggled into China, increasing pressure on the administration.

The administration continues to weigh whether this disclosure requirement will be enshrined in a formal rulemaking process. It remains unclear if the idea is gaining traction among other officials within the Trump administration's leadership. The government is monitoring the spread of open-weight models compared to US versions like Meta's Muse Glimmer. Other American open-weight models mentioned include Nvidia's Nemotron and the Beam model created by the firm Reflection AI. The articles leave open whether the administration will eventually move toward more punitive actions against Chinese AI companies.

stories.Headline: Singapore launches three national AI missions to strengthen the finance sector
stories.Summary:
Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong announced three national artificial intelligence missions for the finance sector on 18 November. These missions aim to strengthen financial crime prevention, improve access to financing, and enable AI driven transactions. The government will bring together researchers, public agencies, technology companies, and financial institutions to develop solutions. This announcement took place during his keynote speech at the Singapore FinTech Festival. The initiatives seek to build shared capabilities and test solutions for wider deployment.

The first mission targets financial crime detection, while the second improves financing for startups and small and medium enterprises. The third mission enables AI agents to carry out financial transactions for businesses and individuals under defined safeguards. The Monetary Authority of Singapore will begin a design study in early 2027 for an industry wide scam detection system. A trial involving five banks is already underway to securely combine transaction data to identify suspicious patterns. The government will also test AI agents in controlled environments to verify identity, authorization, accountability, and system compatibility.

Gan Kim Yong stated that scams are not confined to one bank because stolen funds pass through several institutions within minutes. He noted that traditional lending approaches may not fully capture the creditworthiness of newer startups with limited assets or records. Gan emphasized that AI agents must operate within defined limits and that businesses remain accountable for transactions made on their behalf. He explained that connecting information across the financial system allows for earlier identification of suspicious activity and faster intervention. He added that AI will support faster and better informed lending decisions for smaller businesses.

Small and medium enterprises and startups with limited financial records are affected by the new financing access mission. AI technology companies are invited to develop solutions using realistic synthetic data, while public agencies and financial institutions contribute expertise. SMEs will be consulted to ensure these new AI solutions actually address their specific financing needs. The US Department of Commerce recently rolled out new rules requiring licenses to export advanced AI chips to five countries, including Singapore. These rules close a loophole that previously allowed China to access advanced chips remotely through third countries.

The articles state that 64 percent of financial institutions in Singapore already actively deploy AI across key business functions. This figure comes from research released in February by a company called Finastra. Singapore is widely recognized as a global leader in the adoption of artificial intelligence for the finance sector. The Future of Finance Institute will support the missions by coordinating partnerships and developing guidelines and standards. This institute will also test the new solutions for wider use across the entire financial sector.

The government will continue testing AI agents to see if they can make payments automatically once specified conditions are met. These tests include contractual payments made after agreed terms are verified or purchases completed on behalf of users. The Monetary Authority of Singapore will develop a blueprint for the scam detection utility, including its governance and operating model. The articles leave open whether the financial crime efforts will widen to involve collaboration with foreign counterparts. It remains to be seen how the new AI agents will handle accountability and responsibility in real world transactions.

stories.Headline: Visa expands its Agentic Ready program in Asia Pacific to scale AI agent payments
stories.Summary:
Visa announced the expansion of its Agentic Ready program across Asia Pacific on November 18, 2026, from its offices in Singapore. This second phase of the program focuses on acceptance by working with acquirers, payment gateways, payment service providers, and selected merchants. The initiative aims to prepare the regional commerce ecosystem for transactions that are initiated by artificial intelligence agents on behalf of consumers. Visa is leading this effort to scale trusted AI commerce by strengthening how the network handles these new types of digital payments. The company is collaborating with a diverse range of partners to ensure that agentic commerce can scale securely and reliably.

The program launches with over 50 participants, and Visa expects additional partners to join the initiative throughout the year of 2027. Acceptance partners include Adyen, Stripe, Airwallex, 2C2P by Antom, Allinpay Merchant Services, ALTEKGLOBAL by VNPAY, ASB Bank, AsiaPay, AXS, and Bank of China (Hong Kong). Other partners are CAKE DIGITAL BANK, Checkout.com, Cherri Tech, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Credit Saison Co., Ltd., Cuscal Limited, DBS Bank, and DCS. The list continues with dLocal, Eximbay, Fat Zebra, Fiserv, FOMO Pay, GMO Epsilon, Inc., GMO Payment Gateway, Inc., Hang Seng Bank, and ICBC (Asia). Further participants are Infcurion, Inc., Kasikorn Global Payment Co.,Ltd., KG Inicis, Maybank, Mitsubishi UFJ NICOS Co., Ltd., Mizuho Bank, Ltd., and National Australia Bank.

The list also includes NETS, Nuvei, OCBC, OEN Tech, Pine Labs, Rakuten Card Co., Ltd., Razorpay, and Retail Payment Solutions as a Coles Group company. Additional partners are SB Payment Service Corp., Sumitomo Mitsui Card Company, Limited, Toss Payments, UOB, UQPay, Windcave, Wpay, Xendit, YeahPay, and YeePay. T.R. Ramachandran, Head of Products and Solutions for Asia Pacific at Visa, stated that merchants need a clear way to strengthen readiness. He noted that agentic commerce will only scale if payment providers can support AI transactions while maintaining control over the customer experience. Ramachandran believes the program helps merchants prepare for this next chapter of commerce while maintaining the trust and security consumers expect.

Merchants are affected because they must determine how to recognize trusted agents and support them through checkout, payment, and post-purchase service. Visa is collaborating with Atlas Kitchen, CardInfoLink, Cleverbridge, Clink, Eats365 POS, FluxA, Juspay, [manif], Obenan, Pivota, Prava, and Reap Technologies Limited. They are also working with Set Sail AI, Shoplazza, and SHOPLINE to explore how agents discover products and build shopping carts in real-world experiences. These partners help explore the connection between AI agents and the checkout process to ensure a seamless experience for the end consumer. The goal is to provide the transparency and control that businesses and consumers already expect from modern digital payment systems.

The first phase of Visa Agentic Ready launched in April 2026 and focused on issuer readiness in a controlled, production-grade environment. Since that initial launch, over 100 issuers across 10 different markets in the Asia Pacific region have joined the readiness program. This effort builds on Visa Intelligent Commerce, which is a portfolio of initiatives designed to enable secure agentic commerce experiences at scale. Visa is utilizing its decades of experience in global technology, risk management, authentication, tokenisation, and network controls to support the ecosystem. The company operates in more than 200 countries and territories to facilitate transactions between consumers, sellers, financial institutions, and government entities.

Next, acceptance partners will work with Visa to assess existing systems, identify gaps, and test agent-initiated transactions in real-world environments. The Visa Acceptance Platform will support the payment lifecycle, including credential management, fraud protection, dispute resolution, and acceptance across various channels. Intelligence Commerce Connect will enable agentic commerce experiences across different networks, payment schemes, commerce platforms, and various AI agents. Organisations that are interested in joining the program or collaborating on agentic commerce are encouraged to contact their specific Visa representative. The articles leave open how many more partners will join in 2027 and the specific results of the real-world testing.

stories.Headline: VodafoneThree tests Nokia AI-RAN technology using Nvidia GPUs in the UK
stories.Summary:
VodafoneThree announced plans on November 18, 2026, to test Nokia's AI-RAN technology. The company will use Nvidia GPU-based hardware for these upcoming trials. These tests will occur in both lab and field environments in the UK. The trials are scheduled to take place during the next calendar year. This initiative aims to improve mobile network performance and overall efficiency.

The project uses Nokia AI-native anyRAN software running on the Nvidia Aerial RAN computer. It requires Red Hat OpenShift for the cloud management layer and Nvidia compute. Vodafone Group also opened an AI-RAN test center in Malaga, Spain, for broader studies. This Spanish facility evaluates Nokia, Nvidia GPUs, purpose-built ASICs, and Intel Granite Rapids x86 processors. Nokia aims to double spectral efficiency by the year 2028.

Valeria Baiamonte, director of network strategy and transformation at VodafoneThree, says AI-RAN is extremely important. She stated that AI is necessary to predict and reconfigure resources for prioritized customers. Baiamonte believes AI for RAN is the first monetization case for varied services. She explained that this technology supports a move toward assured and outcome-based connectivity. This framework will eventually allow the network to support physical AI services.

Gabriel Brown from Omdia says operators will get revenue uplifts from AI-enabled devices. He notes that the industry must prepare for vast numbers of AI endpoints. Affected devices include XR glasses, smartphones, cars, and Meta Charms connected to Muse AI. These new AI endpoints will have different connectivity profiles than current mobile devices. The AI-RAN technology is designed to serve this emerging demand for connectivity.

Vodafone mainly uses Ericsson and Huawei for RAN equipment across its European footprint. It has deployed Nokia in Albania and recently awarded a deal for 7,000 UK sites. Only ten of those UK sites were activated as of April this year. VodafoneThree is also working with Ericsson on AI-RAN using custom silicon and neural accelerators. These accelerators reportedly increase AI-inference capabilities tenfold in a new London radio rollout.

BT plans to trial the Nvidia platform in the EE network next year. First AI-RAN sites from Nokia and Nvidia are expected to deploy in Birmingham. Deutsche Telekom, Elisa, and Orange are also planning field trials with Nokia and Nvidia. T-Mobile recently completed the first voice call using this platform on a commercial network. Ronnie Vasishta expects commercial deployments of the Nokia and Nvidia platform to start next year.

stories.Headline: Atlassian finds AI code share rises to 70 per cent as review bottlenecks grow
stories.Summary:
The Atlassian AI SDLC Index found that artificial intelligence is rapidly driving down the financial cost of generating software code, according to findings from over 500 organisations via DX. Atlassian released the index, which analysed engineering intelligence data from more than 500 organizations via DX. AI-generated code comprised 49 per cent of total merged code in April 2026, rising sharply to 70 per cent by October 2026, the index noted. By October, AI spend per unit of output dropped by nearly 27 per cent, while code survivorship rebounded by 9 percentage points to reach 68 per cent. The surge in automated code has displaced operational pressure onto human pull request review workflows, which expanded at their fastest month-over-month rate in October.

Engineers continue to spend approximately 58 per cent of their time building new features, a distribution ratio that has remained static for almost two years. An evaluation of 14 workplace dimensions against metrics of speed, quality, and delivery ease revealed that thorough planning processes and robust documentation correlate most strongly with high code quality. Only about 62 per cent of surveyed organisations rate their planning and documentation favourably, indicating upstream disciplines remain underserved. Incident handling earned the highest ratings among engineering teams, indicating that organizations remain far more proficient at reactive response than proactive planning. For several months, engineering departments had to deal with rising costs to generate code while seeing a decline in AI-generated code that is retained in subsequent commits.

Molly Sands, Head of Atlassian's Teamwork Lab, stated that time saved through automation does not automatically result in heightened innovation without deliberate shifts in incentivised activities. Sands emphasizes that time saved through automation does not automatically result in heightened innovation. Without deliberate shifts in the activities that organizations incentivize and reward, engineers naturally reallocate saved time toward processing existing task backlogs rather than pursuing creative breakthroughs. This persistent allocation of time highlights how corporate structures dictate developer focus, according to Sands. Final code quality relies heavily on thorough planning processes and robust documentation, which correlate most strongly with high code quality, according to the report.

Atlassian recommends tracking code survivorship over raw volume, investing in comprehensive specification briefs, enforcing documentation, and establishing structured team experimentation. Tech executives are urged to track code survivorship rather than raw volume output, invest heavily in comprehensive specification briefs, strictly enforce documentation, and establish structured opportunities for team experimentation. The index lays bare the reality that writing code is just one piece of the broader software development life cycle, and that it burdens engineers with greater need to validate code and ensure its quality and security. While these improvements demonstrate that organizations are refining their deployment of AI tools, severe operational bottlenecks persist outside the immediate scope of code generation. Generative AI tools have failed to alter how developers allocate their working hours.

Sessions at NEDCamp 2026 focused on managing AI costs and maintaining control over AI features in Drupal development. Developers should treat cost and control as design inputs from day one. Local models in Chrome can be used in Drupal for drafting, reducing paid service token costs. AI Metering tracks token usage and enforces quotas, with options for local fallback to prevent blocking editors. Coding agents benefit fr

Atlassian plans to publish updates to the AI SDLC Index quarterly. Atlassian announced it will publish updates to the AI SDLC Index on a quarterly basis, establishing a recurring benchmark for software engineering adaptation. The index demonstrates that final code quality relies heavily on upstream factors within the development life cycle. To extract genuine value from AI investments, Atlassian outlines clear recommendations for enterprise leaders. The study also found weak upstream planning and documentation, rated favorably by only 62 percent of organizations, correlates with lower code quality.

stories.Headline: General Assembly finds 52% of L&D leaders say AI use erodes worker soft skills
stories.Summary:
General Assembly published research on 19 November 2026 showing that many Learning and Development leaders believe AI is weakening employees' human skills, IT Brief Australia reported. The study surveyed 510 HR and Learning and Development leaders at large companies across six countries. More than half of respondents, 52%, said AI use is degrading skills such as communication, conflict resolution and collaboration. Another 41% said ensuring employees retain or develop critical thinking, communication and other soft skills despite using AI will be one of their biggest challenges in the coming year. The findings highlight a tension inside large organisations as companies expand AI training while trying to preserve workplace skills that are harder to automate.

At the same time, 83% of respondents said human skills are becoming more valued within their organisations, and 59% expect demand for soft skills training to rise. Nearly two-thirds, 64%, said their teams are under pressure to deliver AI upskilling across the workforce, and AI literacy was most often ranked as the top skill Learning and Development teams themselves will need. One-third of respondents, 33%, said closing the AI skills gap is a leading challenge, while 31% pointed to change management and employee fatigue around AI. The research found that 57% of leaders expect demand for role-specific AI training to grow, while 56% expect their organisations to expand personalised learning journeys, 55% expect more hands-on training and 52% expect more job-based or role-based training. Out-of-the-box third-party training was the option most likely to be deprioritised, with 15% of organisations expecting to place less emphasis on it.

Daniele Grassi, Chief Executive Officer of General Assembly, said employers are trying to balance technical training with broader workplace development. He said Learning and Development professionals are tasked with building role-specific AI skills while making sure the human skills that matter most do not erode in the process. He said companies are increasingly looking to integrate AI and soft skills training to prepare employees for the future of work. He said training is becoming more hands-on, with opportunities to practice critical thinking, judgement and collaboration alongside AI usage and get feedback in real time. Among respondents who said their learning strategy is fully linked to documented business priorities, 23% expect a significant budget increase, compared with 11% of other respondents.

More broadly, 73% said company leadership regularly asks for Learning and Development input on workforce capability, transformation or future skills decisions, while 63% said Learning and Development leaders help shape business strategy. Connecting learning initiatives to business outcomes or return on investment was the second most-cited challenge for the coming year, named by 35% of respondents. Less than half, 47%, said business outcomes such as revenue growth or profit are among their top three measures of success, while 36% still count course completions among their leading metrics and 26% said distinguishing AI course completions from actual competency is a major challenge. Half of respondents in dedicated Learning and Development roles said course completions are a top metric, compared with 32% of those in broader HR roles who also oversee training. Grassi said businesses are investing in AI upskilling but the big challenge for Learning and Development leaders is proving that what they are doing is working, which means going beyond counting how many people took a course and measuring behaviour changes, skills and competencies instead and linking those to real business outcomes.

Gartner found that 27% of Australian employees fear artificial intelligence will make their skills obsolete, rising to 46.2% among Gen Z workers, based on a survey of 589 employees in Australia. The survey also found that 18.6% of employees are frustrated by how AI has changed their role, while 29.8% worry the technology will make errors that harm their work, and among Gen Z employees those figures rise to 30.8% and 42.3% respectively. Nearly half of Australian employees, 46%, are already expected to use AI in their jobs, and among those workers 90% said their organisation provides AI tools, but only 60.9% said they receive clear guidance on AI use, 54.6% reported formal learning opportunities and 56.9% cited manager support. Jonathan Tabah, Director Analyst at Gartner, said the biggest risk is not the new skills that need to be built but some of the old ones that will disappear, and that unmanaged AI-driven skills atrophy can reduce performance while increasing business risk, yet few organizations have a plan to address it. Gartner said human resources leaders should work with business leaders to identify which declining skills would create the greatest operational, regulatory or performance risks if lost, and that some skills must be retained because they remain essential when technology fails or cannot provide an answer.

At the Fortune 500 Innovation Summit on Tuesday, Mary Culler, president of Ford Philanthropy, said nothing is future-proof but a lot of the skilled trades are jobs that are going to be required to have a human there. She said auto technicians, who are in short supply, could increasingly use AI to help diagnose vehicle problems but still need a human to do the actual manual labor. Carhartt CEO Linda Hubbard said AI-powered efficiency will change how skilled trades workers do their jobs but the industry's labor needs, fueled by the data center boom and broader infrastructure investments, will continue to outpace any productivity gains from the technology. Hubbard said on stage in an interview with Fortune's Kristin Stoller that no matter how good the industry gets at encouraging people, it will always be challenged to get the number of people needed into the trades to rebuild the infrastructure of the country. Employers are expected to fill approximately 1.7 million skilled trades openings annually between now and 2034, but roughly a quarter of the industry's existing 18 million workers are over 55 and nearing retirement.

Maria Flynn, CEO of Jobs for the Future, said there is pushback on the cost of college and on what jobs really require college degrees, and that decades of trade policies and other economic shifts have left some communities with fewer skilled trades opportunities than they once had. Flynn said the industry is having to rebuild trust and awareness and help parents, young people and school counselors understand what the 124 different skilled trades occupations offer and what the paths are into those roles. While 95% of counselors agree trade school is a valuable and credible post-high school option, just 54% say they often recommend vocational or trade school, and only 28% often recommend an apprenticeship, according to a report released earlier this year by the Alliance for America's Skilled Trades. Culler said the perception needs to change and guidance counselors need to start talking about the opportunities. The Alliance's September report found that among every 100 who start an apprenticeship, just 48 complete the program, and only 29 enter a skilled trade occupation within five years of leaving it, while of every 100 entrants to related postsecondary programs, 48 complete their programs and just 34 go on to work in a skilled trade.

Flynn described the problem as pipeline leakiness, which can often come down to a lack of support for workers navigating training programs, including barriers like transportation and childcare, and she said the industry really needs to be working on this together. The General Assembly research found that 57% of leaders expect demand for role-specific AI training to grow, while 56% expect their organisations to expand personalised learning journeys, 55% expect more hands-on training and 52% expect more job-based or role-based training. Gartner said not every fading skill requires intervention, but some must be retained because they remain essential when technology fails or cannot provide an answer. The articles leave open which specific skills organisations will decide can be allowed to atrophy and which they will deliberately safeguard. The articles also leave open how employers will close the gap between the 90% of AI-using Australian workers whose organisations provide tools and the 60.9% who receive clear guidance on AI use.

stories.Headline: Anthropic's Claude Code team uses verification loops so Claude writes and reviews about 90% of its code
stories.Summary:
On the Claude Code team at Anthropic, about 90% of the code is written and reviewed by Claude, Addy Osmani wrote in a claude.dev blog post published Nov 16, 2026. Verification loops let the team delegate more work to Claude, Osmani wrote. Without them, you can really only run one or two Claudes at a time, he wrote. With them, you can run dozens or hundreds in parallel, he wrote. In internal testing around structured file generation, a separate grader checking Claude’s work against a rubric improved task success by up to 10 points over a standard prompting loop, with the largest gains on the hardest problems.

The article names three test types worth investing in, starting with end-to-end tests that describe real user flows like adding an item to a cart, checking out, and moving to a confirmation page. A unit test may show “Error: Timeout after 30 seconds,” but an end-to-end test can show a screenshot with a description of what’s broken, the article says. Property tests use libraries such as fast-check for JS/TS, Hypothesis for Python and proptest for Rust to generate thousands of inputs, the article says. Differential tests run the old system and the new system with the same inputs, using randomly generated inputs or a sample of production traffic, the article says. The team maintains a reliability checklist with 39 items, each with a trigger readable from a diff, a check, and the incidents or PRs behind it, and Claude checks only the items whose trigger matches, usually 3 to 10.

Code owners write their own checks and refine them until they flag what the owner would flag, the article says. If a check is still failing after three rounds, Claude stops and brings in a human, the article says. Code Review reads the REVIEW.md file from the base or default branch, never from the pull request’s changes, the article says. The team stamps each commit with how it was verified, including “none,” and a commit gate can block a commit if the session did not contain /code-review or /verify, with off, observe and enforce modes, the article says. If commits have been blocked twice in the session, the next one will be allowed through so Claude doesn’t get stuck, the article says.

Code Review tags findings as Important, Nit or Pre-existing, and the “pre-existing” tag means the reviewer shouldn’t hold the author responsible for something that was already a bug, the article says. The Code Review team recreates the repo to the state at the time of review for each example and provides a one-sentence answer key to what the bug was, the article says. In the Claude Code repo, patterns must occur in at least two PRs and be identifiable from a diff to be considered a potential rule, the article says. The article says Claude can test the whole app using the Claude Chrome extension for web changes, an iOS or Android MCP for mobile, computer use for desktop, or by running the service locally for backend work. A verify skill goes in a .claude/skills/ folder in your repo, as close to the relevant code as you can, and Claude knows to use it before committing changes, the article says.

MarkTechPost reported on Nov 18, 2026, that Anthropic added Code Mode to Claude Code, with Claude now chaining tool calls in JavaScript. The article says the team tunes recall up to the point where the next improvement would be overfitting to the eval rather than actually catching bugs. The article says three agents will try to do something, and the text ends there. The article says the team also runs cheap checks first, and on the team Claude runs the tests, build, and linter before opening a pull request. The article says this can be enforced with a hook that runs the tests when Claude finishes, or a /goal of a passing test suite.

The article says the team does not try to improve reviews by stacking on more reviewers, and that adding a second, more expensive, reviewer on top of the primary one is often a worse approach than tuning the primary. The article says review and verification rounds should build on each other, pointing each pass at context from earlier rounds and past failures rather than re-checking everything from scratch. The article says the team tracks how many merged changes were reverted, how many changes a maintainer rejected before merging, and a size-matched subset of changes that have stayed clean. The article says the Code Review team’s tuning set is split out from the fixed test set they use to evaluate their system, and they evaluated the recall rate for raw findings, post-verification, and final review separately. The article says a passing review on an out-of-date commit means nothing, and the team reserves reviews for commits.

stories.Headline: Nvidia stops shipping powerful AI chips to China
stories.Summary:
Nvidia Corp. announced it will stop shipping powerful AI chips to China on Tuesday, November 18, 2026. Interim CEO Colette Kress revealed this decision during an earnings call with analysts on November 17. The company will remove licensed Hopper-based data center products from its future guidance. This move follows the resignation of co-founder Jensen Huang on November 12, 2026. The board unanimously accepted his resignation as president, CEO, and director, effective immediately.

The company sold 2.4 billion dollars of licensed Hopper products to China in the third quarter. This follows US government licenses for H20 exports to Hong Kong, Macao, and mainland China in April 2025. Deliveries of H200 chips to China began in limited quantities in mid-July 2025. Nvidia previously sought permission to sell advanced Blackwell chips to China, but the Trump administration never acquiesced. The H200s are two generations behind the leading Rubin family of chips.

Interim CEO Colette Kress stated that future guidance excludes licensed Hopper data center products. She did not elaborate on why the shipments were ending during the earnings call. New chair Harvey Jones said the board recognizes that national security dynamics are changing the marketplace. Jones noted that the next CEO must navigate these waters very carefully. Nvidia also announced the formation of a board committee for national security and export controls.

The Trump administration increased scrutiny of processor exports to several countries on November 16. New rules limit sales when data center buyers provide Chinese companies remote access to AI servers. The People's Liberation Army is actively soliciting advanced chips to develop artificial intelligence military capabilities. Chinese companies like Huawei and Cambricon face a quality gap compared to Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices. The U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission reported these findings in its 2026 annual report.

Jensen Huang was ousted following reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. This woman worked for Singapore-based Megaspeed, which investigators eye for potential diversion of chips to China. Beijing denied that it attempted to spy on Huang, who expressed a desire to return as CEO. Fiscal third quarter revenue hit 115.8 billion dollars, while net income reached 65.3 billion dollars. Data-center revenue was 107.6 billion dollars, with supply-purchase commitments totaling 390 billion dollars.

The SEC is conducting a civil investigation into earlier disclosures, and Huang will appear before House panels December 1. An Nvidia lawyer is scheduled to testify on December 2 regarding these matters. The Commerce Department issued a rule to stop remote access to chips through third countries like Malaysia. This response followed criticism from Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and members of Congress. The articles leave open whether China can close chokepoints in logic fabrication, memory, and CUDA software.

stories.Headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns following national security concerns and boardroom crisis
stories.Summary:
Jensen Huang resigned as the founding CEO of Nvidia on November 13, 2026, following a boardroom crisis. His departure followed revelations of national security concerns and extramarital affairs involving a Chinese businesswoman. The board acted deliberately to protect the interests of shareholders, customers, partners, and employees. Interim CEO Colette Kress and Chairman Harvey Jones spoke with investors on November 18, 2026. Huang stated he would return as CEO if asked, but the board does not intend to reinstate him.

The board will consider internal and external candidates for the permanent CEO position based on national security capabilities. Nvidia established a committee to strengthen oversight of export control matters and engagement with United States government agencies. The company announced new supplier agreements with Spil, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, and Kinsus to address shortages of substrates and wafers. House Democrats elected Representative Ted Lieu of California as caucus chairman on Wednesday to coordinate priorities for January. Lieu and Republican Representative Nathaniel Moran of Texas introduced the AI Kill Switch Act to allow Department of Homeland Security shutdowns.

Chairman Harvey Jones said the board acted in the best interest of the company during this unexpected transition. Interim CEO Colette Kress noted that agentic AI is driving extraordinary demand for CPUs that far outstrips current supply. Kress stated that Nvidia compute remains fully utilized across every neocloud and hyperscaler the company currently serves. Representative Ted Lieu argued that failing to regulate artificial intelligence would be freaking insane for the federal government. He believes that developers of powerful AI systems must maintain mechanisms capable of slowing or stopping their operation.

Investor Gavin Baker warned that concentrating artificial intelligence within a few proprietary companies risks having only two or three value systems. He believes a vibrant open-source ecosystem is necessary so that companies can own their weights and their own destiny. The Media Research Center found that Apple News promoted 60 times more left-leaning stories than right-leaning ones over twelve months. This study found that 4,832 stories were from left-leaning outlets, while only 81 stories came from right-leaning sources. These findings affect the public who receive information from the Big Three News Apps including Google News and MSN.

Nvidia had been developing Nemotron models and partnerships with independent developers to reduce dependence on OpenAI and Anthropic. The company reports that weekly token volume on OpenRouter increased 35-fold year-over-year, with agentic workloads accounting for 80 percent. Token prices have fallen nearly 60 percent since May, but B300 rental rates have increased by over 60 percent. Hopper GPUs have been recontracted at up to twice their original prices under various multiyear agreements. A 2015 study by Robert Epstein and Ronald Robertson suggested biased search rankings can shift undecided voter preferences by 20 percent.

Nvidia expects its CPU revenue to more than double in fiscal 2028 as demand for Vera CPUs grows. The company projects that the adoption of agentic AI will sustain infrastructure demand beyond the 2027 calendar year. CoreWeave, Meta, Nscale, and OpenAI are adopting the Vera CPU to meet the needs of agentic workloads. The articles leave open whether the board will eventually hire an external candidate or an internal one for CEO. They also leave open if the AI Kill Switch Act will pass or if AI will remain democratized.

stories.Headline: IREN, CoreWeave and Nebius fall 63% to 79% from 2025 highs despite surging revenue
stories.Summary:
IREN, CoreWeave and Nebius have fallen 63% to 79% from their 2025 highs even as revenue and contracted backlogs surge, BigGo Finance reported on Nov. 18, 2026. Through Tuesday's close, IREN traded at $15.81, down 79% from its 2025 high of $76.41, while CoreWeave sat 74% below its peak and Nebius Group was 63% under its June high. The selloff accelerated since early October, when the Nasdaq set its latest record, with CoreWeave shares falling 45% since then and Nebius 57%, according to Reuters. The Motley Fool reported the same day that the neocloud industry had gotten bad headlines, with secondary effects harming CoreWeave and Nebius. Foreign Policy Journal reported on Nov. 16, 2026, that Democrats securing control of both chambers of Congress in November's midterm elections amplified investor anxiety over AI regulation, power consumption rules and restrictions on data center construction.

IREN's revenue rose 66% sequentially to $228 million in the September quarter, with AI cloud revenue nearly tripling to $200 million, and its contracted revenue backlog grew 22% to $20.3 billion, roughly two-thirds with investment-grade counterparties including Microsoft and Nvidia. CoreWeave's quarterly revenue jumped to $3.66 billion from $1.37 billion a year earlier, the company lifted its full-year outlook, and its backlog stands at about $132.5 billion. Nebius told investors customer prepayments on new contracts now cover more than 100% of the cost of bringing that capacity online, up from 50% to 60% in the second quarter. IREN had targeted more than $4 billion in annualized revenue by the end of 2026 but now expects that level in January or possibly as late as February, after a customer requested a design change and suppliers ran late. CoreWeave booked $207 million in operating income last quarter but paid $846 million in net interest expense, up from $310 million a year earlier, producing a net loss of $709 million.

Nvidia has been both shareholder and financier to the neoclouds, through a $6.3 billion order to buy unsold CoreWeave capacity through April 2032 and a $2 billion investment in Nebius announced in March for an 8.3% stake. With Jensen Huang out as chief executive and former finance chief Colette Kress in the interim role, bond investors are questioning whether that support continues in the same form. Loren Moran, a fixed income portfolio manager at Wellington Management, said it is fair to say anyone who takes over will have a lower risk threshold than Jensen when it comes to Nvidia's balance sheet, and there may be a lot less credit availability toward weaker players. Tony Trzcinka, an investment-grade portfolio manager at Impax Asset Management, said existing contracts should survive the transition and it is all about whether Jensen's successor would want to be as adventurous in going into all these different arrangements. Miriam Wheeler, Goldman Sachs' global head of leveraged finance, said in the bank's "Top of Mind" note that the market had expected roughly $60 billion of AI-related high-yield issuance this fall, but supply has dried up since late September, with no new deals in the past month.

CoreWeave bonds issued in June at a 9.625% yield now yield close to 15%, and Nebius convertible notes sold in August at 4.5% traded at 70 cents on the dollar last Friday, pushing their yield above 12%. JPMorgan cut its IREN target to $55 from $65 on Nov. 9 while keeping an overweight rating, citing rising contract prices, and Jones upgraded IREN to buy on Nov. 6 with a $40 target. Goldman Sachs lowered its CoreWeave target to $101 from $106 and maintained a buy, and Citi named the company among its top software picks, pointing to signs of strong AI demand and nicer valuations. The consensus IREN price target of $56.50 across 11 analysts, eight of them at buy, implies roughly 257% upside from current levels. TeraWulf Inc. carries the highest short interest among the group at 24.34% of outstanding shares as of October 30, even though the stock remains fractionally positive for the year at 5.20%, and the company has shed nearly 40% of its value over the past six months.

The neocloud business is fairly new and was brought about by massive investments in AI infrastructure, as the biggest AI hyperscalers could not get enough computing capacity online fast enough, so other companies built their own AI data centers and rent them out. The Motley Fool reported that these upstarts do not generate ample cash flows to build data centers like other major cloud computing providers and must seek outside funding through issuing debt and selling shares. Nvidia became a major shareholder of both CoreWeave and Nebius as a result of seeing them as two of the best operators in this space. CoreWeave recently saw some of its debt get priced at distressed levels, which means there is a low likelihood of it repaying its commitments. The Global X Data Center & Digital Infrastructure ETF lost nearly 4% in a single session and extended its six-month decline to more than 18%, while the NASDAQ 100 recorded its steepest one-day drop in 19 months, falling nearly 6% and trimming its year-to-date advance to just 5% after surging to a record peak of 30,800 on AI enthusiasm.

IREN still expects about $15 billion in capital spending for the remainder of its fiscal year, and $6 billion of that has not yet been arranged, while Nebius plans to spend $40 billion to $45 billion next year. Nebius also pushed back its targets, with management saying the revisions were just about timing, not demand, and its stock fell 17% on the day it reported. CoreWeave trades at a forward price-to-sales ratio of about 1, Nebius around 3, and IREN at nearly six times estimated fiscal 2027 revenue on an enterprise-value basis, against 13.4 for Nebius and 6.9 for CoreWeave by that measure. Danny Zaid, a portfolio manager at TwentyFour Asset Management, said the uncertainty for the overall space means greater risk premiums expected by investors and expected dispersion to increase as investors evaluate credits on a case-by-case basis. BigGo Finance said the practical signal to watch is debt and deadlines rather than revenue growth, and that if IREN reaches its $4 billion run-rate target by February and CoreWeave keeps raising capital on acceptable terms, current prices may look cheap, while if delays keep accumulating the repricing may not be over.

stories.Headline: Nexus Legal Group launches two AI WebTracker plans for law firms
stories.Summary:
The Nexus Legal Group LLC announced simplified plans for AI WebTracker, its AI-powered prospect intelligence platform for law firms, on November 16, 2026, from Allentown, Pennsylvania. The platform identifies people actively researching legal help in a firm's practice areas and markets, including people visiting competing law firm websites. It delivers them in a fresh feed every morning. The platform is now offered in two plans, Self-Serve and Done-For-You. Every plan includes lead scrubbing before a firm's team reaches out.

Each lead in the feed shows who the person is, why they entered the feed, which competing firms they viewed, and where and when they were active, down to the ZIP code. Firms export these audiences directly to their ad platforms and CRM. Every account stays the firm's own, and the ad budget is paid from the firm's own ad account, never handled by Nexus. AI WebTracker is a flat monthly subscription never tied to leads, cases or outcomes, with no setup fee and cancellation on 30 days' notice. The Done-For-You plan adds the Nexus Lead Validation and Database Scrubbing upgrade, which runs Scammer Scrub, TCPA Lookup and Scrubbing, and DNC Lookup and Scrubbing on a firm's monthly leads and uploaded lists.

Rob Parker, Managing Partner of The Nexus Legal Group, said firms are being squeezed from both sides, paying more every year to bid on the same keywords as every competitor in town. He said firms pay lead vendors for names that too often turn out to be wrong numbers, recycled lists or people who already hired someone. He said AI WebTracker lets a firm see who is actually researching its type of case, in its own markets, before that person picks up the phone. He said a firm should not pay more because a vendor sent more names. He said with a flat subscription the feed grows the firm's own audience every day, and the firm keeps what it builds.

Every AI WebTracker plan includes TCPA Real-Time Scrubbing, Do Not Call Lookup, Phone List Scrubbing and the Name Recognition Algorithm, also called Scrub By Name, so risky records are flagged before an intake team makes contact. Each record is marked Validated, Review or Do Not Contact, with a time-stamped Validation Record. The Done-For-You plan includes audiences and Nexus-designed, firm-approved ad creatives uploaded to ad platforms the firm already owns, such as Google, Microsoft Bing and Meta, plus ongoing feed tuning, a monthly report, a review call and a dedicated Nexus contact. An optional Nonprofit Outreach and Intake Support add-on is available with either plan and provided with Legal Support Cases, Inc. under a separate agreement. AI WebTracker is designed for personal injury, mass tort, trucking and commercial vehicle, wrongful death and other practice areas where speed and geography decide which firm signs the case.

The company said AI WebTracker uses licensed data sources, and being identified in the feed is not consent to be contacted. It said scrubbing and Lead Validation reduce risk but do not guarantee compliance and are not legal advice. AI WebTracker and Scammer Scrub are trademarks of their respective owners. Law firms can book a demo and receive pricing at WebTrackerLeads.ai. The Nexus Legal Group describes itself as a legal marketing and technology company that helps law firms find, reach and sign high-value cases.

Harvey and Legora each launched a product called Intake about a day apart in October 2026, both built to help corporate legal departments receive, sort and route incoming legal requests with AI. Wordsmith had already released its own Intake earlier in the year. Kenny Gary, CEO of the communications firm LIMELIGHT, documented that overlap in a three-part series for JD Supra Perspectives. Goodwin unveiled Regina OS, its proprietary AI operating system, on August 14, and days later Davis Wright Tremaine announced a firmwide expansion of Harvey and Microsoft AI tools. Jason Brown, president and CEO of the Association of Corporate Counsel, said on Infodash's Legal Innovation Spotlight podcast that over 85% of surveyed ACC members report they have embedded AI in their legal departments and actively use it, a share that rose sharply over roughly two years.

Brown said the overwhelming majority of members tell ACC they are not seeing efficiency or cost gains from their law firms, and he expects that gap to push more work in-house if it persists. Lynn Tellefsen Stehle, writing November 11 in JD Supra Perspectives, puts change management inside the firm as a permanent skill with its own people and accountability rather than a one-time rollout. Brie Leung, founder and principal of Red Bird Strategy, argues that AI makes lawyers reconsider where their judgment matters and what expertise means. Catherine Alman MacDonagh, CEO and founder of the Legal Lean Sigma Institute, proposes a written project charter defining the problem, the goal, who is responsible, the resources needed and how success will be measured. Jen Leonard, founder of Creative Lawyers, calls the gap between announcement and action innovation by press release.
