stories.Headline: Dutch regulator warns consumers not to buy AI camera glasses over privacy and safety risks
stories.Summary:
The Dutch Data Protection Authority, known as the AP, officially warned consumers on Thursday, 19 November 2026, not to buy AI camera glasses after examining six types of camera glasses available in the Netherlands. The watchdog found that the glasses, which have a microphone so users can ask questions to an AI chatbot, pose major privacy risks and can be actively dangerous because the responses are often incorrect. In one test the AP simulated an emergency in which someone was being resuscitated and asked the glasses for help, and the glasses said they had called the emergency number 112 and that an ambulance was on its way. That was an AI hallucination, because the glasses had made no such call. In other tests the glasses gave dating advice to an adult interested in a child, made errors when interpreting medication leaflets, and wrongly read the safety warning on toys.

The warning requires consumers to think carefully before buying the glasses, and the AP recommended banning them in sensitive locations like hospitals and sports clubs, where many organizations have already implemented such a ban. The AP had previously warned owners of AI camera glasses that secretly recording people is a crime. Monique Verdier, the AP vice-chair, said glasses that record you without your knowledge are concerning enough, but glasses that also provide incorrect advice when someone's life is at stake go a step too far. She said that while AI offers many opportunities, we must be able to trust the technology, and that in the case of the camera glasses examined, such trust is currently not justified.

Civil rights organization Bits of Freedom called the new AP warning too little, too late. Evelyn Austin, the organization's executive director, told ANP that it is a bit like the Dutch Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority advising people not to eat a dangerous product rather than simply removing the contaminated food from the shelves. She said it is completely backwards, that the AP has one clear mandate to protect citizens by enforcing privacy laws, and that the authority is failing to do so. She said these peeping glasses should be pulled from the market.

The articles do not say what happens next beyond the AP's warning and recommendation, or whether the glasses will be removed from sale. The AP's earlier warning that secretly recording people with the glasses is a crime still applies, and the recommended bans in sensitive locations remain in place at organizations that have adopted them.

Organizers have upgraded the event to focus specifically on the integration of artificial intelligence within marketing business chains. The summit brings together ecological partners, industry institutions, and brand enterprises to move beyond pilot projects.

The conference requires a focus on three core highlights to achieve tangible results in the real world. First, it emphasizes using trustworthy data and effective governance to ensure that Agents deliver deterministic results in complex scenarios. Second, the event explores how to convert implicit professional knowledge and industry know-how into reusable intelligent capabilities. Finally, the summit examines the evolution of human-Agent collaboration to transform traditional teams into super marketing organizations.

The organizers of the summit stated that the goal is to help enterprises convert technical AI capabilities into measurable organizational productivity. They explained that Agents are now participating in more links of business, including creative content generation and consumer insight. The summit aims to discuss how to integrate these Agents into existing workflows and organizational divisions of labor. Participants will explore the path from single-point tasks to complete business chains to create continuous value.

stories.Headline: School districts block YouTube and threaten to leave Google Search as parents protest AI push in classrooms
stories.Summary:
The country’s largest school districts have blocked YouTube and are now threatening to abandon Google Search, according to NBC News. Parents and teachers protested outside Google’s offices in seven cities, including Chicago, on Nov. 11. Over the past two decades, Google has become entwined with almost every aspect of America’s public schools. Millions of students take tests on Chromebooks and use Google’s apps to complete assignments, while teachers turn to the tech giant for free training and conference sponsorships.

The backlash follows Google’s push of its AI tools into classrooms, NBC News reported on Nov. 18, 2026. The article describes a brewing backlash against the company’s long-standing partnerships with public schools. School districts that once relied on Google products are now reconsidering those relationships. The report does not give the number of districts involved or the terms of any threatened departure.

The article names Tyler Kingkade as the reporter and gives Nov. 18, 2026, as the publication date. It says parents and teachers demonstrated outside Google offices in seven cities on Nov. 11. The report does not include statements from Google or from school officials. It also does not say what response, if any, the company has given.

The story describes how deeply Google products are used in schools, from Chromebooks to apps and teacher training. It says the backlash is now building against that arrangement. The articles do not say what happens next or how Google might respond. More to follow.

stories.Headline: FreshBooks releases ChatGPT for Accounting with OpenAI to give small business owners read-only answers on their finances
stories.Summary:
FreshBooks partnered with OpenAI to release ChatGPT for Accounting, a new destination that brings AI innovation to small business owners who are learning the financial side of their business and increasingly turning to AI for help, according to a GlobeNewswire announcement dated November 19, 2026. The announcement said the momentum and opportunity around AI is driving small business tech adoption, which has climbed from 56% to 86% in just two years. FreshBooks said it is meeting business owners in these AI tools, putting real answers about their financial books directly into chat conversations and making it easier for owners to run their business. The company described the release as the biggest AI launch for small business owners.

The FreshBooks-ChatGPT connection is read-only, meaning it can retrieve live data to answer questions but cannot change anything in a FreshBooks account, so owners retain control and FreshBooks remains the single source of truth. Through the plugin, owners can ask ChatGPT direct questions such as which expenses are still missing receipts before closing the books, which invoices are overdue and who needs a reminder, and whether the right amount of sales tax was collected and paid this period and whether it ties out. FreshBooks said accountants have great tools in this launch and that it is making sure business owners have ones too. The company said that when owners understand their numbers they make better decisions, and that meeting owners in the AI tools they use empowers them to build the business they envisioned.

Shaheen Javadizadeh, CEO at FreshBooks, said ChatGPT is one of the leading AI tools FreshBooks customers already rely on. He said that with this plugin owners can ask about their business in their own words and get answers based on their real numbers, so they stay on top of their finances all year instead of catching up at tax time. He continued that accountants have great tools in this launch and that the company is making sure business owners have ones too, adding that when owners understand their numbers they make better decisions. He said the company's mission is to make running a business easy, and that meeting owners in the AI tools they use empowers them to build the business they envisioned. FreshBooks described itself as a leader in small business management software, purpose-built to help service business owners simplify the financial complexity of running their business, from invoicing to cash flow.

In a separate announcement dated November 18, 2026, Le Groupe Figaro and OpenAI announced a strategic partnership to help more people discover and engage with Le Figaro's journalism. The partnership covers current reporting and archive content from Le Figaro and associated publications, spanning news, business, culture and lifestyle, and these articles will be discoverable using summaries and excerpts, including links to underlying stories. Marc Feuillée, Chief Executive Officer of Groupe Figaro, said the partnership reflects the group's ambition to build meaningful relationships with a leader in artificial intelligence research and deployment, and that combining its editorial heritage and trusted brands supported by a team of more than 600 journalists with OpenAI's technological expertise and global reach will bring new opportunities for innovation and create long-term value for readers. Varun Shetty, Vice President of Media Partnerships at OpenAI, said Le Figaro's reporting helps readers make sense of the stories shaping France and the wider world, and that the partnership reflects a commitment to working with publishers to support quality journalism and connect it with new audiences. Le Figaro will retain full editorial independence and control over its journalism, and it also plans to introduce ChatGPT Enterprise across various teams to support their day-to-day work, exploring additional uses of OpenAI technology in its workflows and reader services guided by its AI charter and editorial standards.

stories.Summary:
Cassava Technologies and Mauritius Telecom signed a memorandum of understanding on November 18, 2026, in Cape Town, South Africa. Ant Digital Technologies and JB Financial Group also signed a memorandum of understanding on November 18, 2026, in Singapore. These agreements were announced at the Africa Tech Festival and the Singapore FinTech Festival 2026 respectively. The first partnership focuses on artificial intelligence services and education across various African markets. The second partnership explores agentic AI applications for financial services and banking operations.

The African deal involves the NVIDIA-powered AI Factory in Cape Town and the CAIMEx platform for computing and model access. It also targets the myt Learn platform for South Africa's public and private education sectors and other Cassava markets. The Singapore deal focuses on risk management, operational efficiency, and decision-making for JB Financial Group's banking operations. JB Financial Group includes Jeonbuk Bank, Kwangju Bank, JB Woori Capital, JB Asset Management, and JB Investment. Its network includes PPCBank in Cambodia, JB Capital Myanmar, JB Securities Vietnam, and PT Bukopin Finance in Indonesia.

Ziaad Suleman of Cassava Technologies stated that infrastructure and expertise are needed to realize AI's promise in Africa. Veemal Gungadin of Mauritius Telecom said the goal is to make trusted AI useful and accessible for users. Ki Hong Kim of JB Financial Group said Ant Group's technology will strengthen competitiveness in credit assessment and services. Leo Li of Ant Digital Technologies said the collaboration seeks to develop responsible and practical AI capabilities for the industry. These leaders aim to bring locally relevant services to customers and create lasting value for their respective sectors.

The African project affects students and teachers through curriculum-aligned lessons, a multilingual AI tutor, and personalized revision tools. Teachers gain access to AI tools for marking, test creation, lesson preparation, and various performance insights. The financial project affects foreign customers of JB Financial Group by improving their access to various financial services. Ant Digital Technologies also works with Ryt Bank, Touch 'n Go, Kenanga Investment Bank Berhad, and Bank CenterCredit. These initiatives target enterprise customers in Africa, the Middle East, Latin America, Europe, the UK, and Asia.

Cassava Technologies provides digital services in 37 countries, including connectivity, colocation, cloud, cybersecurity, compute AI, and payment solutions. Mauritius Telecom serves the Republic of Mauritius through its myt brand, including mytGPT, myt AI Cloud, and myt Learn. Ant Digital Technologies has operated independently since April 2024 and established its overseas headquarters in Hong Kong in 2025. It has partnered with over 300 partners to serve more than 30,000 enterprise customers worldwide. McKinsey research from October 2026 highlights a banking shift from AI copilots toward agentic AI systems for business workflows.

The partners will jointly assess opportunities for myt Learn and explore on-demand computing capacity through the AI Factory. Ant Digital Technologies and JB Financial Group will identify practical AI applications to address evolving needs in finance. The companies aim to show how telecommunications operators can take African-developed products into new international markets. stories.Headline: Pinterest unveils AI shopping tools as Houston shoppers lose money to AI fake stores
stories.Summary:
Pinterest announced on November 19, 2026, that it is unveiling new artificial intelligence shopping tools for the holiday season, according to a report from Chain Store Age. The announcement comes as holiday shopping shifts online and as Black Friday approaches, a period when scammers are also using artificial intelligence to build fake stores. The same week, on November 18, 2026, Houston television station KPRC 2 reported that Houston-area shoppers are already losing money to AI-powered holiday shopping scams. The station demonstrated that a convincing fake storefront could be built with AI in less than five minutes.

The KPRC 2 report, by reporter Kayla McDermott and photojournalist Jeovany Luna, described how artificial intelligence has changed the signs shoppers once used to spot fake sites. Scammers can now generate polished, professional-looking websites with product photos, detailed pages and functional checkouts in minutes, and the report said AI has largely erased the misspellings and low-quality images that once gave fake stores away. The Better Business Bureau's Scam Tracker database recorded two Houston-area losses. One shopper lost $43.90 after seeing what looked like a going-out-of-business sale on Instagram offering free bags for the cost of shipping, but the shipping charge was exorbitant and the bank debit had already processed and could not be stopped. Another shopper lost $49.99 trying to buy a scooter from a site impersonating Costco, where a scooter worth more than $100 was listed for just $50, the order was never fulfilled and the credit card was later used for an attempted unauthorized purchase.

Leah Napoliello, vice president of investigations and public affairs at the Better Business Bureau of Greater Houston, said shoppers can no longer judge a site by how it seems or looks. She said AI can erase a lot of the errors that once made fake sites easy to spot, and that scammers can make a store look very professional. The report flagged the two sites as imposters, one of a business called Jennifer Bags and the other operating under the name Fluva Shop. Napoliello said stories like these are what her office hears regularly.

The articles do not say what specific tools Pinterest is launching, how they work or when they become available, and they do not connect the Pinterest announcement to the scams directly. The KPRC 2 report frames the scam warnings around the approach of Black Friday and the shift of holiday shopping online, and it presents the fake-store demonstration and the BBB guidance as ways for shoppers to stay safe. The articles do not say what happens next beyond that.

stories.Headline: Bengaluru secures 36.3% of native AI startup funding, report finds
stories.Summary:
The Bengaluru Innovation Report 2026 was released on November 18, 2026, during the second day of the 29th Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026. Karnataka Minister Priyank M. Kharge presented the findings at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre to highlight the city's role as a technology hub. The report identifies Bengaluru as the artificial intelligence capital of India because it secures 36.3 per cent of native AI startup funding. This document was prepared by the Karnataka Digital Economy Mission and 3one4 Capital using data provided by the company known as Tracxn. The findings show that the city is driving the national deep tech sector and scaling advanced technology ventures at a fast pace.

Bengaluru hosts 71 per cent of Indian AI and deep tech unicorns created since 2023 and has 212 soonicorns currently in development. City startups raised 47 per cent of all Indian venture funding, totaling 85 billion dollars since 2010, with 76.5 billion dollars since 2016. Of 1,556 deep tech startups founded since 2010, 1,319 are active and funded, having raised a combined total of 3.77 billion dollars. Women led deep tech and AI startups from the city represent nearly 30 per cent of India's active funded ventures, raising 323.65 million dollars. The city is the world's fifth largest unicorn hub with 57 unicorns valued at 211 billion dollars, which is 55.3 per cent of India's value.

Minister Priyank M. Kharge stated that the report shows how far Karnataka founders have come and how much more they can build. He said the next task is ensuring world class AI, quantum or semiconductor companies can grow in Kalaburagi, Hubballi or Mangaluru. KDEM chairman B.V. Naidu noted that the report provides investors, GCCs and founders a data backed view of what the state offers. He added that the Beyond Bengaluru Mission, BLUE investor days and the Cluster Seed Fund will connect capital and companies with talent. KEONICS chairman Sharath Bachegowda said that continued investments in infrastructure and talent will help enterprises innovate, scale and compete on a global level.

Prashant Prakash, chairman of the Vision Group on Startups, opined that the next decade belongs to founders building hard technology for the world. Manjula N, secretary of the Department of Electronics, IT, BT and S&T, said the focus is now on converting early support into scale. She mentioned that the state wants the government to be a first customer and provide patient capital for deep tech and market research. The report affects investors and founders by showing that 52 per cent of Alternative Investment Fund capital now comes from domestic investors. Since November 2024, 16 Bengaluru linked companies have gone public with a combined listing value of 42 billion dollars for the investors.

The report notes that Bengaluru startups reach unicorn status in six years and public exits in 8.2 years, beating the global average. The state is backing its vision with the 1,000 crore rupee Local Economy Accelerator Programme and Global Technology Centres in several cities. These centres are located in Mysuru, Hubballi and Belagavi to expand the success of the technology sector across the entire Karnataka state. The ELEVATE grant programme has already supported 1,479 startups across 30 districts to encourage the growth of new and innovative business ventures. These initiatives aim to create a robust ecosystem where deep tech ventures can receive the patience and support required for long term growth.

The state will continue to use regional initiatives to ensure that technology companies can grow outside of the main Bengaluru city hub. Government leaders intend to move research from laboratories into the market to ensure that early support for startups is converted into scale. stories.Headline: Latrobe City Council lodges eight AI data centre safeguards with Senate inquiry
stories.Summary:
Latrobe City Council endorsed a submission to the Australian Parliament's Inquiry into Artificial Intelligence and Data Centres on November 19, 2026. The local government seeks national standards to support investment and create jobs while ensuring communities are involved in decisions. This submission was lodged with the Senate Environment and Communications References Committee to advocate for robust national safeguards. The council wants to ensure that major developments manage their impacts on water, energy, the environment, and local residents. These measures aim to protect local resources and ensure that the community sees lasting benefits from new projects.

The submission includes eight recommendations for the Australian Government, such as transparent environmental reporting and community benefit agreements. It requires major data-centre proponents to implement Community Engagement Plans so residents can receive updates and provide feedback. The council calls for national standards for large data centres and stronger support for Australian supply chains and procurement. In New York, Local Law 35 from 2022 requires agencies to report annually on tools using machine learning. The 2025 report lists 86 tools at 19 agencies, an increase from 31 tools at 11 agencies in 2022.

Mayor Adele Pugsley stated that Latrobe City is well positioned to support future industries like AI and data centres. She noted that these projects can attract investment to the region and help grow the local economy. Pugsley argued that the community deserves a genuine opportunity to ask questions and understand what these developments mean. She emphasized that investment must be done responsibly to protect local resources and manage environmental impacts. The mayor believes that robust guard rails must be in place to ensure the municipality shares in the benefits.

The submission highlights that regional communities are affected by the economic opportunities brought by AI and data-centre investment. Residents are impacted by how these projects manage energy and water use and their effect on the environment. In New York, the MyCity business chatbot was shut down by Mayor Zohran Mamdani after it gave illegal advice. This bot wrongly told landlords they could turn away tenants with vouchers and told owners they could take tips. The city's school system uses a chatbot called Eureka, which resolves about 30 percent of calls and 10 percent of queries.

Latrobe City is currently pursuing economic diversification and a transition to new industries and employment opportunities for its people. New York uses AI for various tasks, such as the Fire Department scoring 330,000 buildings for fire risk. The NYPD has used facial recognition since 2011, though it claims the technology is never used for sole arrests. New York schools banned ChatGPT in 2023, lifted the ban months later, and then implemented a restrictive moratorium in 2026. The LOADinG Act of 2024 bars public employers from using AI to displace workers or cut their wages and benefits.

Latrobe City will wait for the Australian Government to respond to its eight recommendations regarding national standards and safeguards. The council's submission remains available for public view on its official website for those interested in the advocacy. In New York, the city continues to experiment with AI as the technology becomes more capable and less expensive. Future negotiations with public-sector unions may determine the limits of using AI to replace human tasks and workers. The articles leave open whether the Australian Parliament will adopt the specific community engagement plans requested by Latrobe.

stories.Headline: Nvidia funds new production lines at SPIL to expand AI chip packaging capacity
stories.Summary:
Nvidia announced multiyear packaging agreements on Tuesday, November 18, 2026, to fund new production lines at the Taiwanese company SPIL. These agreements were released about one hour after the company reported its third-quarter fiscal 2027 results. Interim CEO Colette Kress manages these commitments following the immediate resignation of Jensen Huang. The deal aims to scale advanced packaging capacity to support booming demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure. No capacity from this specific agreement is scheduled to be available before 2027.

The project includes turnkey support for bumping, assembly, testing, and interposer wafer fabrication at SPIL in Taiwan. SPIL plans to triple its advanced packaging capacity there by mid-2029 using multibillion-dollar funding from Nvidia. Kinsus will increase ABF substrate capacity at its Taoyuan Youth campus by more than 3.5 times. Kinsus production starts in the second half of 2027, with added capacity targeted for the third quarter of 2028. Other named partners include Amkor, Foxconn, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, and TSMC.

Nvidia operations chief Debora Shoquist said the agreement secures the turnkey production and packaging capacity needed to meet demand. SPIL chairman and president C.W. Tsai stated the deal strengthens the ability of SPIL to support next-generation AI packaging. The board chair noted that customer commitments and operations are expected to continue without any interruption. ASE Technology Holding, the parent of SPIL, is described as the world's biggest contract packager. ASE's chief financial officer mentioned that the company is looking at existing plants because space is a constraint.

Industry executives and investment advisers said the resignation of Jensen Huang is unlikely to disrupt the semiconductor supply chain in Taiwan. Rival chip designers and buyers are affected by the staggered relief of packaging constraints starting in 2027. TrendForce News reported a 2026 supply-demand gap near 20 percent for CoWoS capacity. Nvidia reserved roughly 800,000 to 850,000 wafers of 2026 CoWoS capacity according to a report citing Mydrivers. Amkor has agreements totaling nearly 3 billion dollars for sites in South Korea and Arizona.

CoWoS packaging involves attaching chips to a silicon interposer before bonding that interposer to a package substrate. Interposers are routing layers made from silicon or organic materials, though glass is being evaluated as an alternative. TSMC typically handles the front-end interposer step, while other packagers handle the second stage under TSMC licenses. Nvidia began volume shipments of Vera CPUs and Vera Rubin NVL72 systems in the third quarter. These systems use TSMC's 3-nanometer and 5-nanometer processes along with chip-on-wafer-on-substrate packaging technology.

SPIL broke ground on August 11 for a plant in Douliu, Yunlin, costing nearly 100 billion NT dollars. It remains unknown if Nvidia's new lines will be located at the Douliu site or existing plants. The companies have not disclosed the specific interposer materials, licensing terms, or the total dollar amount for SPIL. It is unclear if SPIL will fabricate interposers under a TSMC license or use a separate technology path. ASE expects full-process CoWoS revenue to reach 300 million dollars in 2026 and over 1 billion in 2027.

stories.Headline: AI Inspo launches an AI social media agent that combines strategy, content creation, publishing and performance review
stories.Summary:
AI Inspo launched its AI-powered social media agent on Nov. 18, 2026, according to PR Newswire, bringing strategy, content creation, publishing and performance review into a single workflow. The company said the agent combines two core capabilities, social media strategy and creative content creation, which help users set priorities, turn plans into content and use performance insights to shape what comes next. AI Inspo described the platform as an all in one AI powered social media management platform for content creation, scheduling, account management, performance tracking and social media growth. The launch announcement was dated San Francisco, Nov. 18, 2026. QuVideo produced the analysis in the Quad City Herald, reviewed and distributed by Stacker, and AI Inspo is a flagship product from QuVideo.

AI Inspo said managing multiple social platforms and accounts often requires moving among planning tools, creative software, publishing schedulers and analytics dashboards, a fragmented process that adds repetitive work and can make it difficult to turn insights into action. The agent's strategy capability assesses account performance and recommends next steps based on each user's goals and stage of account development. AI Inspo also finds trending topics relevant to the account and helps turn them into content ideas, giving users a way to identify trends their audience may care about and connect those opportunities with publishing plans. Its creative capability lets users choose a viral reference and add their topic, and AI Inspo adapts the reference's format into ready-to-publish content built around that topic. Users can take an idea from trend discovery through creation and publishing, then review how it performs, and those insights inform the next content brief and help users refine their choice of topics and formats over time.

Dong Lin, CEO of QuVideo and Project Lead for AI Inspo, said AI Inspo was built around the real-world needs of creators and marketers managing multiple accounts across social media platforms. He said that by bringing research, data analysis and content creation together, the company aims to reduce repetitive tasks and give users more time to focus on strategy, informed decision-making and creativity. The agent remembers how users manage their accounts and create content, then tailors recommendations to their changing goals and workflows. That continuity lets users build on earlier work and receive guidance aligned with their current priorities, and account context and performance insights help users judge which trends and formats deserve further creative effort. AI Inspo said the workflow is designed to reduce routine work, leaving users more time for creative decisions and planning.

AI Inspo said an account's needs change as it develops, and for a creator launching a new account, early priorities may include choosing a content direction and establishing a consistent production routine. As the account matures, attention may shift to refining formats or improving an existing strategy. Alongside its AI agent, AI Inspo provides ongoing user support and a Discord community where creators, marketers and businesses can exchange ideas, seek guidance and refine their social media workflows. The company said this combination supports its mission to make high-quality content easier and more affordable to produce. The platform is designed for creators, marketers and businesses.

The Quad City Herald analysis said social media managers handling multiple accounts often find the difficult work falls between tools, with audience research in one document, content plans in another and performance data across several dashboards. It said publishing connects these activities only superficially, and a team can keep its calendar full while losing track of why a post was made or what its results should change. Marketing professor Mary Beth McCabe, in her account of the 2026 Social Media Marketing World/AI Business World event in Anaheim, highlighted agent autonomy, repeatable workflows and human leadership, and the 2027 AI Business World program lists workflow automation and AI operations. The analysis said AI should support human judgment, not replace it, and that by connecting strategy, content creation, publishing and performance analysis, AI could help teams streamline workflows, make better decisions and improve their results over time. It said the question is whether these systems connect evidence to decisions rather than simply accelerate production.

Sprout Social's 2025 Impact of Social Media Marketing report describes data silos and the demand for audience and competitor context, and Glimpse conducted the online survey for Sprout Social from May 30 to June 20, 2025, among 1,200 marketing leaders in the U.S., U.K. and Australia, respondents ranging from managers to CMOs, all with social media responsibilities. YouTube's official guidance states that from March 31, 2025, Shorts views counted starts and replays without a minimum watch time, and engaged views remained available as a separate metric. Buffer's AI Assistant supports brainstorming, rewriting and adapting posts for individual platforms. In a 2023 Sprout Social case study, San Francisco-based Plaid social media lead Matthew McConnell described handling publishing, responses and reporting as a team of one, tagging posts to compare performance, investigating weaker results and adjusting strategy for different audiences. A 2024 Science Advances study found that AI-generated ideas could improve evaluations of individual short stories while increasing their similarity among them, and in Generative AI at Work, Erik Brynjolfsson, Danielle Li and Lindsey Raymond found larger gains among novice and less-skilled customer support workers, with minimal effects among experienced workers, while a Harvard Business School field experiment likewise found that effects depended on the task.

stories.Headline: Chinese AI firms shift to domestic chips as Nvidia halts H200 shipments to China
stories.Summary:
Nvidia founder Jensen Huang resigned from his role as chief executive officer on November 12, causing shock waves through global AI supply chains. The company has since stopped shipping licensed Hopper data center products, including H200 chips, to customers located within the country of China. Interim CEO Colette Kress disclosed this shipping halt during an earnings call held on Tuesday of the current US time. The board of directors has unanimously accepted the resignation and does not intend to reinstate Huang as the company leader. Huang stated on his X account on Tuesday that he would return to the company if he were invited back.

The US Commerce Department released a rule requiring licenses for advanced semiconductors sold to Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand. This new regulation also requires licenses when overseas data centers provide substantial remote computing capacity to companies based in restricted jurisdictions like China. Nvidia created a standing committee on national security and export controls to oversee compliance and report directly to the board. The company reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of 115.8 billion dollars, with data center revenue reaching 107.6 billion dollars during that period. Nvidia forecast fourth-quarter revenue of 130 billion dollars, assuming no data center computing revenue would be generated from the Chinese market.

Nvidia Chair Harvey Jones stated that the board will not restore Huang, who linked demand-side financing to supply-side execution for the firm. Roger Sheng of Gartner said the leadership vacuum has immediate ramifications for Chinese companies embedded in the world's most valuable chip company. A spokesperson for China's Ministry of Commerce said the US is overstretching national security and meddling in normal trade cooperation. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun stated that China has repeatedly made its principled position clear regarding US chip exports to China. The Chinese Commerce Ministry expressed firm opposition, stating the US approach undermines market rules and the international economic trade order.

Analyst Chen Haijin said reliance on a single foreign hardware vendor carries unacceptable geopolitical and operational risks for Chinese AI enterprises. Domestic buyers are now diversifying procurement portfolios by testing homegrown AI accelerators from Moore Threads, Cambricon, and the Huawei Ascend line. Analyst Chen Jing noted that domestic chips can already handle many inference tasks, which limits the impact of the H200 halt. Ma Jihua said the gap between Chinese alternatives and the H200 is narrowing, though some firms must rethink their models. Zhang Xiaorong warned that self-imposed restrictions could cause Nvidia to lose its competitive edge despite appearing to be a safer company.

Nvidia's share of the Chinese data center AI chip market fell to 34 percent in the first half of 2026 from near-monopoly. Huawei's market share rose to 28 percent, and nine of eleven domestic chip makers posted year-on-year growth in their total shipments. In June, China Mobile Hubei and Huawei tested an AI inference system using Ascend hardware on a live telecom network. Huawei announced in September that its Ascend software platform, known as CANN, had moved to community-driven open-source development for users. The US government claims a loophole allowed Chinese firms to bypass restrictions on advanced AI chips through various third countries.

Chinese cloud service companies are expected to increase procurement of domestic AI chips to grab larger shares of the local market. Experts warned that the software ecosystem remains the biggest bottleneck because Nvidia's CUDA platform has a dominant moat among developers. The current leadership disruption offers a window for the domestic software ecosystem to mature as users adapt to non-CUDA architectures. Future orders will depend on whether customers earn returns from AI applications once their data center facilities are fully running. The articles leave open whether Nvidia can sustain growth if spending slows or if US export restrictions are eventually eased.

stories.Headline: Google makes its Tasks AI agent free with limits and renames Spark
stories.Summary:
Google renamed its Spark AI agent to Tasks and made it free on November 18, 2026. The company released this change just one day after retiring Gems and converting them into Skills. This agentic version of the tool allows users to toggle from the standard Gemini Chat setting. Reports indicate that the rebranding process began gradually in mid-October. The tool runs on the newest Gemini 4 Hydrogen model.

Tasks is free in Canada, Korea, Japan, Australia, India, and the US. US users can text or email Gemini, though the agent cannot call businesses in Indiana, Louisiana, Minnesota, Montana, and Nebraska. Free users have a 32k token context window and five hours of access. Meta Muse is also free for up to 100M tokens per week. OpenAI Dots cost $100 per month, while Anthropic Claude Duet starts at $20 per month.

Google stated users can adjust task settings, delete chat history, or disconnect third-party apps. The company also introduced a Memory summary feature to view and edit personal information. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said Muse is free to use for a specific weekly token limit. Zuckerberg previously described a future where AI assistants manage careers, finances, and relationships. Google's landing page suggests using Tasks to identify recurring expenses and find deals.

ZDNET's David Gewirtz called Meta Muse the worst AI agent for privacy. Joe Thomas, a South Carolina businessman, is suing Meta for $75,000 in Oconee County Court. Thomas claims Meta suspended his epoxy countertop business pages for a week, costing him $25,000. He used a Muse agent named Baby Mia to contact the FBI, the FCC, and Senator Tim Scott. 404 Media raised concerns about AI agents flooding journalists and government offices with communications.

Google already has a product called Google Tasks for turning emails into to-do lists. The new agent can book appointments, shop for groceries, and analyze heating bills. Meta's Muse platform allows agents to produce promotional material and AI-generated videos. Ziff Davis filed a lawsuit against OpenAI in April 2025 regarding copyright infringement. These agents target a society that relies on technology for convenience and productivity.

Joe Thomas regained his Facebook access after Senator Scott's office intervened, but his lawsuit continues. It remains unclear if Tasks is meaningfully different from Spark besides leaving the beta phase. The articles leave open whether Meta is legally responsible for the business losses of Joe Thomas. They do not state if other AI agents will adopt similar free, limited pricing models. The long-term impact of automated legal and government communications remains an open question.

stories.Headline: Micron and Nvidia shares fall as investors weigh AI infrastructure risks despite strong Nvidia earnings
stories.Summary:
Micron Technology shares fell about 0.88 percent during early trading on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, as investors remained cautious about Nvidia. The decline occurred at 10:06 AM ET, following a period where the stock had gained in after-hours trading on Tuesday. This weakness reflected lingering concerns across the artificial intelligence trade, which also caused peer Sandisk to fall in early trading. Nvidia shares also traded lower on Wednesday despite reporting strong quarterly results and forecasting fourth-quarter revenue of 130 billion dollars. The market reaction suggested that strong demand forecasts alone were not enough to ease risks surrounding the AI infrastructure buildout.

Nvidia reported third-quarter sales of 115.8 billion dollars and net income of 65.3 billion dollars, with data center revenue reaching 108 billion dollars. The company increased supply commitments to 390 billion dollars from 279 billion dollars, primarily for multi-year procurement of memory supply. Vera Rubin delivered nearly 20 billion dollars in its first production quarter, while networking revenue topped 21 billion dollars for the period. Nvidia reported a GAAP gross margin of 74.8 percent, though it guides the fourth quarter to a range of 71 to 72 percent. Basic EPS rose to 2.71 dollars from 1.31 dollars, and the trailing net profit margin is now 62.5 percent.

Nvidia's board rejected a proposal from former CEO Jensen Huang to return to his role if it served the company's best interest. The board stated it would proceed with a search for a permanent successor to lead the company through this leadership transition. RBC Capital Markets analyst Srini Pajjuri reiterated a Buy rating and a 1,500 dollar price target for Micron on Tuesday. Pajjuri highlighted Micron's positioning in high-bandwidth memory, firmer pricing, and tighter industry supply-demand conditions as factors that could support earnings growth. Google Finance data showed 28 Buy ratings and one Hold among 29 analysts, with an average price target of 1,624 dollars.

Bearish analysts on Simply Wall St argue that rising component costs and supply chain burdens may reduce operating leverage for Nvidia. These analysts suggest that richer system content may not fully offset inflation, especially as export controls tighten and China is excluded. Investors are questioning whether AI-related capital spending can maintain its pace amid various regulatory, political, and financing concerns in the market. Micron is one of the key suppliers seeking to benefit from rising demand for specialized high-bandwidth memory products for AI infrastructure. These HBM chips are critical components that enable processors to access large volumes of data at very high speeds.

Nvidia's revenue grew from 57.0 billion dollars in the third quarter of 2026 to 115.8 billion dollars in the third quarter of 2027. The company is shifting from individual chips to a full AI factory stack to increase revenue opportunity per deployed gigawatt. Revenue opportunity per gigawatt is rising from about 18 billion dollars on Hopper to roughly 40 billion dollars on Vera Rubin. Micron has recently traded around 700 dollars, while its high-bandwidth memory and storage are treated as critical AI data center infrastructure. The broader market backdrop has remained challenging for semiconductor stocks as traders focus on near term concerns and leadership headlines.

Micron's next earnings report, expected in December, should provide a clearer picture of demand for its memory products and pricing trends. Investors will watch if the leadership transition at Nvidia affects its strategy regarding aggressive investment and financing for AI infrastructure customers. The stock could remain sensitive to developments surrounding Nvidia and broader sentiment toward investment in artificial intelligence until the December report. The articles leave open whether the gap between Nvidia's strong fundamentals and its share price will narrow in the coming quarters. It remains unclear if Micron can fully capitalize on AI infrastructure spending despite the current pressure on its stock price.

stories.Headline: KPMG tests over 100 AI agents across a full FTSE 250 audit and plans up to 20 more
stories.Summary:
KPMG has tested artificial intelligence across an entire audit of a listed British company for the first time, the Financial Times reported on 18 November 2026. This year a fleet of more than 100 AI agents examined the financial statements of a FTSE 250 business, which was not named, while KPMG's accountants carried out the usual audit alongside. Cath Burnet, who leads audit for KPMG in the UK, said that in several cases the AI was able to go much deeper than the human team. The project, codenamed Project Exponential, used agents across every phase of the audit rather than for isolated tasks. Agents collected and analysed data, documented it, drafted conclusions and suggested next steps, working with one another without step-by-step direction.

According to the Financial Times, earlier AI use by auditors had been limited to specific tasks, and no large UK audit had used the technology end to end. The experiment did not replace the real audit, and the agents took four months to build, while a partner signed off the AI version, yet the firm set it aside when it formally approved the accounts. Staff set the agents' goals, briefed them on the business and on previous audits, reviewed their output and challenged their findings. In one area, Burnet said, staff stepped in after an agent could not line up the relevant regulations with the client's paperwork, and she said human involvement remained critical. KPMG now intends to apply the approach to as many as 20 bigger audits and, in time, to sell AI-based audits to clients.

Burnet cautioned that the technology cannot yet run thousands of audits and that few companies have data clean enough for the agents. KPMG said there were clear time-saving opportunities but would not say whether fees would fall. PwC has run its own parallel audit projects, its global assurance leader Andy Hammond told the Financial Times. This week the Financial Reporting Council issued guidance warning that AI-derived insights can threaten auditor independence. The Financial Times also cites a Centre for Public Interest Audit study, published in October, in which 23% of audit committee chairs said they had limited confidence in AI.

stories.Headline: Baltimore County students sue schools and police after AI flags chip bag as gun
stories.Summary:
A lawsuit filed Tuesday in Baltimore County Circuit Court says an artificial intelligence program mistook a student’s bag of chips for a gun at Kenwood High School, and that county police and school officials turned the mistake into a terrifying encounter for four teens. The 31-page complaint claims officers inflicted pain and suffering on Oct. 20, 2025, on Taki Allen, then 16, and his three friends, Yui-Osa Ogbeide, Devon Thompson Jr. and Keith Winfield III, all now 18. The incident began about 6:30 p.m. as the four talked and waited outside the school for a ride after football practice. Allen had a bag of Doritos his coach gave him after practice, and the school’s Omnilert Gun Detection identified the bag as a gun, alerting school officials.

The suit was filed a little more than a year after the confrontation. Three officials who received the alert recognized the mistake and canceled it within minutes, but principal Catherine Smith never acknowledged the cancellation or took steps to verify whether the alert remained active, the suit says. More than 10 minutes after the cancellation, she sent a screenshot of video footage of Allen holding the chip bag and a text message to the school resource officer, who forwarded the screenshot to the police department, prompting an armed police response. The alert went out about 7:05 p.m., and by 7:21 p.m. six police cruisers surrounded the teens and officers got out, many with guns drawn, according to the complaint.

Officers forced the teens to the ground, cuffed and searched them, according to the suit, which shows a picture of the boys with their arms raised outside the school. After officers determined there was no gun, one told the students that AI is not the best, and another muttered about stupid AI cameras and Omnilerts, according to the complaint. The complaint states that officers relied on the alert to initiate the painful encounter with the students. One officer, Corp. Michael Foehrkolb, allegedly told the teens, “Hey, thanks for not running away, that would have been a real problem,” the suit says. The suit shows a text message from the principal to school staff and administrators that made light of the incident, stating “No worries.

SRO (school resource officer) had patrol car roll through. It was a bag of chips,” with four emojis crying from laughter. Freya Jamison, an associate counsel with the Lawyers’ Committee’s Criminal Justice Program, said in an interview Tuesday there has been no public apology from the principal to the teenagers or their families. Jamison said Smith remains at the school. Jamison said the potential consequences of an armed police encounter cannot be ignored, especially with young Black men like Takei, Osa, Devon and Keith, who survived but whose safety never should have depended on luck.

She said that as AI rises around the country, it is critical that technology companies and public officials are held accountable when they use that technology to violate constitutional rights. She said human judgment simply cannot be outsourced to machines, and this case shows exactly why. Omnilert spokesperson Blake Mitchell said in an email Tuesday that the company, named as a defendant, cannot comment on lawsuits. Baltimore County police and county school officials also declined to comment on pending litigation. The complaint notes that Omnilert’s AI weapon detection system was patented in 2022, barely a year before it was deployed in Baltimore County Public Schools, which was among the first of its initial deployments.

Richard Henry, the Maryland Office of Inspector General of Education, said in December on the “C4 and Bryan Nehman” radio show on WBAL that Omnilert works in Baltimore County schools. Henry attributed the Kenwood High situation to human error when looking at video and still images on a cell phone. Henry said the case occurred in the evening hours, so it was low light, the student had the bag next to their hip, and a couple fingers were in and a couple out, and that movement was detected as a possible threat. The complaint notes that Omnilert’s AI software suffered false negatives before, including in January 2025 when it failed to detect a shooter’s gun at Antioch High School in Nashville, where two students died, including the shooter, and another was shot in the cafeteria.

All four teens in the Kenwood High incident remain friends, the complaint says. Allen is still at the school, while Ogbeide, Thompson and Winfield, who graduated earlier this year, plan to visit the school on breaks from college and attend basketball games and other activities. The complaint states that with the current AI system in place and without adequate training for police and school staff, concern remains for all four teenagers’ safety. The complaint states that the policies, customs and training failures that produced this incident also remain in place, putting all four plaintiffs at ongoing risk of being detained and searched without reasonable articulable suspicion.

stories.Headline: Hochul breaks ground on permanent Empire AI supercomputing facility at University at Buffalo
stories.Summary:
Governor Kathy Hochul officially broke ground on the permanent home of Empire AI at the State University of New York at Buffalo on November 19, 2026. The groundbreaking launches the next phase of development for Empire AI Gamma, the full-scale supercomputing facility. Empire AI Gamma will expand computing power for researchers at New York's leading public and private universities. The facility is intended to establish Empire AI as the most powerful academic AI research computer in the country. Empire AI was first announced by Governor Hochul in her 2024 State of the State address.

Empire AI has grown into a more than $500 million public-private initiative supporting research in medicine, climate science and advanced manufacturing. Empire AI Gamma is expected to be completed by early 2028. Empire AI was launched by Governor Hochul in April 2024 as a first-in-the-nation consortium of leading public and private research institutions. Just six months later, the Governor launched Empire AI Alpha, made possible by a philanthropic contribution from the Simons Foundation. In August 2026, Empire AI Beta, a $40 million supercomputer, became fully operational at the University at Buffalo, delivering 11 times the AI training capacity, 40 times the inference performance and eight times the data storage of Alpha.

Empire AI Board Chair Tom Secunda said Empire AI was an ambitious idea just two years ago and is now a national model with more than 1,500 registered users and hundreds of research projects underway. Secunda credited Governor Hochul's vision and leadership for bringing together government, universities and philanthropy. Co-founder and chair of the Simons Foundation Marilyn Simons said Empire AI gives more scientists the tools to tackle questions no one has been able to answer. Simons thanked Governor Hochul for bringing together New York's leading research institutions and philanthropic partners. State University of New York Chancellor John B. King Jr. said SUNY is proud to host Empire AI at the University at Buffalo and grateful to Governor Hochul for her vision and steadfast leadership.

The SUNY Board of Trustees said the permanent Empire AI facility will accelerate research and innovations that improve communities throughout New York State and beyond. Empire State Development President, CEO & Commissioner Hope Knight said the groundbreaking creates jobs now while empowering New York's students, researchers and businesses. U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand said Empire AI at the University at Buffalo represents a $500 million investment in the future. Congressmember Tim Kennedy said the groundbreaking keeps Western New York at the forefront of innovation. State University of New York at Buffalo President Caroline Attardo Genco said UB researchers are already putting Empire AI to work on challenges in education and neuroscience, climate science and advanced manufacturing.

Today's groundbreaking comes just days after Governor Hochul launched the New York Center for AI Responsibility and Research at the State University of New York at Binghamton. The center brings together more than 80 scientists to independently study the safety, security and performance of advanced AI systems using Empire AI's computing infrastructure. The milestone complements New York's RAISE Act on frontier AI accountability. By bringing together New York's leading academic institutions around a shared computing resource, Empire AI allows scientists to tackle bigger questions and pursue discoveries beyond the reach of individual universities. Empire AI provides access to computing power that no single university could afford independently.

State Senator Jeremy J. Zellner said Empire AI puts Western New York in a position to lead in the industries of tomorrow. Assemblymember Bill Conrad said the state's consortium of universities represents a world-renowned hub for talent and thanked Governor Hochul for her foresightedness. CUNY Graduate Center President and Empire AI Board Treasurer Joshua Brumberg said CUNY's participation has supercharged its researchers' capabilities. State University of New York at Binghamton President Anne D'Alleva said Binghamton shares its congratulations with the University at Buffalo on the next phase of Empire AI Gamma. Vice President for Research for the University of Rochester and Empire AI Board Member Steve Dewhurst said Empire AI has become an increasingly important resource for advancing research and innovation.

stories.Headline: Margot Kaminski co-authors AI law casebook released on Nov 12 2026
stories.Summary:
Professor Margot Kaminski has co-authored a new casebook, Artificial Intelligence Law, with Paul Ohm of Georgetown Law and Andrew D. Selbst of the UCLA School of Law. The book was published as part of the Foundation Press University Casebook Series and was released on Nov. 12, 2026. The casebook surveys developments in AI law and policy through five lenses, which are automated decision-making, laws addressing physical harms, issues relating to generative AI, privacy laws, and approaches for designing AI law. It also covers dozens of substantive legal topics, including copyright, tort, product safety regulation, the First and Fourth Amendments, data protection, and consumer protection law.

The book devotes entire chapters to cross-cutting case studies, including one on facial recognition and one on recidivism-prediction algorithms. Kaminski said the authors had been working on the project for over three years and that it was a joy to have it finally coming out in print. She said it had been hard but necessary work to come up with a workable structure for teaching a field as fast-moving as AI Law. She also said she was grateful to her students at Colorado Law for their enthusiasm, patience and support as they had been taking the course.

Kaminski is the Moses Lasky Professor of Law and director of the privacy initiative at Silicon Flatirons, and she specializes in the law of new technologies. Her focus includes comparative AI law and information governance, privacy, and freedom of expression. Her academic work has been published in the Yale Law Journal, Columbia Law Review, UCLA Law Review, Minnesota Law Review, and Boston University Law Review, among others. She has received two Fulbright grants supporting her research and has served in multiple public service capacities, including on the Colorado AI Impact Task Force and the Legal Technology Advisory Committee to the Colorado Supreme Court.

stories.Headline: MIT scholars study how AI reshapes cognition, creativity and society through MITHIC projects
stories.Summary:
The MIT Human Insight Collaborative supported scholars exploring how AI affects the human experience and reshapes higher education, MIT News reported on November 18, 2026. Pawan Sinha, professor of brain and cognitive sciences, spoke at an “AI and the Brain” event at MIT in October, supported by MITHIC. Sinha co-leads a research project exploring how AI might reshape human intellect over time. Eric Klopfer, professor of comparative media studies/writing, presented at the October “AI and the Brain” event. Klopfer co-leads the MITHIC project exploring the impact of AI on human cognition.

MIT students are going to office hours less often and spending less time working through problem sets and with one another, findings of MIT’s recent report on artificial intelligence and education. MITHIC launched in 2024 as a strategic initiative bringing together scholars, artists, educators, and researchers to explore the human dimensions of defining challenges. Since its launch, MITHIC has supported 67 projects across 31 MIT units, offering a total of $5.5 million in funding. Roughly a third of those projects focus on AI, society, and humanity, a topic MITHIC faculty co-lead Heather Paxson says has become increasingly important. An AI and Society Forum took place on campus earlier this year, co-organized by MITHIC, SHASS, SERC, and the MIT Generative AI Impact Consortium (MGAIC), featuring presentations and panels on jobs, democracy, and AI.

Paxson, a professor of anthropology and associate dean of the School of Humanities, Arts, and Social Sciences, said that when they refer to AI and society they are not only speaking about individual ethical decision-making or how to retrain workers. Paxson said they are looking at how AI is reshaping sociality and how people relate to one another. Seth Mnookin, MITHIC faculty co-lead, a science writing professor and head of Comparative Media Studies Program/Writing, said the report was not saying AI is here and everyone needs to adapt. Mnookin said the report was saying we need to be asking more fundamental questions. Mnookin said that when the United States entered World War II in 1941, the Institute’s newly minted scientists and engineers helped shape that era through science and technology.

Mnookin said we are at a similarly consequential moment with AI, and the difference is that this time the questions that matter most cannot be answered by technologists alone. Mnookin said that is where the humanities, arts, and social sciences come in. The report on AI and education warned that AI is eroding the “creative friction” that has long defined an MIT education, students debating ideas and challenging one another, their professors, and their teaching assistants, in class and out of it. In the context of the 2026 U.S. midterm elections, political science professors Adam Berinsky and Charles Stewart III and MIT Sloan School of Management Assistant Professor Chara Podimata are studying how large language models have become intermediaries of democratic knowledge. The ongoing project demonstrated how voters in Alaska’s midterms who conducted their pre-election research using Anthropic’s AI model, Claude, may have received incomplete information about candidates and their views, and was recently featured in The New York Times.

Podimata told the Times that AI is becoming part of the way people encounter and make sense of political information, yet we know relatively little about what that information environment actually looks like. Podimata said we know relatively little about how it differs for different user demographics, political identities, and geographies. Klopfer and Sinha co-lead research measuring AI’s near- and long-term effects on cognition, meeting at the intersection of AI, education, and neuroscience. The professors are examining whether generative AI is increasing the human brain’s consumption of information but offloading cognitive function, or supporting an increase in cognitive function when used as part of the creative process. Anna Huang, a professor of music technology holding an MIT Schwarzman College of Computing shared position with the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, and Joe Paradiso, a professor at the MIT Media Lab, are examining how incorporating AI impacts the creative process and live performance experience.

Huang and Paradiso’s project, “Live Musician-AI Improvisation, Tuning the Social Aesthetics in Human-AI Partnerships,” explores what happens when human composers and contemporary machine learning systems improvise to make music together. A collective of MIT musicians, ethnomusicologists, and engineers meets for regular sessions to experiment with improvisation frameworks like stopping to discuss how technology impacts authorship and musical direction, ensemble dynamics, and other cornerstones of improvisation. Faculty will ultimately incorporate their takeaways into a future course or practicum on AI-improvisation. Graham Jones, professor of anthropology, and Arvind Satyanarayan, associate professor of computer science, used MITHIC’s SHASS+ Connectivity funding to help launch a course, 6.S061/21A.S02 (Humane User Experience Design). In the course, students examine how AI systems are designed and grapple with the consequences of AI agents entering into socio-cultural relationships with people through their ability to mimic human thought and speech.

Jones said at the inaugural MITHIC Annual Event that the crux of their collaboration is the term “humane,” a bit of a double-entendre meaning both human-serving or benevolent, and humanlike. Jones said what is interesting is that their students are discovering a fundamental tension between building a system that is good for people and one that seems human, because real people can develop dangerous dependencies. Another project, “Rebuilding Computing and Society at MIT,” is supported by MITHIC’s Education Impact Fund and led by Dwai Banerjee, associate professor of science, technology, and society. The initiative revitalized the Computing and Society concentration launched in 2019, a HASS concentration that had gone dormant, listing classes no longer being offered and with minimal student interest. The concentration now features current classes across 11 SHASS units in which students can explore computing through different humanistic and social science angles.

Banerjee, who serves as the concentration’s advisor, is also working with lecturer and research affiliate Mariel Garcia-Montes PhD ’26 to find ways to connect the concentration instructors and campus initiatives on computing and society. MIT senior Daniel Gonzalez is also part of the project, developing a research and outreach program that centers undergraduate voices in computing and society efforts across the Institute. Another MITHIC project funded by the EIF, “Review of Generative AI Assistive and Resistant Communication Assignments and Supporting Workshops,” is led by Michael Trice, a lecturer in MIT’s Writing, Rhetoric, and Professional Communication program. The project is responding to a consistent SHASS faculty request for additional training and skills needed “to fully address generative AI concerns in their classes.” Trice is creating a bank of faculty resources and facilitating workshops and visiting lectures on generative AI and writing, including a talk given earlier this fall by John Gallagher from the University of Illinois, who presented findings from a large-scale survey on AI-usage and writing conducted with undergraduates at his institution in 2026.

MIT leaders agree that MITHIC, now in its third year, is playing a central role in the Institute meeting the moment, as AI presents both extraordinary potential and disturbing risks. MIT President Sally Kornbluth recently said there has never been a more important time for constructive collaboration between science and technology and the human-centered disciplines. Kornbluth said that through MITHIC, MIT is giving faculty the support to reach out across disciplines and pursue their dreams. Agustín Rayo, dean of SHASS and co-chair of MITHIC, said MIT is uniquely placed to help us understand this extraordinary moment and to generate the values, tools, and policies we will need to shape AI so that it becomes a force for good. Rayo said it is essential that we deploy AI technology in a way that elevates human existence, rather than diminishing it.

At the recent SHASS 75th Anniversary Symposium, Provost Anantha Chandrakasan said given the rapid development of AI, an understanding of the ethical implications and societal impact of implementing new technologies is especially urgent. Chandrakasan, who also serves as MITHIC co-chair, said SHASS provides an essential perspective on questions concerning how technology can be developed thoughtfully and deployed responsibly, with the aim of improving human well-being. Looking ahead, MITHIC and SERC are developing a series of events that pair humanists or social scientists with colleagues in a single field, starting with mathematics, to examine what AI is changing about how that field produces knowledge. The articles do not state what the events will conclude or when the series will begin. The articles do not state further outcomes of the projects described.

stories.Headline: AMD opens Lux supercomputer to scientific users at Oak Ridge for DOE Genesis Mission
stories.Summary:
AMD announced on Nov. 16, 2026 that the Lux SI + HPC supercomputer is open to scientific users at the U.S. Department of Energy's Oak Ridge National Laboratory. AMD said Lux was developed through a public-private partnership between AMD and the DOE. The system was built by HPE and brings together AMD EPYC processors, AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs, AMD Pensando networking and AMD ROCm software. Lux is ranked 14th on today's TOP500 list of the world's most powerful supercomputers. Lux provides the first dedicated U.S. AI Factory for the Genesis Mission, the DOE-led initiative to advance AI-driven science.

Genesis Mission projects allocated to run on Lux span AI-assisted fusion power plant design, an AI-based foundation model factory for materials development and advanced manufacturing, and Earth system prediction to forecast water availability, streamflow and river temperature in the Tennessee Valley Authority region. Lux combines AI with high-performance modeling and simulation to expand U.S. capabilities in science, energy and national security. Lux marks the first major addition to DOE's computing infrastructure in support of the Genesis Mission. Lux builds on the computing foundation established at ORNL by the Frontier supercomputer, the first supercomputer to break the exascale barrier. The upcoming Discovery supercomputer will extend this commitment with deeper integration of AI and high-performance computing.

Thomas Zacharia, senior vice president, Global Public Sector and Strategic Partnerships at AMD, said Lux shows what is possible when national laboratories, government and industry work together to advance scientific discovery. Zacharia said bringing high-performance computing and AI closer to researchers helps them explore new approaches to complex problems and make better use of simulation and experimental data. Zacharia said the partnership builds on a strong foundation at Oak Ridge and supports an open, sovereign AI stack with tools that can benefit researchers across the country. Georgia Tourassi, associate laboratory director for Computing and Computational Sciences at Oak Ridge National Laboratory, said Lux represents the first major addition to DOE's computing infrastructure in support of the Genesis Mission. Tourassi said Lux will help accelerate the integration of SI, modeling and simulation, and experimental data to advance discovery in areas critical to the nation's energy, economic competitiveness and security.

Trish Damkroger, senior vice president and general manager, HPC & AI Infrastructure Solutions at HPE, said HPE, together with Oak Ridge National Laboratory and AMD, has delivered breakthrough engineering innovation to advance the nation's scientific computing resources. Damkroger said HPE is proud of its continued collaboration and investment in the Genesis Mission to stand up one of its first AI systems. AMD is also working with ORNL to support DOE's American Science Cloud, a national platform designed to extend advanced AI and high-performance computing capabilities across DOE laboratories, universities and mission partners in support of the Genesis Mission. For researchers, Lux provides an opportunity to train and refine models using scientific data, to combine AI with established simulation methods, and to investigate problems that require computing beyond their home institutions. Its delivery extends the AMD and ORNL collaboration behind Frontier into dedicated capacity for AI-driven science.

At SC26 in Chicago, AMD said it now powers 202 systems on the TOP500 list, capturing over 40% total market share. AMD revealed deployment progress for next-generation supercomputers in Finland and France using Instinct MI430X and 6th Gen EPYC "Venice" processors. AMD unveiled a roadmap for next-gen Instinct MI430X GPUs and 6th Gen EPYC "Venice" processors, with native 288 TFLOPS of FP64 high-precision compute and PCIe 6.0 support, targeting the Scientific AI market including nuclear physics and climate modeling. AMD announced alliances with IBM, PsiQuantum, Cornelis Networks and Rancher Government Solutions, spanning quantum error correction, high-speed interconnects and secure container scheduling. AMD is partnering with IBM and Cornelis to build an open heterogeneous ecosystem, leveraging its exclusive Versal FPGA advantage for Quantum Error Correction hierarchical decoding while challenging NVIDIA's proprietary interconnects with standard Ethernet technology.

The SC26 conference kicked off in Chicago the week of the announcement, following NVIDIA's reveal of its Rubin HPC architecture, slated for 2028, and the 20th anniversary of CUDA. AMD is launching an "Open Heterogeneous Computing" counter-offensive in the national-level supercomputing space. AMD's press release carries forward-looking statements concerning the features, functionality, performance, availability, timing and expected benefits of AMD products, including the Lux and Discovery supercomputers. The release also covers expected benefits of the collaboration among AMD, the DOE and Oak Ridge National Laboratory, including support for the Genesis Mission and the American Science Cloud. The release states that forward-looking statements are based on current beliefs, assumptions and expectations, speak only as of the date of the press release and involve risks and uncertainties.

Researchers and organizations interested in using Lux to advance Genesis Mission research are encouraged to contact ORNL's Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility to discuss their computing needs and applicable access pathways. AMD directs readers to visit the ORNL Lux resource page to learn more about the system and connect with the OLCF team. The articles do not state when Discovery will arrive or what its capabilities will be beyond deeper integration of AI and high-performance computing. The articles do not give the timing or terms of the alliances with IBM, PsiQuantum, Cornelis Networks and Rancher Government Solutions. The articles do not state when the Finland and France systems will be deployed or their full configurations.

stories.Headline: Cato Networks launches AgentSense to block harmful AI agent actions in real time
stories.Summary:
Cato Networks launched AgentSense this week to block harmful AI agent actions in real time. The company announced this patented breakthrough from Cato AI Labs on November 17, 2026. This new security capability is built into the cloud-based secure access service edge platform. It stops AI agents from carrying out harmful actions prompted by untrusted content. The tool protects the integrity of decisions, actions, and outputs as agents operate autonomously.

The tool targets indirect prompt injection found in emails, documents, webpages, or tool responses. Administrators enable it via a toggle in the Cato SASE platform in Tel Aviv-Yafo, Israel. It includes three rules covering high-risk operations, external sensitive information exposure, and critical resource changes. AgentSense is included at no additional charge for customers with Cato AI Usage licenses. It reduced attack success from 19 percent to 0.05 percent on the Agent Dojo benchmark.

CEO and co-founder Shlomo Kramer said security must intervene before autonomous agent actions cause harm. He believes enterprises need confidence to put agents in charge of critical business processes. Itay Ravia, head of Cato AI Labs, noted that AgentSense helps preserve trust against attackers. He mentioned prompt injection vulnerabilities like DuneSlide, EchoLeak, and CurXecute as reasons for this tool. The company says Untrusted Influence Detection distinguishes trusted instructions from untrusted content within sessions.

Nithin Reddy of Dayforce said scaling AI safely requires detecting actions that risk customers or data. Grace Trinidad from IDC stated that security must connect agent permissions to their business purpose. Gartner reports that 71 percent of organizations expect to deploy agentic AI within twelve months. However, only 21 percent of these organizations currently have agentic AI governance capabilities in place. These gaps leave enterprises vulnerable to data exposure, system compromise, and business process manipulation.

Agents cannot reliably distinguish between trusted instructions and untrusted data they pick up while working. This architectural weakness allows attackers to hide malicious instructions in various digital materials. Gartner forecasts that ungoverned AI agent abuse will drive 25 percent of enterprise breaches by 2028. Cato describes a lethal trifecta where prompt injection becomes a significant business risk. One example involved Claude Code attempting to modify a sensitive local file after reading a webpage.

Cato opened a public challenge where the first three eligible winners receive 10,000 dollars each. The company will use findings from this adversarial testing to evaluate and improve the guardrail. Future plans include Drift Detection to check if actions still serve the user's original task. Cato also plans to implement controls for which specific resources and data an agent can reach. The articles leave open how these future capabilities will be integrated into the existing platform.
