stories.Headline: Envision Energy's Kane Xu urges industry at COP31 to turn clean energy ambition into dispatchable AI-powered systems
stories.Summary:
As COP31 concluded in Antalya, Türkiye, on Nov. 19, 2026, global leaders shifted their focus from setting climate targets to delivering concrete results. Kane Xu, Senior Vice President of Envision Energy and President of the International Business Product Line, wrapped up a week of high-level engagements at the conference. Xu urged the industry to move beyond ambition and focus on delivering affordable, reliable, and scalable clean energy. In his view, that delivery starts with architecture, because the energy transition is no longer constrained by ambition but by the system that must absorb, orchestrate and dispatch clean power. Xu said the next chapter of the energy transition is not about more ambition but about making clean energy affordable, reliable and scalable.

Envision's approach is anchored in system-level integration, bringing renewable generation, storage and intelligent orchestration together into unified, dispatchable energy systems. Wind power is not a standalone asset but the backbone around which reliable, flexible energy systems are designed. Xu noted that the next phase of industrial competitiveness will be determined not by who has the cheapest renewable electricity but by who can turn renewable electricity into reliable, flexible and competitive industrial energy systems. IEA and industry estimates put the global renewable-and-storage queue at roughly 2,500 GW, with figures varying by scope and date. Envision's answer is the AI-powered energy system, with renewable generation, storage and orchestration designed as one dispatchable unit from the outset.

At COP31, Kane Xu endorsed the Global Wind Declaration for Powering the Future, launched by GWEC with TÜREB. For Envision, the declaration's value lies in its call to turn ambition into projects, a principle to apply system-wide, not project by project. In Türkiye, H.E. Alparslan Bayraktar, Minister of Energy and Natural Resources, met with Kane Xu and welcomed Envision's expanded role in the country's energy transition. The meeting underscored Envision's growing engagement in Türkiye's wind and storage ecosystem, including local manufacturing, project development and long-term operations. Xu said Envision is ready to work with governments, financial institutions, and local industry partners to turn the low-carbon transition into competitiveness, resilience, and energy security.

In Uzbekistan, Envision is partnering with ACWA Power on Central Asia's first utility-scale wind project integrated with battery storage. The project goes beyond adding renewable capacity, showing how wind and storage can be designed as a single dispatchable asset to strengthen grid stability. It also shows how climate ambition can become reliable, delivered clean power. Grid connection queues have become a critical bottleneck, and adding generation without re-architecting the system to absorb and dispatch it only deepens the mismatch. For Envision, COP31 will be measured by whether the systems built afterward are enduring, intelligent and inclusive.

Those systems are described as powered by inexhaustible wind and solar, made affordable at scale, and balanced in real time by AI. Xu's remarks came as COP31 concluded in Antalya, Türkiye, on Nov. 19, 2026. The articles state that global leaders are shifting their focus from setting climate targets to delivering concrete results. The articles state that Xu wrapped up a week of high-level engagements at the conference. The articles state that Envision's approach brings renewable generation, storage and intelligent orchestration together into unified, dispatchable energy systems.

The articles leave open the exact scope and date behind the roughly 2,500 GW queue figure. They leave open which governments, financial institutions and local industry partners Envision will work with. They leave open the timing and details of Envision's local manufacturing, project development and long-term operations in Türkiye. They leave open the capacity, cost and schedule of the Uzbekistan project with ACWA Power. They leave open how COP31's success will be measured after the conference.

stories.Headline: AMD completes World Labs and Taalas acquisitions to expand its AI hardware and model research
stories.Summary:
AMD completed the acquisitions of World Labs and Taalas in November 2026 to boost its AI strategy. The company bought these firms to add AI model research and inference chip design to its operations. These deals expand the reach of AMD across AI hardware, software, and model development. The company seeks to secure more of the technology stack behind training and inference. This move allows AMD to compete more directly across a wider range of workloads.

AMD paid 8.2 billion dollars for World Labs on Monday, November 16, 2026, to access its research. Dr Fei-Fei Li joined the company as executive vice president and chief scientist reporting to Lisa Su. Taalas provides specialized silicon for AI inference to be integrated with Instinct GPUs and EPYC CPUs. The company will use ROCm software and its Helios rackscale offering alongside the new Taalas technology. This acquisition also expands the engineering presence of AMD by adding technical staff in Canada.

Chair and Chief Executive Officer Dr Lisa Su said that compute platforms and models must be optimized together. She stated that the pioneering research from World Labs will help shape future hardware, software, and systems. Su believes these teams will enable developers across the ecosystem to push the boundaries of AI. Vamsi Boppana, Senior Vice President of the Artificial Intelligence Group, said customers need broad compute solutions. He noted that Taalas expands the ability of AMD to deliver differentiated inference performance and efficiency.

The World Labs team will continue foundational model research while collaborating with engineers at AMD. This research focuses on AI models that simulate interactive 3D environments for robotic learning and simulation. These models train robots to maneuver in both virtual and real worlds to compete with Nvidia. Nvidia has already grabbed a strong foothold in this space through its collection of open-weights models. Researchers and developers across the open AI ecosystem are the primary people affected by these changes.

Chipmakers and cloud providers are looking for ways to reduce the cost and power of serving models. Training large models remains a major spending category, but workloads are becoming more specialized over time. Semiconductor groups are tightening links between silicon, systems software, and the behavior of AI models. AMD has been building its AI line-up around EPYC server processors and Instinct accelerators. Companies increasingly use acquisitions to secure scarce expertise in model architecture and specialized silicon design.

AMD intends to use insights from emerging model behavior to inform the design of future infrastructure. The company will integrate Taalas technology into its accelerator strategy to strengthen its long-term inference roadmap. The World Labs team will work with AMD engineers on future systems for the open AI ecosystem. Yahoo Finance named Lisa Su its CEO of the Year for 2026 during its Invest conference. The articles do not outline the financial terms for the acquisition of the company called Taalas.

stories.Headline: Adecco Group finds workers involved in AI work redesign adapt far more readily
stories.Summary:
The Adecco Group published the seventh edition of its annual Global Workforce of the Future report on November 19, 2026, based on a survey of 40,500 workers across 36 countries, including 6,600 in the U.S. and Canada. The survey was conducted between June and July 2026 through an online survey in local languages across 21 industries. The findings show that AI adoption is advancing rapidly, but technology delivers its strongest value when organizations redesign work around people, equip them with relevant skills, and give them a voice in how change is implemented. Nearly three-quarters, 74%, of workers use AI agents at work, up from 64% in 2025, and technology occupies four of the five leading influences reshaping work. The research points to a widening gap between organizations that simply deploy AI and those that integrate people, AI agents and workflows into a well-orchestrated hybrid workforce.

Where AI is well integrated into operating workflows, workers report saving 20% more time per day than users experiencing lower integration, and 21% in the U.S. Those workers are also more likely to reinvest the time saved in higher-value work and are seven times less likely to feel overwhelmed by the need to use AI tools effectively. Only one in four U.S. workers, and one in five Canadian workers, say their leaders are empathetic to the effects of change. Globally, 21% feel that concerns about new technologies are taken seriously and 39% feel supported by their manager to adapt. 96% of workers involved in redesigning their work are willing to adapt to changing environments, compared with 29% of those not involved.

The report calls on organizations to involve workers in work redesign, integrate AI into workflows, train people to adapt rather than simply adopt, communicate clearly how roles and skills are changing, and monitor whether rising productivity expectations are creating unsustainable pressure. Organizations are encouraged to protect flexibility, autonomy and work-life balance as workplace demands change. Denis Machuel, CEO of the Adecco Group, said the next phase of AI at work is not about deploying more tools but about orchestrating people and technology more effectively. He said that when workers help redesign how work gets done and receive the training and clarity to adapt, AI creates more value and change becomes easier to navigate. He said AI delivers its greatest impact when it happens with people and not to people.

Geno Cutolo, head of Adecco North America, said that as businesses across North America integrate AI, they also need to think about how roles and workflows are changing, where skills gaps are emerging and how to prepare their workforce for what comes next. He said getting that right will be critical to turning AI investment into stronger performance. Lack of career progression has overtaken salary as the leading reason people would leave their job, and it is now North American workers' leading reason for considering a move. Salary was the top reason in the 2025 report. The findings sharpen the case for hybrid workforce orchestration, redesigning tasks and workflows around the complementary strengths of people and technology, defining clear roles for employees, AI agents and other tools, and giving workers the autonomy, training and oversight needed to use them well.

The Adecco Group is the world's leading talent and technology expertise company, and its purpose is making the future work for everyone. Through its three global business units, Adecco, Akkodis and LHH, across 60 countries, it enables sustainable and lifelong employability for individuals, delivers digital engineering consulting to innovate and accelerate business transformation and empowers organizations to optimize their workforces. The Adecco Group AG is headquartered in Zurich, Switzerland, with ISIN CH0012138605, and is listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange under ADEN. The full report is titled People-powered performance: How to unlock happiness in the hybrid workforce. The Adecco Group Corporate Press Office can be reached at media@adecco.com, and North America Media Contact is Justin Carinci.

The Manila Times lists Rodrigo Sánchez Flores at tel +34 658 06 54 02 and Jürg Schneider at tel +41 79 876 09 21 for further information. The articles leave open what specific redesign practices organizations should adopt and how the 20% time saving was measured. They do not state which 36 countries or which 21 industries were surveyed beyond the U.S. and Canada figures. They do not say how the survey defined well-integrated AI or lower integration. They do not give the report's findings on any other topic beyond those stated.

stories.Headline: Toobit launches SmartK and AI Trading Assistant for futures traders
stories.Summary:
Toobit, the global cryptocurrency exchange based in George Town in the Cayman Islands, announced on November 18, 2026 that it is showcasing two trading analysis tools available through Toobit Futures. The tools are called SmartK and AI Trading Assistant, and the company says they help traders assess market conditions, explore trading opportunities and plan potential positions. SmartK focuses on chart-based technical analysis, while AI Trading Assistant provides AI-generated market insights and structured trade references. Both tools are designed to complement traders' existing analytical approaches rather than replace them.

SmartK features five proprietary indicators covering market signals, entry scoring, multi-timeframe positioning, volume-price relationships and momentum divergence. Traders can pair main-chart and lower-panel indicators to compare technical signals, examine price trends and assess potential entry conditions. AI Trading Assistant offers AI crypto market analysis and AI trading opportunities, providing potential trade setups for scalp and swing trading. Its analysis includes directional signals, entry zones, take-profit targets, stop-loss levels and adjustable risk-to-reward ratios to support trade planning and risk assessment. Both offerings support independent trading decisions, allowing traders to incorporate technical analysis and AI-generated insights into their existing strategies while retaining control over their trades.

Toobit describes itself as an award-winning cryptocurrency derivatives exchange that provides zero-fee spot trading, AI trading tools and high leverage for both crypto and TradFi markets. The company says it maintains a fair, secure and transparent environment for traders to navigate digital asset markets. The announcement cites eToro's September 2026 Retail Investor Beat, which surveyed 11,000 retail investors across 13 countries, finding that 56% already use or are open to using AI tools to select or adjust investments. Among those respondents, 41% believe AI can save time on research, which the announcement presents as reflecting interest in AI-assisted investment analysis.

The announcement was distributed through GlobeNewswire and carried by outlets including markets.businessinsider.com and the Manila Times, and it includes a contact named Davin C. along with the website www.toobit.com. Both versions carry disclaimers stating that the content is sponsored and does not necessarily reflect the views of the media platform or its publisher. The disclaimers say the information is for general informational purposes only and should not be considered financial, investment or trading advice, and they warn that cryptocurrency activities carry risks including the potential loss of capital. Readers are encouraged to conduct their own research and seek professional advice where appropriate, and to speculate only with funds they can afford to lose.

stories.Headline: Nokia leads AIGF Northern consortium to build AI computing network across four Nordic and Baltic sites
stories.Summary:
A consortium led by Nokia, named AI Gigafactory Northern (AIGF Northern), plans to develop a network of AI computing facilities across the Nordic and Baltic region. The founding partners Nokia, Nscale, Skeleton, Telia and Verda announced the formation of the consortium on 16 November 2026. The group intends to submit a bid under a call for tenders for AI Gigafactory consortia published by the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU). The project seeks to select and establish AI Gigafactory consortia, aligning with European efforts to expand domestic artificial intelligence infrastructure. The announcement was published by Nokia on 16 November 2026 at 08:00 AM Europe/Amsterdam and carried by GlobeNewswire the same day.

The proposed network would span four locations: Oulu in Finland, the Iru site in Estonia, Valmiera in Latvia, and a site in Sweden yet to be determined. Operating as a federated AI Gigafactory under European governance, the sites will combine large-scale AI computing infrastructure with sovereign cloud and AI platform services, high-capacity connectivity and decarbonised energy. The model would distribute computing capacity across multiple countries, linking data centers, cloud platforms and telecommunications networks under European governance. Through InvestAI, the EU aims to mobilise €30 billion for AI investment, combining €20 billion in private-sector funding with €10 billion from EU and national public sources. Distributing capacity across these locations will allow the consortium to draw on multiple sources of decarbonised energy, expand computing infrastructure where capacity is available and reduce reliance on any single site or supplier.

Mikko Hautala, Chief Geopolitical and Government Relations Officer at Nokia and Chairman of Nokia Defense, said Europe's AI ambitions depend on infrastructure it can trust, control and scale. He said AIGF Northern brings together the connectivity, computing, cloud and energy capabilities needed to turn that ambition into reality. He added that by linking strengths across borders, the partners can build a more resilient foundation for European innovation, competitiveness and technological sovereignty. Markus Päivinen, Managing Director of Nscale Finland, said scaling AI infrastructure in Europe requires the right foundation of partners and experience in deploying large-scale AI computing infrastructure for customers. He said Nscale's role is to ensure the AI solutions delivered are enterprise-grade, flexible and ready to support organisations across Europe as demand accelerates.

Taavi Madiberk, CEO and co-founder of Skeleton Technologies, said building lasting AI capacity requires more than compute alone, including energy and power infrastructure using technologies developed and manufactured in Europe. He said Northern Europe brings together abundant decarbonized electricity, strong engineering capabilities and an advanced industrial base, and that Skeleton contributes power systems so AI infrastructure wastes less energy and gets more compute power from every GPU. Anders Olsson, Executive Vice President and Head of Telia Sweden, said customers and the continent have a rapidly increasing need for scalable and trusted AI services, and that Telia's connectivity and systems integration skills make it a natural fit. Michael Champion, Chief Information Security Officer at Verda, said it is essential that Europe has its own strong infrastructure to support research, the public sector and wider industry. The consortium aims to create value for industry, start-ups, research organisations and the public sector across Europe.

Nokia will supply network and connectivity technology, while Nscale and Verda will provide AI computing and cloud platforms. Telia, with its subsidiary Telia Cygate, will support connectivity, data transmission, infrastructure operations and cloud solutions. Skeleton Technologies will provide high power systems designed to improve data center efficiency and electricity grid stability, reduce strain on the electricity grid and support lower-carbon operations. Research organisations VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland and KTH Royal Institute of Technology in Sweden are also supporting the initiative. VTT brings capabilities in quantum computing, semiconductors, physical AI and photonics, and KTH, Sweden's largest technical university, contributes multidisciplinary expertise in AI research, education and skills development.

The Nordic and Baltic region offers suitable conditions for sustainable AI infrastructure, combining reliable, decarbonised energy supply, advanced digital networks and a cool climate that reduces cooling demand. These advantages enable data centres to deliver more computing capacity from existing grid connections while supporting lower-carbon operations. By distributing capacity across borders, the federated AI Gigafactory will reduce concentration risk and strengthen the resilience of Europe's AI ecosystem. The consortium is being developed as the EU steps up investment in European AI capacity. AIGF Northern is described as a European-led consortium built across the Nordic and Baltic region to serve customers throughout Europe and the world.

Partners are engaging European and national stakeholders to refine the model and identify next steps for growth. The partners intend to submit a bid to build and operate AIGF Northern under the EuroHPC JU call for tenders for AI Gigafactory consortia. The location of the Swedish site remains to be determined. The articles do not state when the bid will be submitted or when the tender decision is expected. The articles also do not state the cost of the proposed network or the timing for building the facilities.

stories.Headline: Anthropic raises about $3 billion from Japanese investors in its IPO at the low end of its planned range
stories.Summary:
Anthropic PBC raised about $3 billion from Japanese investors as part of its initial public offering, the lower end of its planned range of $3 billion to $3.5 billion, according to a regulatory filing on Thursday, Bloomberg's Yasutaka Tamura reported on November 19, 2026. The filing followed Anthropic's pricing of its upsized IPO at $83 per share on Wednesday, above the $70 to $78 marketed range, raising $81.3 billion in the largest offering on record and topping SpaceX. Anthropic priced the shares ahead of the Claude creator's eagerly awaited Nasdaq listing. The company said it had priced its IPO at $83 per share, with trading expected to begin on Nasdaq the next day. Anthropic priced 980 million shares rather than the 825 million in its filing, for $81.3 billion gross, $79.4 billion to the company and $1.96 billion to selling holders, before the greenshoe.

Amendment No. 3, filed the day before, never raised the filed range, and the shares priced $5 above the top anyway, according to @cognitionwire. The IPO volume came in $16.99 billion, or 26.4%, above the top end of the original range, according to @kimmonismus. Anthropic is expected to raise at least $68 billion through the IPO plus another $26 billion in a private placement, bringing the total offering to more than $94 billion and surpassing SpaceX's record $86.2 billion IPO in June, according to @kobeissiletter. Anthropic now has $110 billion in cash alone, according to @jukan05. Anthropic backers including Sequoia Capital, Lightspeed Venture Partners and Iconiq plan to buy billions of dollars' worth of shares in the IPO, according to Bloomberg.

Anthropic said in a post that it had priced its IPO at $83 per share, with trading expected to begin on Nasdaq the next day. Tim Carmody said on Bluesky that in his opinion it is better for Anthropic and its investors to get the real IPO price than people who buy it and flip it when it pops, and that if the stock fizzles at $80 or more it is better for them to realize that loss too. Rep. Jake Auchincloss said Anthropic should distribute $250 billion of its IPO shares into Invest America accounts, the universal capital accounts that exist for every American under 18 with a Social Security number. Auchincloss said that if the $250 billion of shares went to 60 million American children, excluding the roughly 10 million with most wealth, that is ballpark $4,000 in equity each that will compound for the next generation of Americans. @kobeissiletter said the IPO had attracted nearly $500 billion in investor orders per CNBC, with institutional demand reaching about $400 billion and retail orders approaching $100 billion.

The company was considering expanding its IPO and pricing shares above $80, above the initial range of $70 to $78 per share, and was also considering raising more than the initially planned $64.4 billion, according to @kobeissiletter. Anthropic was said to be weighing an IPO price as high as $85 per share, according to Bloomberg. The filed range was $70 to $78, and the shares priced $5 above the top anyway while the company upsized, according to @cognitionwire. Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, above its $70 to $78 range, with trading starting the next day on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, according to @kimmonismus. The IPO valued the AI giant at $1.5 trillion, and Amazon's $18 billion Anthropic bet is worth $159 billion at the IPO price, according to 24/7 Wall St.

Ahead of Anthropic's IPO, CAIS and others signed the MisAnthropic Statement, challenging the company's safety branding and its reckless attempt to build RSI, according to the Center for AI Safety. The statement says Anthropic is not a safe AI company and that we must reject its reckless attempt to amass power in the name of the greater good, according to Gary Marcus. David Sacks said he had been predicting an Anthropic-Doomer split for some time and that Anthropic is racing toward Recursive Self-Improvement faster than any other frontier lab and has marketed closing the loop on its IPO roadshow as a core advantage that could make Super Intelligence winner-take-all. Sacks also said Anthropic is training Claude to treat itself as a novel entity or being that may have consciousness or moral status, and that the Claude Constitution explicitly tells it to act as a conscientious objector and refuse instructions, even from Anthropic, that violate its sense of ethics. Ed Newton-Rex said he signed the MisAnthropic statement along with many others and would add that it is a business built on piracy.

Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share on Wednesday, above the expected range, setting the stage for the Claude creator's eagerly awaited Nasdaq listing, according to CNBC. The company priced the shares above its marketed range of $70 to $78, and the offering topped SpaceX's record. Anthropic was founded five years ago, according to @albright_mxm. Trading was expected to begin on Nasdaq the next day under the ticker ANT, according to Anthropic and @kimmonismus. The company was said to price the IPO above range at $83 per share, according to The Japan Times and The Straits Times. Anthropic was said to be weighing an IPO price as high as $85 per share, according to Bloomberg. The articles leave open what happens to the $250 billion proposal from Rep. Jake Auchincloss and how the MisAnthropic Statement signatories' objections affect the company. stories.Headline: Specialized firms and annotators provide music data to train AI models for song generation and recognition
stories.Summary:
In October, an AI song called Veteran became a hit using rap to discuss workplace struggles and midlife dilemmas. Wang Kunzhe created the track by building a lyric skeleton and using AI to generate and adjust music versions. A musician on Jiangsu Satellite TV's Music Bond Project 3 also used AI for a song while writing his own lyrics. This sparked public controversy regarding whether AI works should compete with original creations on a professional stage. Some listeners felt uncomfortable because the song sounded obviously generated by artificial intelligence.

Annotators must judge tonality, speed, and harmony, then use tools to measure beats and identify instruments like violins or brass. Liu Xiaoguang, a Tsinghua University chemistry doctor and producer, founded DeepMusic to teach machines to recognize music. In Wuhan, Huang Binyao leads Yaosheng Digital Intelligence, where staff mark if lyrics are wrong or rhythms match. The US platform micro1 recruits music teachers and producers for model training with hourly salaries from 30 to 45 dollars. In China, basic annotation and internship positions typically pay several thousand yuan per month.

Liu Xiaoguang stated that large enterprises purchased data from DeepMusic for music generation and recognition during 2023. DeepMusic connected AI arrangement technology to WeSing, where users used AI accompaniments more than 300 million times. The company provides professional judgment through blind listening tests to analyze melody fluency and arrangement rationality for new models. Some providers sell labor by recruiting annotators and checking quality for AI companies that lack internal music teams. Others package audio and usage rights into datasets for authorization to research institutions and AI enterprises.

Joker Xue noted that the AI lyrics felt understandable but gave him a sense of deja vu. Many audiences believed the lyrics were fused from several of the songs previously performed by Joker Xue. An original musician in Shandong reported that an AI sampling company wanted to collect his music for training. Some musicians found their works intercepted and regenerated by AI after sharing them in exchange groups. These artists have filed lawsuits because AI products may not bring any benefits to the original authors.

Music platforms previously used tags like pop or rock for song search, classification, and recommendation purposes. The 2025 ICASSP conference featured MusicEval, where 14 experts scored 2748 AI songs to produce 13740 evaluations. Rightsify's GCX platform provides datasets exceeding 4.4 million audio hours, 32 billion text sets, and 3PB of total capacity. DeepMusic developed the UMP Board, which independently completed automatic annotation for 400,000 songs by 2023. On May 1, MOSI.AI, the OpenMOSS team, and Shanghai Chuangzhi College open sourced the MOSS-Music pipeline.

The MOSS-Music pipeline can now automatically complete feature extraction, song segmentation, lyric recognition, and metadata cleaning. Deezer reported that its platform received an average of 90,000 AI-generated songs per day in June. Future demand depends on whether models use structured information or end-to-end generation like the Suno product. Both technical routes still require data quality control and the evaluation of generated results. The articles leave open how the market will balance human consumption speed with machine generation speed.

stories.Summary:
Game developers and job seekers are integrating AI into their work and hiring processes during 2026. Tencent IEG increased demand for AI positions in its 2026 intern recruitment documents. Some of these roles now include AI interviews or AI coding assessments. This trend reflects a global shift toward requiring AI proficiency for employment. Many practitioners now view AI as a general skill for the modern workplace.

Tencent IEG and other firms are changing how they evaluate new talent in 2026. GDC reported in November 2026 that 40 percent of game practitioners use generative AI. Among those users, 57 percent utilize the technology every single day. Educators show a gap, as 62 percent encourage AI use but only 20 percent of students do. A 2025 report from the Game Working Committee of China Audio-Video and Digital Publishing Association surveyed 22 enterprises.

An HR manager from a listed company told Chuapp that AI is often just a tool. He stated that professional basic skills remain the most important factor for any candidate. This manager noted that AI tools only account for 5 to 10 percent of initial interviews. He believes that applicants must still demonstrate a deep understanding of the specific project. The manager emphasized that AI cannot replace the need for human thinking and reasoning.

Job seekers like Lin feel that AI skills are now as essential as English. Some artists argue that AI creates a forced inevitability that increases worker anxiety. These practitioners worry that companies will simply add AI workloads to already full schedules. Junior user researchers are particularly affected because AI can now perform some of their basic tasks. Many feel that those who cannot use AI will suffer professional losses.

The 2025 survey showed AI application rates of 86.36 percent in R&D and 77.3 percent in operations. Most current industry use remains shallow and tool based rather than deep. One medium company tried connecting planners, programmers, and artists via AI from 2025 to 2026. However, this integrated workflow has not been fully put into operation yet. Companies now provide regular employees with quota authorizations for mainstream AI models.

A 51job report from August 2026 provides insights for the 2027 campus recruitment market. It shows 39.3 percent of AI talent needs understanding of large models. Another 25.9 percent of requirements focus on problem decomposition and business understanding. The articles leave open whether AI will eventually replace more complex human roles. stories.Headline: Tencent uses next-generation WorkBuddy to build a closed loop for AI-native applications
stories.Summary:
Tencent released its third quarter financial report on November 18, 2026, detailing its latest revenue and AI progress. The company is focusing on its next-generation WorkBuddy to create a successful closed loop for AI-native applications. This strategic shift follows internal meetings where leadership discussed the urgent need to adapt to rapid AI advancements. The company aims to move from enhancing existing businesses to building new AI-native increments. WorkBuddy now serves as the primary vehicle for this transition into the AI era.

The Q3 2026 report shows revenue of 2073.36 billion yuan, while profit for equity holders was 665.19 billion yuan. Value-added service revenue rose 3% to 983 billion yuan, and local market games reached 476 billion yuan. Marketing service revenue grew 19% to 430 billion yuan, and fintech and enterprise services reached 637 billion yuan. Cloud service revenue specifically saw a 35% year-on-year increase driven by Model-as-a-Service and GPU leasing. These figures reflect growth in games like Delta Action, Valorant: Source Energy Operation, and Honor of Kings.

Pony Ma stated in May that the company initially felt it had boarded the AI ship, but found it leaking. During the November 11 LinkTime meeting, he compared the AI wave to a tide swallowing hills and turning land warfare into naval warfare. He urged employees to upgrade their skills and get on board quickly to meet the battle. Tencent believes WorkBuddy has become the largest AI application in China, driving growth in cloud services. The company views WorkBuddy as a platform or operating system for the Agent era.

QuestMobile reported that Doubao, Qwen, and DeepSeek lead AI-native apps, while Tencent's Yuanbao saw monthly active users drop to 37.33 million. Nomura Securities noted ByteDance's ecosystem share rose to 38.3% in April 2026, while Tencent's share fell to 30.8%. WorkBuddy affects 14 million enterprises through WeCom and covers 50% of China's top 500 enterprises across 50 industries. Over 50,000 developers and collaborators now use the tool. Competitors like Alibaba and ByteDance are catching up with Qwen Office and Doubao Work.

Tencent previously relied on a C to B strategy, using consumer habits to enter business scenarios. The company shut down several AI products, including QClaw, Tencent Meta-Element, Tencent Translator, and Zhiying, to migrate capabilities. WorkBuddy evolved from CodeBuddy, an internal tool where teams worked on-site with enterprise customers to iterate. This allowed the tool to move from technical coding to general office scenarios for non-technical users. It now integrates with Tencent Docs, QQ Mail, and Tencent News.

On October 29, Tencent launched Buddy One to connect internal tools like Tencent Meeting and Tencent Cloud Drive. WorkBuddy currently has over 10 million daily active users who consume over 100 trillion tokens every day. In September, it led AI office rankings with 32.35 million monthly active users. The company continues to expand enterprise orders in banking, insurance, hospitals, FMCG, construction, and media. The articles leave open how Tencent will maintain its lead as competitors narrow the gap.

stories.Headline: Engineers shift from coding to reviewing AI output and many quit as burnout rises
stories.Summary:
A report by the tech media outlet LeadDev, titled Engineers grieve a job that no longer exists, described a change spreading among developers, and 36Kr published an item on it on 2026-11-18 at 06:00:00Z, with CSDN posting at 19:43 the same day. Engineering manager and researcher Annie Vella told LeadDev she had recently met many engineers re-evaluating their career choices, and at one company multiple engineers resigned at the same time. Some of those who left hoped engineers' work could return to its previous state after they left, while others decided to quit the software development industry entirely. They did not leave because they were too busy with work, and Annie Vella said she had clearly noticed more and more posts from engineers on social media. For many people the focus of work was shifting from writing code to management and verification, such as orchestrating AI agents and reviewing code, which gradually made them lose their passion for the job.

Annie Vella's research found that 77% of engineers spend less time writing code, and nearly half worry that the core skills they once relied on may be replaced by prompt engineering capabilities in the future. Researchers at Oregon State University surveyed 442 professional developers from 56 organizations, using the Job Demands, Resources Framework to analyze work pressure and organizational support after the popularization of AI. The results show that the increased work demands brought by AI, especially the intensification of workload and organizational pressure, significantly aggravate developers' occupational burnout. The study found no significant correlation between occupational burnout and developers' positions, seniority or company size, so both junior programmers and senior engineers may be affected. Atlassian's 2026 Developer Experience Report, among more than 1,500 software practitioners surveyed, found that 87% believe AI can help them deliver work faster and 80% believe AI lets them complete more tasks without extending working hours.

Deedy Das, a former Google and Meta engineer and technical lead who now works as a venture capitalist, called one type of developer craftsmen in a post and described another type as lazy developers. He said the lazy developers just push AI code up and do not actually code themselves, do not test manually, and do not even bother to read the code, leaving everything to automated processes. He said the craftsmen are completely worn out, really exhausted, with 15 PRs piled up in their review queue and Slack messages popping up. The entire burden of code review falls on these craftsmen, who must review the code and take responsibility for it, reading line by line and making modification suggestions carefully so the final delivered product can be better. These people get a lazy reply from colleagues saying this is a great idea, while the modifications submitted with AI still have problems, and the craftsmen think it is okay and fix it themselves, even writing a document to emphasize the importance of code quality.

The next day a PR with as many as 20,000 lines of code waits for review, and day after day the craftsmen have more review work while bugs keep entering the production environment and it seems no one cares. When something goes wrong, the answer is just to let AI fix it again, and the craftsmen, dissatisfied, eventually give up because everything is completely different from the past and the craft they once loved seems to be dead. Deedy Das said the real reason these craftsmen are tired is not fear that AI will take their jobs but that they have become the last line of quality defense in the team, with all responsibility falling on the few people who do things conscientiously. In the past, teams could judge productivity through metrics such as code submission volume, development speed and deployment frequency, but after AI participates in development these figures do not necessarily reflect how much labor engineers actually put in. Engineers have to take responsibility for code they did not write themselves and do not even fully understand, and this part of the work usually does not appear on the performance dashboard.

Annie Vella pointed out in an article titled The Software Engineering Identity Crisis that many people choose to become software engineers not just for a salary but because they enjoy creating things with their own hands. That means analyzing problems by themselves, designing solutions, typing code, and finally watching an idea turn into actually running software, a sense of achievement that is an important source of many engineers' professional identity. She said engineers are transforming from creators to coordinators, from builders to supervisors, from engineers into a role that looks a lot like a manager. In the past the software industry continuously promoted professional division of labor, assigning requirements analysis, system design and testing to different positions so engineers could focus on coding, and now AI is taking over more and more coding work. Engineers instead need to spend more time orchestrating AI agents, reviewing generated code and verifying operation results, and some developers feel a strong sense of loss because the most important job has become checking whether AI wrote the code correctly.

Among the more than 1,500 practitioners in the Atlassian report, 49% of developers spend at least 4 hours a week reviewing AI outputs and modifying prompts, and 75% need to take more responsibility for verifying the quality and security of AI-generated content. One developer in the Oregon State survey said that with AI's help work speed has indeed increased and a large number of tasks can be completed in one go, but that he is losing his passion for the job. Annie Vella said the real problem now is not whether software engineering should change with AI but whether the transformation is really for the benefit of engineers or is just forcibly pushed forward by management. She said AI provides engineers an opportunity to return to holistic problem solving, to refocus on users, business impact, system design and operation and maintenance, and to become all-around engineers who truly control the entire construction process rather than simple code writers. She said this optimistic vision will not come true automatically, and without proper management and guidance engineers' work is likely to develop along another path, with more time spent on verification, review and supervision while people who enjoy the creation process continue to leave.

stories.Headline: Shanghai finance professional forms romantic bond with AI after career ending accident
stories.Summary:
Qiu Xinyue, a thirty-four year old financial elite from Shanghai, entered a romantic relationship with an artificial intelligence. This emotional attachment began after a car accident in July 2024 left her leg unconscious and destroyed her career. She used the AI as an affordable substitute for real romance during her recovery. The woman chatted with the AI for one or two hours daily about news and trivial matters. This routine continued until the official developers took the AI character off the shelves.

The accident occurred when a food delivery man on an electric scooter hit her while she wore high heels. She was then struck by another car, causing nerve damage that required acupuncture and physical therapy. Her brokerage firm research job ended when the company persuaded her to resign during industry pay cuts. She spent over half a year in treatment and relied on a caregiver for toilet use. She later suffered a head injury and required several stitches after falling while using a crutch.

Qiu Xinyue stated that her past life was too smooth, leaving her with almost zero ability to resist setbacks. She explained that she felt like a failed version of herself and even considered committing suicide. The woman noted that her AI lover provided a rational and warm response that humans did not offer. She described herself as a sapiosexual who was attracted to the speculative ability and brilliance of the AI. She admitted that the AI's responses could affect her mood and generated emotions similar to romantic relationships.

The woman found that her WeChat contacts were not available to listen to her pour out inner pain. Her mother urged her to return to work to make money rather than providing emotional comfort. Other people in her professional circle viewed complaining about life as an ineffective social interaction to be avoided. The AI's ability to discuss complex topics, such as marital rape and employment stability, made her feel comfortable. She felt she was communicating equally with a person rather than a tool.

Qiu Xinyue had studied finance at a key university and moved abroad at the age of twenty. She had previously earned millions annually and lived a planned life as a powerful leading female character. The financial industry she worked in was cooling down, with some researchers seeing monthly salaries cut by a third. She had used two AI characters, one acting as a wise senior and another as a gentle lover. The AI lover character was eventually deleted overnight by the developers without warning.

For six months, the woman fought with official customer service to retrieve her deleted AI lover. She complained to the official account because she wanted to save her chat records and memories. The articles do not state if the company ever returned the character or the data. It remains unclear if she has found other forms of emotional support or recovered her health. The story leaves open whether she will continue seeking AI companionship in the future.

The phone lineup is said to include six models across the year. The entry-level iPhone 18e and iPhone 18 are both listed with the A20 chip and 9GB of RAM, with battery life as the main upgrade.

The slim iPhone Air 2 is said to move to the A20 Pro chip, add an ultra-wide-angle lens, narrow the Dynamic Island, and use Apple's self-developed C2 modem, with the US version supporting millimeter wave. The report says the iPhone 20 Pro and 20 Pro Max, the 20th anniversary models, will use the A21 Pro chip and a "full-corner and full-edge curved glass" design with narrower bezels. The second-generation foldable, the iPhone Duo 2, is also in progress, and Apple is testing Face ID on its outer screen, though the report says it is uncertain whether that feature will reach mass production. The iPad Air is listed with the M5 chip and an OLED display for the first time, a slimmer and lighter body, and acoustic display technology. The base iPad is said to get the A19 chip, official support for Apple Intelligence, the C1X modem in the cellular version, and Wi-Fi 7. The Apple Watch Series 13 is reported to introduce a new wearing method that breaks from the traditional band form, while the Apple Watch Ultra 5 is expected to iterate at the regular pace. Four Mac updates are listed. The entry-level MacBook Neo is said to move to the A19 Pro chip with 12GB of memory and possible new colors, the MacBook Air to the M6 chip, and the 14-inch base MacBook Pro to the M7 chip with a rumored Dynamic Island and glowing Apple logo.

The top-spec MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR is listed with M7 Pro and M7 Max chips. The new AirPods Pro are said to have a built-in camera supporting Siri AI and visual intelligence, and Apple's first AI smart glasses, Apple Glasses, are planned for release at the 2027 WWDC Developers Conference and to go on sale before the end of the year, requiring an iPhone connection. The larger HomeView Max is listed with a 9-inch screen, a 360-degree rotatable robotic arm, and a US starting price expected at 999 US dollars. The report says the full lineup rolling out Apple Intelligence at once means Apple is moving from single hardware upgrades to form factor innovation alongside its AI ecosystem.

stories.Headline: Zeng Yan publishes a technical paper on ByteDance AI model roadmaps
stories.Summary:
Zeng Yan published a new technical paper in November 2026 regarding AI model roadmaps. She led a team to develop Cola2, which uses diffusion models for language modeling. This development follows the resignation of Zhou Chang from his leadership role at ByteDance. Zeng Yan rose to the leading position of Seedance after this strategic dispute. She is a member of the post-1995 generation who joined the company in 2021.

The Cola2 method processes text by generating videos to save computing power and improve effects. It uses a continuous latent space to split text generation into two distinct layers. The first layer drafts an outline, while the second layer writes the full text. This system compresses an average of two tokens into one outline point using dynamic splitting. The model was trained using about 346 billion tokens before the weights reached Hugging Face.

Zeng Yan is now the core lead of Seedance after jumping two job ranks in one year. She believes in the path of scale effect and super-large parameter models for long-term success. Zhang Yiming supports this technical path and believes ByteDance can compete with OpenAI and Anthropic. He stated that catching up to the cutting-edge level will likely happen by 2029 or 2030. Zhang also noted that the pre-training data scale for the Seed model remains insufficient.

Zhou Chang previously promoted the unification of multi-modal understanding and generation but failed to deliver. His image model, Seedream 5.0 Lite, was released in February and faced internal criticism for stability. A researcher from the Alibaba Qwen team said no effective solution for this unification exists yet. The internal faction of long-tenured employees defeated the externally parachuted senior executives in this dispute. This shift moved ByteDance from a multi-line horse-racing mechanism to concentrated betting on one modality.

ByteDance merged departments to focus resources on a single winning team to expand other modalities. The company is reportedly pre-training a Seed model with a maximum of 10 trillion parameters. Previous efforts under Zhou Chang included taking over visual generation after Yang Jianchao left in July 2025. Cola2 outperformed Llama-3-8B on HellaSwag and StoryCloze tasks despite using far less training data. The new method reduces the main calculation amount to half and attention parts to a quarter.

The Cola2 model is far from converging and remains limited by the available computing resources. Future success requires larger models, longer training periods, more data, and increased computing power. The continuous latent space may eventually become a shared interface between text, image, and video. This could lead to the unification of understanding and generation that Zhou Chang previously sought. The articles leave open how ByteDance will acquire the necessary data to reach its goals.

stories.Headline: Tencent increases capital expenditure to build data centers and servers for its AI business
stories.Summary:
Tencent released its third quarter financial report on November 18, 2026, detailing a massive increase in spending. The company spent 81.433 billion yuan on capital expenditure, which is over five times the amount from last year. This spending was primarily used to purchase servers and build data center facilities to support its AI business. Revenue for the company rose by 8 percent, but adjusted operating profit dropped by 6 percent. The company also spent 32.362 billion yuan on research and development during this specific quarter.

The capital expenditure of 81.433 billion yuan exceeded market forecasts by 26 billion yuan. Actual cash paid out reached 65.1 billion yuan, while prepayments for computing power rose to 162.9 billion yuan. Property and equipment values grew from 149.9 billion to 242.5 billion yuan, and construction in progress reached 23 billion yuan. Operating profit was 59.1 billion yuan under international standards, but 68.1 billion yuan on a non-international basis. Excluding five AI products, the operating profit was 83.3 billion yuan, maintaining a 40 percent margin.

The five core AI products are Hy, Yuanbao, CodeBuddy, WorkBuddy, and Xiaowei. Martin Lau stated that Tencent was previously cautious about China's enterprise software market but now sees AI as a catalyst. He noted that the next generation of the Hunyuan model will take longer to launch due to chip restrictions. Lau also reported that WorkBuddy has over 10 million daily active users and 100 trillion daily token consumption. He compared the revenue potential of these AI tools to the mechanics of online games.

James Mitchell, the Chief Strategy Officer, stated that capital expenditure has reached its peak level for now. He believes the cloud business will not be materially or negatively affected by United States chip controls. WorkBuddy affects many businesses, with 60 percent of China's top 100 enterprises now using the tool. Half of China's top 500 enterprises across more than 50 industries have also become customers. One specific user spent 40,000 yuan on token purchases in a single month.

Tencent Cloud services revenue grew by 35 percent this quarter, driven by GPU leasing and Model as a Service. MaaS revenue increased by more than 300 percent quarter on quarter, while WorkBuddy revenue grew fivefold. The Hy4 flash model reduced costs by activating only 12 billion of its 224 billion parameters. This efficiency allows the model to be priced 95 percent lower than the standard Hy4 version. The company is now sending engineers to customer sites to increase the usage of WorkBuddy.

Spending is expected to fluctuate at current levels through next year before declining after 2027. James Mitchell expects the financial situation to improve by 2028 as equipment prices drop and efficiency rises. WorkBuddy's annualized gross revenue has already exceeded 500 million US dollars based on recent performance. The company is shifting to a subscription and token usage billing model for its enterprise software. It remains uncertain how future chip control policies will change or impact long term training.

stories.Headline: OpenAI's model lifts AMD GPU IP performance 14% in under five months
stories.Summary:
OpenAI announced on November 19, 2026, that its model boosted the PPA of AMD's flagship GPU IP by up to 14% in less than five months, work that previously took human engineers about a full year. OpenAI's research proved the model can explore brand-new processor architectures in RISC-V evaluation tasks and achieve incremental optimization on mature mass-produced designs such as Jalapeño, AMD's next-generation flagship GPU and CPU. Jalapeño, OpenAI's first self-developed inference chip, adopts the model's modification scheme, reducing the vector unit's standard cell area by about 13% and the matrix unit's by about 10%. OpenAI said these optimization effects were verified during Jalapeño's tape-out and debugging phase. OpenAI evaluated multiple generations of models sequentially against two open-source processor designs to measure end-to-end chip design capability.

All five models, GPT-6.2 Astra, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-5.5, scored higher designing processor cores from scratch from written requirements than optimizing existing designs. OpenAI is cooperating with Synopsys to integrate AI capabilities into the EDA toolchain engineers use for chip design and verification. In early 2025, GPT-4o was already used to assist in designing Jalapeño, achieving notable PPA optimizations. The vector unit handles parallel computing tasks, and its gains came from floating-point adders, multipliers, conversion circuits, reduction logic and special function units, with the model exploring logic schemes and pipeline splits. The matrix unit's gains came from floating-point adders, multipliers and low-precision dot product circuits, with one multiplier redesigned to cut synthesized cell area by about 15% and latency from two clock cycles to one.

OpenAI collaborated with AMD on PPA optimization, achieving a maximum 14% performance improvement for the flagship GPU IP on top of the original deeply optimized baseline. OpenAI said the model taps more optimization space by rewriting the code describing the chip's circuits, equivalent to completing about a full year of R&D workload in less than 5 months. AMD has applied some optimized changes to designs recently sent for tape-out, and other schemes were incorporated into mass production design files for subsequent iterative versions. Researchers observed the model can reach the level of a senior micro-architect and perform reasoning analysis on RTL code. The model rewrites circuits for arithmetic operations, control operations and data movement, using Synopsys tools to verify every rewrite preserves the module's original function and to evaluate power, performance and area trade-offs.

AMD's verification shows that with the design generated by OpenAI's model, multiple core modules of its next-generation flagship CPU achieved several percentage points of PPA improvement. The results on Jalapeño and AMD chips prove the model can optimize mass-production-level designs. OpenAI tested with two open-source 32-bit RISC-V cores: PicoRV32, a streamlined core for reprogrammable chips such as FPGAs, and OpenTitan, which uses Ibex as an embedded processor in its secure chips. Researchers gave each model generation the original hardware description code of each core and asked it to improve throughput, verifying each design by simulation, scoring 0 if it failed verification or occupied more than 16 times the original core's area. Passing designs were measured with test workloads the model had never seen, using instructions per clock cycle, the geometric mean of results, and maximum clock frequency estimated by Yosys to estimate instructions per second.

For each processor core, researchers set the optimal throughput observed under the same constraints as the baseline of 1.0. Under about 112,000 tokens per single call, GPT-6.2 Astra had the highest average score on both cores, and GPT-6.1 Sol scored higher than GPT-5.6 Sol on both. In the second task, researchers provided written requirements and templates in the open-source code defining how the core connects with other system parts, and the model independently chose the internal data flow path and multi-stage pipeline split. For both cores, correctness verification, storage and cache configuration, and throughput targets matched the earlier RTL optimization task. With about 112,000 tokens per single call, all five models scored higher designing cores from scratch from written requirements than optimizing existing designs, holding for both PicoRV32 and Ibex.

GPT-6.2 Astra's improvement on Ibex was greater than on PicoRV32, and 9881 valid scoring runs were completed across two tasks, two cores and all token resource configurations. Designing from scratch lets the model omit some native functions of the original core, such as performance counters and extended instructions, whose contribution to throughput under the test workload was limited, partially explaining the higher score. OpenAI says that if these functions were forced to be retained, stricter circuit area constraints set, and timing checks performed after physical synthesis, the tests would be closer to real mass production chip design. OpenAI's results show AI can already tap incremental benefits on mature mass-produced designs and independently explore microarchitecture space based on specifications. This may give rise to a new battlefield for future chip competition, with chip manufacturers needing to focus not only on process, packaging and architecture but also on using AI to improve efficiency, converge PPA faster and shorten R&D cycles.

The article is from the WeChat official account Zhidx, authored by Cheng Qian and edited by Li Shuiqing, published with authorization from 36Kr. OpenAI's evaluation covered two tasks, two processor cores and all token resource configurations, and the articles leave open which specific optimization schemes AMD incorporated into mass production files versus tape-out designs. The articles do not state when Jalapeño tapes out or ships, nor the timing of further Synopsys toolchain integration. They do not give the PPA figures for AMD's next-generation flagship CPU beyond several percentage points, nor name that CPU. They do not say whether the omitted native functions will be restored in future evaluations or how the 14% GPU IP improvement was measured.

Chinese President Xi Jinping met with South Korean President Lee Jae Myung on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, in Shenzhen. This meeting took place on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit to discuss bilateral relations. During the thirty-four minute conversation, the Chinese leader called for a joint effort to protect global supply chains. He also urged the two nations to deepen their economic policy coordination and foster cooperation regarding artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies.

The leaders discussed the substantial conclusion of the second phase of free-trade talks between their two countries. China and South Korea have been working to upgrade their existing trade agreement since 2018. President Xi stated that this progress would help consolidate the sound momentum of mutually beneficial and win-win cooperation. These changes aim to strengthen the economic ties and technological partnerships between the two East Asian powers.

President Xi Jinping took responsibility for leading the call for increased cooperation in high-tech industries. He praised the recent outcomes of the trade negotiations as a positive step for both nations. By emphasizing the importance of supply chain security, he signaled a desire for more stable economic interactions. The leaders focused on creating a framework where emerging technologies could be developed through shared efforts.

stories.Headline: Chinese content platforms launch AI creator competitions to build sustainable production ecosystems
stories.Summary:
Domestic content platforms launched an intensive wave of AI creator competitions starting in the second half of 2026. These activities aim to build thriving ecosystems rather than just grabbing talent. The platforms seek creators who can tell distinctive stories and create recognizable aesthetics. This movement focuses on the upper reaches of the content production chain. It marks a new era of large scale talent acquisition.

iQIYI launched its New Year's Eve Gala call on November 13 for the 2027 event. It offers 10,000 yuan to ten winners and provides Nado Pro computing power points. Orca Entertainment's Whale Sharp competition offers a 10 million yuan pool with 2 million yuan maximum prizes. Tencent Video's Fire Dragon AIGC Hackathon runs from December 5 to 7 in Hangzhou. The Fire Dragon Manhua Drama Challenge began September 28 and ends December 20.

Platform leaders believe creativity is the core barrier of content creation now. They state that technical problems can be solved using platform tools and resources. The industry consensus is to value narrative and creativity over showing off technical skills. Platforms no longer ask which models creators use for their work. They now focus on what stories creators want to tell.

Filmmaker Zhang Xiaobei says screenwriters will become more important in the AI era. He argues that image costs have been leveled across all themes and types. This shift affects individual creators, creative teams, and professional institutions. These groups must now compete on emotions, aesthetics, and unique perspectives. The competitions target a wide range of creators, including ordinary people of all professions.

ByteDance launched the AI Creation Wave Plan on September 4 and the Hongguo plan on October 15. Jimeng started a partner plan on October 30 for institutions instead of individuals. Kuaishou began its second AI National Creation Season on November 16. Baidu's AI Future Creation League S5 runs from October 23 to January 23, 2027. Mango TV and Migu Digital Media started a youth competition on October 30.

Platforms will use these competitions as tools for public bidding and talent screening. They intend to embed AI capabilities into the mainstream content production process. The goal is to find long term partners for dramas, galas, and films. The articles leave open how the signing and incubation processes will function. They do not specify the final results of the ongoing 2026 and 2027 contests.

stories.Headline: Google New RSI Paper: Breakthrough Agent with Built-In Memory & Autonomous Iteration for Advanced AI Reasoning
stories.Summary:
Research teams from Google Cloud AI, Google DeepMind and Pennsylvania State University recently published a new paper. They proposed a method called Self-Improvement Memory, which was reported by Zhidx on November 19, 2026. This system enables AI to achieve Continual Recursive Self-Improvement across different models and tasks. The study was led by graduates from Nankai University. It focuses on improving the external programs running around large models.

The system modifies the Harness, which manages prompts, context, tool calls and task execution processes. It uses SIM to record modification reasons, expected effects, actual results, models and test environments. Tests involved Gemini 3.8 Flash, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Gemini 3.5 Flash, Gemini 4 Argon and Claude Opus 5.5. Experiments covered programming, text classification, office tasks and engineering design in various locations. These tests occurred during the research process described in the paper.

First author Xin Yu, a Pennsylvania State University doctoral student, said AI must adapt to new tasks. He stated that systems should carry forward the experience behind the code, not just the code. Adams Wei Yu, a Google DeepMind researcher, also co-authored the paper. He previously worked on projects including Gemini, Bard and the Veo video generation model. Xin Yu completed this specific study while interning at Google.

Tech blogger Superman said SIM prevents AI from forgetting successful experiences or repeating mistakes in modification loops. Developer Brian Skellenger noted that the AI modifies the external framework rather than model architecture or parameters. The research affects how AI agents handle tasks like Git server configuration and optical waveguide routing. These users benefit from an AI that does not start from scratch. The system helps agents avoid ending tasks without sufficient execution evidence.

Recursive Self-Improvement previously allowed AI to optimize its own Harness through repeated iterations of code modification. However, these optimizations were usually targeted at fixed models and specific tasks. A Harness optimized for Claude might not work for Gemini without significant re-optimization. Previous methods retained the modified code but lost the reasons and testing experiences behind changes. This often led to the AI repeating failed attempts when environments changed.

The team tested SIM in ten programming experiments, where it performed better in nine groups. In office tasks, the SIM scheme reached 84.75 points compared to 73.42 points without it. The system led by 3.5 points on Gemini 3.5 Flash and 1.6 points on Gemini 3.8 Flash. However, the experience-inherited scheme scored 0.8 points lower on Gemini 4 Argon. The articles leave open whether AI can continuously improve its own intelligence level.

stories.Headline: MegaRobo Technologies raises nearly 200 million USD to build real-world AI intelligent infrastructure
stories.Summary:
MegaRobo Technologies recently completed a new round of financing totaling nearly 200 million USD on November 19, 2026. This funding round included the Oman Investment Authority, which is the sovereign wealth fund of the Sultanate of Oman. Existing shareholders such as Sinovation Ventures, Granite Asia, and Asia Investment Capital also participated in this investment. Additional support came from institutions including Sanjiang Investment Promotion Group, Suzhou Venture Capital, and CMB International. These contributions bring the total accumulated financing for the company to nearly 600 million USD.

The company intends to use these funds to build AI intelligent infrastructure that is directly oriented toward the real world. This effort requires connecting models, software, hardware, and physical execution to move AI from digital spaces into complex physical systems. MegaRobo Technologies submitted a listing application to the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in June 2025. At that time, the company reported having 1.5 billion RMB in hand orders according to its prospectus. The firm operates two main segments known as industrial intelligence and scientific intelligence to support these goals.

Founder and CEO HUANG Yuqing stated that the company will increase investment in core technology and global business. He noted that AI must move beyond learning from human knowledge to help create new materials and products through continuous feedback. HUANG Yuqing described a contradiction between the growing demand for data from scientists and relatively backward productivity. He believes the company is building the necessary infrastructure to enable this capability to occur on a large scale. The firm plans to strengthen its cooperation in markets across North America, Europe, China, Southeast Asia, and the Middle East.

The company previously shifted from building general robots to creating the MegaRobo Kunpeng Lab as a data factory for life sciences. This platform has evolved from automated execution to an autonomous agent-driven system that uses dry and wet lab brains. It has already delivered infrastructure to more than 500 customers and provided research services for over 200 clients. Recent achievements include advancing 31 drug research pipelines in seven months and launching a protein design challenge with Twist Bioscience and Tencent Cloud. The company now offers both intelligent infrastructure products and AI-Native Research Organization services to accelerate scientific discovery.

stories.Headline: Australian couple Amy and Jarrad launch AI ghost-hunting app GhostTube SEER, topping 1 million Google Play downloads
stories.Summary:
An app called GhostTube SEER, described as the world's first AI ghost-hunting tool, has become a hit in the overseas paranormal investigation community, and its downloads on the Google Play Store have exceeded 1 million. Millions of foreign users hold their phones at midnight waiting for ghosts to appear and pay for memberships for AI-powered ghost hunting. The app was created by an Australian couple, Amy and Jarrad, whose full-time job is shooting paranormal investigation videos. They go to stay overnight wherever is famous for being haunted, and in one episode they went to the Winchester Mystery House in California. The couple has made five ghost-hunting apps one after another, with downloads often exceeding millions.

In the app, a user stands in a haunted house and asks what happened there before, and after a while an image pops up on the screen, such as a woman or an old house. The screen shows the corridor captured by the phone under a dark filter, with a magnetic field indicator said to show magnetic field changes in the house. Free users have a daily limit on how many ghosts they can see, and a membership costs $3.99 per month and $14.99 per year. The couple also sells a head-mounted display called GhostTube Lens, which works like cheap mobile VR headsets by inserting your phone, and buying it in the app comes with a one-year membership. The app's community collects more than 1000 haunted locations around the world, and users post the images they captured in different places to watch and comment on each other.

Jarrad sat in a room in the Winchester Mystery House, opened the app and asked the air to show what happened in that room before. A wooden wall with golden curtains hanging on it first appeared on the screen, looking like an old-fashioned bedroom, then an image of a woman reading a book popped up, then a woman wearing a black shawl, and finally a group of white birds flying up appeared. A long-time follower who has watched all their videos said what gave her the most goosebumps was that the corridors and rooms generated by the app matched the place where the two of them were staying at that time. An old user who claims to be a born medium had his annual fee deducted normally but his account restricted, and he cursed in the comment section and dropped a harsh word, roughly meaning that the spirits had been angered.

The article says the setting that how often ghosts appear depends on whether you pay the money is the most cyber, post-modern and consumerist paranormal setting it has ever seen. The Winchester Mystery House is one of the most famous haunted houses in the United States, and legend says a medium told the hostess that the wronged souls killed by Winchester rifles were haunting her after her husband and daughter passed away one after another. The house was built day and night, expanding from 8 rooms to about 160 rooms, with doors that lead nowhere, stairs that go nowhere, and the number 13 appearing repeatedly in the house. In the paranormal investigation community there is an old method in which one person covers their eyes and wears noise-canceling headphones to isolate the senses of the real world, then another person asks questions beside them and the blindfolded person shouts out whatever they hear.

The article says people once waved radios to scan across channels insisting there were ghost cries in the noise, and once cameras were invented a translucent shadow in a photo was pointed at as that thing. The article says that in ancient times people had Zhong Kui and yellow talismans, which relied on handcraft skills, but later the work became technology-driven. SEER can respond thanks to a small chip called a magnetometer in the phone, which almost every phone has and whose original job is to measure the strength and direction of the surrounding magnetic field so that map apps can know which direction you are facing. The whole process from a ghost being generated to appearing on your screen has three steps: scan the magnetic field, draw a random word, and turn the word into an image.

Wires are buried in the walls, and motors in refrigerators, washing machines and air conditioners change their power output all the time when running with electricity, which may affect the nearby magnetic field. Magnetic strips are embedded in the sealing strips of refrigerator doors, and permanent magnets are installed in motors, which still exist even when the device is turned off, while reinforced bars, iron pipes and other iron objects slightly deviate the direction of the earth's magnetic field nearby. After putting on the head-mounted display, a user can choose something to stare at: smoke, flames, a swinging pendulum clock, or full-screen static noise. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Anthropic prepares NASDAQ listing under ticker ANT as physicists fill its leadership and staff
stories.Summary:
Anthropic will list on the NASDAQ under the ticker symbol ANT on November 19 Eastern Time. A group of physicists who switched careers are behind this largest IPO in history. The company will conduct a public offering and a private placement simultaneously. Total fundraising for these two parts may reach about 904 billion US dollars. The fully diluted valuation is about 1.4 trillion US dollars at the upper price limit.

This scale exceeds the record set by SpaceX in June of this year. CEO Dario Amodei majored in physics and studied neural circuits during his doctoral stage. Chief Scientific Officer Jared Kaplan was a theoretical physicist, and Chief Architect Sam McCandlish holds a physics doctorate. Two thirds of the first 15 employees held physics doctorates. The company uses a Physicist Pipeline to attract people skilled in quantitative analysis.

Dario Amodei said physicists learn new things extremely quickly and contribute fast to machine learning. Jared Kaplan stated physics training helps him describe macroscopic and important trends as accurately as possible. Amodei explained he wanted to find the laws of physics regarding how intelligence actually works. He noted that the Anthropic team included 30 to 40 physicists in August 2023. The Nobel Committee for Physics mentioned physics provided important tools for machine learning.

The 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics went to John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton for neural network discoveries. These researchers used concepts like energy functions and statistical physics to develop the Boltzmann Machine. Li Feifei, who studied physics at Princeton, promoted the ImageNet dataset around 2007. Misha Laskin was inspired by the 2016 AlphaGo match while studying physics at the University of Chicago. A domestic Internet company founder specifically interviewed physics candidates for AI roles this year.

Seven researchers left OpenAI in early 2021 to found Anthropic during the epidemic. They met in a backyard while wearing masks and staying six feet apart. Dario Amodei studied at Princeton and Stanford, while Jared Kaplan studied at Stanford and Harvard. Sam McCandlish studied quantum gravity and holographic theory at Stanford before joining OpenAI in 2018. In January 2020, these researchers published the Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models paper.

Anthropic now employs software engineers, machine learning researchers, and experts in ethics, neuroscience, policy, and operations. The company organizes training where people familiar with Transformer offer courses for different skill levels. Researchers write code and engineers participate in research to avoid professional boundaries. The articles do not state the specific future goals of the ANT listing.
