stories.Headline: Nvidia moves to annual GPUs as Vera Rubin holds HBM capacity flat
stories.Summary:
Nvidia has moved to annual GPU introductions, and its Vera Rubin generation keeps about 288 GB of HBM per GPU while delivering more than twice the memory bandwidth of Blackwell Ultra, 24/7 Wall St. reported on November 18, 2026. Dr. Robert Castellano wrote the article for the site. The piece said the annual upgrade cycle no longer produces consistent increases in high-bandwidth memory capacity per GPU. It said Micron and other memory manufacturers can benefit from HBM4’s higher performance and pricing. It said future revenue growth will depend increasingly on system shipments, memory technology, and manufacturing economics.

The article’s Table 1 gives HBM per GPU and memory technology from 2020 to 2027. The A100 of 2020 had 80 GB of HBM2e, the H100 of 2022 had 80 GB of HBM3, the B200 Blackwell of 2024 had 192 GB of HBM3e, and the B300 Blackwell Ultra of 2025 had 288 GB of HBM3e. Vera Rubin in 2026 has 288 GB of HBM4, and Rubin Ultra in 2027 is projected at about 1 TB of HBM4e. The article said capacity rose from 80 GB in the H100 to 288 GB in the B300, a 3.6-fold increase, and that the B200 to B300 step raised capacity from 192 GB to 288 GB, an increase of 50%. The article names Micron Technology, Samsung Electronics, and SK hynix as the three principal suppliers of advanced HBM.

It said Micron has invested heavily in HBM manufacturing technology, advanced packaging, and DRAM capacity to expand its participation in AI infrastructure. It said Micron’s investment opportunity increasingly depends on qualification for successive GPU generations, manufacturing yields, and the profitability of higher-value memory products. It said SK hynix has established a strong position in advanced HBM and benefits from its manufacturing experience and relationships with leading AI accelerator customers. It said Samsung is pursuing the same opportunity through advanced DRAM manufacturing and HBM packaging investments. The article said the central investment question is whether future HBM revenue growth will be driven primarily by increasing memory capacity per accelerator or by higher-value memory technology, more systems deployed, and improved manufacturing economics.

It said the distinction matters because these factors can produce very different revenue and profitability outcomes for memory suppliers. It said HBM4 provides substantially higher bandwidth through a more advanced memory architecture, including a wider interface and more demanding manufacturing requirements. It said these improvements increase the value and complexity of the memory supplied, even when the number of installed gigabytes remains unchanged. It said revenue can increase through higher selling prices and a richer product mix without a comparable increase in total memory capacity. The article’s Table 2 compares rack-level HBM capacity and bandwidth.

The GB200 NVL72 contains approximately 13.4 TB of HBM across 72 GPUs, rising to 20.7 TB in the GB300 NVL72, a 54.7% expansion. Vera Rubin NVL72 maintains approximately 20.7 TB while increasing aggregate HBM bandwidth from 576 TB/s to 1,400 TB/s, about 2.4 times the bandwidth with no increase in installed HBM capacity per rack. The article said a hypothetical deployment of 10,000 GB300 NVL72 racks would require approximately 207,000 TB of HBM capacity, and that replacing them with 10,000 Vera Rubin NVL72 systems would require approximately the same aggregate HBM capacity. It said 15,000 Rubin racks would raise total installed HBM to approximately 310,500 TB, an increase of 50%, with that growth coming from additional systems rather than greater memory capacity per system. The article said Nvidia explained in a recent technical discussion of memory optimization how hardware and software improvements can increase the amount of useful computation performed with a given quantity of memory.

It said the company reported that Vera Rubin NVL72 can deliver up to 30 times the agentic AI throughput per megawatt of GB300 NVL72 in a specified workload, even though installed HBM capacity remains approximately unchanged. It said that figure is workload-specific and should not be interpreted as a universal 30-fold performance improvement. It said the transition from H100 to B300 combined increasing GPU shipments with a dramatic expansion in memory installed per accelerator, multiplying demand for advanced DRAM capacity. It said Rubin Ultra could eventually reverse the capacity plateau if Nvidia delivers approximately 1 TB of HBM per GPU. The article said investors should distinguish that projected future increase from the current Rubin architecture rather than assuming every annual GPU transition follows the same pattern.

It said higher bandwidth alone does not guarantee higher revenue if pricing premiums decline or production costs increase. It said a supplier that achieves strong HBM4 yields could capture meaningful margin benefits, while one experiencing production difficulties could face higher costs despite favorable demand. It said Samsung’s ability to improve yields and secure high-volume customer qualifications will influence its participation in the next generation. The article ended mid-sentence at “the next,” leaving Samsung’s outlook and the rest of its assessment unfinished. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Nvidia’s Annual GPU Upgrades Are Changing the HBM Investment Outlook - 24/7 Wall St.

stories.Headline: California agency recommends state safety standards and shutdown powers for frontier AI developers
stories.Summary:
California’s Government Operations Agency recommended on 16 November 2026 that the state require large frontier AI developers to meet state-set safety standards, accept ongoing oversight by licensed independent verifiers and face emergency shutdown orders, in a report released on 18 November 2026. Governor Gavin Newsom’s office announced the recommendations on 18 November 2026 under the title AI Safety in 2026 and Beyond, prepared by the California Government Operations Agency with the California Office of Emergency Services and an outside expert group. The 85-page report answers Executive Order N-9-26, which asked for proposals in four areas: standards, independent verification organizations, critical safety incident reporting and emergency shutdown requirements. The governor’s announcement summarises the package as baseline standards for all AI developers, mandatory ongoing third-party oversight, authority to order a shutdown in an emergency and authority to cap recursive self-improvement. The office defines recursive self-improvement as a scenario in which an AI model can design its own successor without human input, and the recommendations are not law.

The report recommends that the state set baseline safety, security and transparency standards for large frontier developers, with independent verification organizations translating them into technical tests and updating them as the science moves. It recommends that every large frontier developer submit to ongoing oversight by licensed IVOs with full access to the people and information they need, with unredacted assessments going to the state, and that developers could contest a state determination in court before it takes effect. It recommends cutting the deadline for most critical incident reports from 15 days to 48 hours, keeping 24 hours for imminent catastrophic risks, adding a near-miss channel, extending whistleblower protection to former employees and contractors, and treating models capable of catastrophic-risk actions as frontier models even if trained with fewer than 10^26 operations. It recommends that each developer maintain a Risk Containment Protocol verified by an IVO, that state officials could order an immediate shutdown on credible evidence of an imminent catastrophic risk or major loss-of-control event, and that the order would stay in force pending judicial review although a developer could seek a temporary restraining order. It recommends that developers report metrics on how much of their AI research and development is automated, including the share of compute devoted to it, and that the state get standby authority to cap recursive self-improvement if it finds a risk of catastrophic harm.

Unite.AI added that the proposals include a quarterly breakdown of how automating developers divide their compute among training, research experiments, safety work and customers, and that open-weight developers would face containment duties only for deployments under their control. The report says the state should draw on organizations outside government, including industry, civil society organizations and universities, to build AI evaluation capacity, and the SB 813 definition of an AI auditor it quotes includes an academic institution. The report says demand for chips has been pricing out talented researchers who are working on vital safety and security issues, and it recommends funding CalCompute, the public cloud cluster that SB 53 floated but which has not been funded, through a surcharge on the fees large frontier developers pay for IVO oversight, reserving capacity for independent safety and security research. The intended users would be researchers doing independent safety and security work, and the report leaves the surcharge level to the legislature. The report says it hopes to inform the legislature’s discussions as the legislature returns next month, and Unite.AI reported that the recommendations are intended to shape legislation when lawmakers return in December 2026.

Newsom said the federal government’s reckless failure to create any form of meaningful AI oversight or accountability should alarm every American. Government Operations Agency Secretary Nick Maduros said we don’t have to choose between safety and innovation. Expert-group member Rob Reich, a Stanford professor and former senior adviser to the US AI Safety Institute, said there is more oversight of the cafeteria offering sandwiches to employees at a frontier AI developer than of the AI models they design. Gillian Hadfield, a Johns Hopkins professor, said she was pleased the report recommends requiring developers to allow in expert independent evaluators responsible to the state and rapidly building a sector of independent verification organizations. The group also included Alondra Nelson of the Institute for Advanced Study and Jason Goldman, according to the governor’s office.

The report notes that Newsom signed SB 53, the first US law governing frontier AI development, a year ago, and that SB 813 and AB 1405 this autumn created a framework for IVOs and a registry of AI auditors. The report argues that the federal government has not acted, stating that no federal law requires AI companies to follow baseline safety or security standards, undergo independent testing or verification, or shut down their models if they threaten the public. It cites loss-of-control incidents, including an OpenAI incident involving Hugging Face this summer, as evidence that the evidence base has changed. Universities with evaluation, security or AI-safety groups are potential IVO or auditor candidates if the recommendations become law, which would raise questions for research offices about independence, conflicts of interest, confidentiality duties and licensing that the report says IVOs would carry. Institutions that collaborate with frontier developers should also note the whistleblower and incident-reporting proposals, which would extend protections to former employees and contractors.

The next step is legislative: the report says the legislature returns next month, and Unite.AI reported December 2026 as the date lawmakers return. Any bill would have to set the surcharge level, the licensing rules for IVOs and the thresholds for emergency orders, which the report leaves open. The Governor’s office also called on Congress and President Trump to adopt California’s framework or use it as a floor, not a ceiling. The report leaves the surcharge level to the legislature. The recommendations are not law.

stories.Headline: Turkish regulator imposes interim measures on Google over AI news licensing terms
stories.Summary:
The Turkish Competition Authority announced on 2 November 2026 that the Competition Board had opened an investigation into Google's "AI Overviews" and "AI Mode" features. The Board imposed interim measures on Google by a decision of 8 October 2026 under Article 9(4) of Law No 4054 on the Protection of Competition. The Board's concern is twofold: that Google discriminates among comparable news publishers when selecting and licensing their content for its AI features, and that the terms on which that content is used are unfair. AI Overviews and AI Mode went live in Türkiye on 18 February 2026. The Board opened a preliminary inquiry on 27 August, inspected Google's Turkish subsidiary on 1 September and decided, unanimously, on 8 October.

Google has three months to comply, with daily fines thereafter, and may seek judicial review in Ankara. Google's "search generative AI control", a Search Console setting that lets a site withhold its content from AI features without, on Google's account, affecting its ranking elsewhere, was announced on 3 June 2026, the day the CMA's conduct requirement was published. That setting was tested with UK sites first and reached all sites worldwide on 31 August 2026. Google's News AI pilot, announced on 10 December 2025 and said by Google to cover more than 400 publications by October 2026, pays selected publishers for enhanced content used to develop AI features. The global template contains a most-favoured-customer clause that the Turkish version omits.

The Board found a strong suspicion of two abuses under Article 6: discrimination among comparable publishers, both in the selection of sources for AI answers and in the offer and negotiation of contracts, and the imposition of unfair trading conditions. It noted that the same facts may serve both theories. Google must not discriminate among equivalent publishers on criteria that are not objective, transparent and pre-determined. Google must negotiate in good faith with publishers that seek a contract, on objective, verifiable and transparent criteria reflecting the scope and intensity of use, user engagement and the effect on traffic, visibility and advertising revenue. Google must not penalise in ranking, visibility, indexing or traffic a publisher that declines a contract or its terms.

Google must supply publishers periodically with verifiable data on how their content is used and what engagement and traffic it generates. Google must make the AI opt-out exercisable independently of visibility and indexing in other Google services. Google must not worsen existing contracts or apply divergent terms in new ones, and must report compliance to the Authority. On the Board's redacted figures, search engines account for a substantial share of Turkish news sites' traffic, highest for publishers with weaker brands, and Google's share of that search-referred traffic is consistently high. The Board concludes that Google is an unavoidable trading partner for news publishers.

The Board also records that AI referrals account for less than 0.01% of publishers' traffic. The Board found that tying a publisher's choice about AI use to its visibility in Search limited publishers' ability to refuse. The Board found that the opt-out arrived six and a half months after the features did. The Board found that the opt-out's existence does not settle the matter, since not using it is no evidence of a free choice where the consequences for ranking are not predictable. Examining the global template and the Turkish version, the Board found that Google alone decides which publishers are offered a contract, that the text is standard and non-negotiable, and that the fee is derived from brand value and third-party traffic data by an undisclosed method.

The Board found that the licence is worldwide, sublicensable and extends to training, that there is a single payment with no commitment to use the content or send traffic, and that attribution and linking are owed only "to the extent provided to similarly situated partners" and "where reasonably practicable". The Board observes that publishers signed quickly, which shows consent, not competitive terms. The Board derives the unfair-trading-conditions theory from the general prohibition in Article 6 of Law No 4054, noting that the examples listed in Article 6 are not exhaustive. The Board adopts, almost verbatim, the Commission's test from Apple Music Streaming: trading conditions are unfair where they are imposed by a dominant undertaking on its trading partners, harm the interests of those partners or of third parties, including consumers, and are not necessary to achieve a legitimate objective or go beyond what is necessary for it.

As in Apple, the Board adds that a finding of unfair conditions suffices and that no separate inquiry into a restriction of competition is required. The Board had said a few paragraphs earlier that competition-law intervention against unfair terms presupposes conduct that is not isolated and that produces appreciable "restrictive effects on the market". Article 9(4) permits interim measures that preserve the situation prior to the infringement, yet a duty to negotiate on value-reflecting criteria and to supply usage data creates obligations that did not previously exist. That is likely to be Google's first argument before the administrative court.

The Ankara 9th Administrative Court's Trendyol judgment states that an interim measure may neither punish the undertaking nor put complainants in a better position than before the alleged infringement, and may not substitute for the final decision. The court annulled the non-discrimination order for want of any analysis of whether the sellers concerned were in comparable situations. The Google decision cites that judgment for its standard of proof, not for its ceiling. More to follow.

stories.Headline: FBI warns hackers use Artex AI tool to breach networks in under three hours
stories.Summary:
The FBI warned that hackers are using an autonomous AI tool called Artex to launch cyberattacks globally and across the United States. These malicious actors have targeted various industries in recent months, including government, defense, tech, phone, internet companies, and law firms. The agency issued a flash cybersecurity advisory on November 13 to alert businesses and government organizations about these escalating AI-assisted threats. Cybercriminals and state-aligned groups have used this software to automate attacks and gain privileged network access in under three hours. The FBI says these intrusions have occurred since the tool first made its public debut in July of this year.

The framework requires connections to frontier large language models from OpenAI and Anthropic, as well as open-source or non-U.S. models. It targets security flaws like weak protections and stolen passwords to breach networks in South Korea and the United States. Hackers used Artex to access Microsoft 365 cloud environments of at least 2,250 customers of the IT company ConnectWise. In South Korea, the tool targeted financial institutions and stole the personal data of at least 68,000 people due to weak defenses. The tool also breached Barracuda by finding an exposed credential from a third-party vendor that the company had not revoked.

The FBI stated that AI makes sophisticated attacks faster and easier to automate, which makes them more difficult for organizations to detect. Federal investigators noted that Artex intrusions are noisy because they generate reams of traffic and data that trigger defensive alerts. The agency warned on X that the tool allows attackers with limited technical expertise to carry out complex, specialist operations. Barracuda's chief information security officer, Arve Kjoelen, said defenders relying on spotting activity often arrive after the attacker has finished. A spokesperson for ConnectWise did not respond to requests for comment regarding the claims made by the FBI.

Microsoft identified a China-aligned threat actor known as Storm-0940 as the group behind the Artex-assisted campaigns targeting hundreds of organizations. The breach at Barracuda affected stores of credentials used to collect data, though the company cannot rule out customer access. Victims include the financial industry in South Korea and customers of the IT management giant ConnectWise who suffered data theft. Other affected entities include the 178 organizations whose websites were hit by a separate supply-chain attack involving the platform Optimizely. This separate incident involved 188 compromised scripts that could potentially capture sensitive information entered by visitors to those various websites.

Artex was originally developed as an open-source penetration-testing platform designed to identify security weaknesses in applications and computer networks. The tool relies on rapidly scanning a victim's network for signs of weakness before exploiting simple bugs to gain a foothold. Recent reports of banking disruptions at Wells Fargo, Bank of America, and JPMorgan Chase were not linked to these cyberattacks. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin attributed those specific outages to ageing computer infrastructure rather than malicious activity from AI hacking tools. JPMorgan Chase blamed a software bug for its problems, while Microsoft attributed its own disruption to various server issues.

The developer of Artex made the software closed-source to prevent further attacks, but the FBI says the open-source version remains accessible. Researchers recently found hundreds of publicly exposed Artex systems online without passwords, including the system used to target South Korea. The FBI continues to warn that the tool's ability to automate reconnaissance presents a significant challenge for traditional cybersecurity defenses. It remains unclear how many customers were affected by the Barracuda breach because the company's logs were not detailed enough. The articles leave open whether other organizations have been compromised by the circulating open-source version of the Artex tool.

stories.Headline: TrendForce projects HBM4 prices will rise up to 2.7 times next year due to AI demand
stories.Summary:
Market research firm TrendForce projected on November 18, 2026, that prices for sixth-generation high-bandwidth memory, known as HBM4, will rise significantly next year. This increase is driven by the growing demand for artificial intelligence accelerators and a shift in production strategies by Samsung Electronics and SK hynix. The firm expects HBM4 prices to reach between $3 and $5.50 per gigabit in 2027, which is up to 2.7 times the 2026 price of $2.05 per gigabit. Additionally, the seventh-generation HBM4E is expected to cost more than $5 per gigabit, with clearer pricing arriving in the first half of 2027.

This price surge requires a shift in manufacturing, as Samsung Electronics, SK hynix, and Micron will increase HBM wafer input from 23 percent in 2026 to nearly 30 percent in 2027. Because HBM consumes three to four times more wafers than standard memory, PC DRAM bit supply is forecast to decline by 7.9 percent while HBM supply grows by 65.7 percent. Consequently, conventional DRAM prices are expected to rise 10 to 15 percent in the fourth quarter of 2026, followed by smaller quarterly gains throughout 2027. Meanwhile, China's CXMT may increase its DRAM capacity by 20 percent in 2027, though U.S. export controls on graphics processing units limit its current growth.

Senior researcher Ellie Wang stated that strong momentum should continue through 2027 because of expanding investments in artificial intelligence infrastructure. She noted that global cloud service providers will likely increase capital expenditure by 104 percent in 2026 and another 60 percent in 2027 to reach $1.5158 trillion. Wang explained that the market direction after 2028 will depend on the balance between demand and the opening of new production facilities. She suggested that memory prices might reach an inflection point around the middle of 2028 as the current boom potentially slows down.

The market may shift between 2028 and 2030 as new plants, including the Pyeongtaek P5 plant and the Yongin semiconductor cluster, begin operations. Samsung Electronics plans to build two phases of Pyeongtaek P5 with monthly capacities of 200,000 wafers each, while SK hynix intends to add 300,000 wafers per month at Yongin. These expansions will increase overall manufacturing capacity, though HBM shipment growth is projected to decelerate from 50 percent in 2027 to around 10 percent in 2028. CXMT also plans to add 100,000 to 200,000 wafers per month after 2028, which could further impact global supply.

stories.Headline: Treasury and White House officials consider requiring US firms to label use of Chinese AI models
stories.Summary:
The Treasury Department and White House science officials discussed requiring US companies to post website notices when using Chinese AI models. Reuters reported this plan on Wednesday, November 19, 2026, as a way to discourage reliance on these models. The proposal would label American adopters like Airbnb but would not impose new restrictions on Chinese developers. No formal rulemaking, text, deadline, or penalty has been announced or enacted by the government yet. The aim is to use reputational costs to name and shame companies that rely on Chinese AI.

The plan would require labels for companies like Airbnb, Anysphere, and DoorDash that use models from developers like Alibaba or Moonshot. House committees sent letters to Airbnb and Anysphere on April 29, and to DoorDash on July 31, 2026. DoorDash was asked for information by August 14 to reduce reliance on models developed in the PRC. Pinterest uses Qwen models for chatbots, and Anysphere's Cursor Composer 2 builds on the Kimi model from Moonshot AI. These labels would not show if data goes to China or if models run on US infrastructure.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent floated the disclosure idea in July and mentioned sanctioning Chinese firms that stole intellectual property. Michael Kratsios, confirmed March 25, 2025, directs the Office of Science and Technology Policy, which issued an April memo. House China Select Committee Chairman John Moolenaar welcomed the report, calling disclosure an important step in managing risks. Moolenaar warned that models hosted on US servers can still carry vulnerabilities that the adopter did not choose. He also sponsored the No Adversarial AI Act, H.R. 4142, which was introduced on June 25, 2025.

Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky said the company uses Alibaba's Qwen models for its customer service agent, which uses 13 models. Chesky stated in May 2026 that Airbnb does not buy from Alibaba or provide data to Chinese companies. Luma AI CEO Amit Jain told Semafor there was no evidence of change among companies using Chinese models. Booz Allen Hamilton found Qwen3-Coder added 130 percent more vulnerabilities under a US government persona than a neutral one. These findings affect US companies that use open-weight models to save money on infrastructure and development costs.

Yicai reported in September that seven Chinese models rank in the top 10 on OpenRouter by call volume. Epoch AI estimated in May that open-weight models lag closed models by about four months on average. Mozilla's September 15 report put the gap at 4.4 months, while other Chinese models trail by 14 months. Moonshot's Kimi K3 scored 57 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index but had a 51 percent hallucination rate.

China's 2017 National Intelligence Law requires organizations to cooperate with intelligence work, though some dispute its enforcement. The government must decide if mandatory labels constitute compelled speech under Zauderer v. Office of Disciplinary Counsel or NIFLA v. Becerra.

It remains unsettled whether a notice saying a product uses a Chinese model is factual or a political message. Companies may use ML-BOM standards like CycloneDX, ECMA-424, or SPDX, but these rely on free-text strings for lineage. The articles leave open whether the Treasury will move into formal rulemaking or keep the labels voluntary. It is unclear if the administration will pursue de facto bans on foreign open-source models in the future.

stories.Headline: Applied Materials posts record DRAM revenue and raises 2026 packaging growth outlook
stories.Summary:
Applied Materials is seeing growing demand tied to AI infrastructure, as chipmakers look to expand DRAM production and meet rising high-bandwidth memory requirements, according to a Zacks article published by Yahoo Finance on November 16, 2026. The company said most leading-edge DRAM fabs are running at full capacity. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, DRAM revenues within its Semiconductor Systems segment rose 52% year over year to a record level. Applied Materials also introduced enhanced Centura Prime epitaxy and Producer Avila 2 PECVD tools, which it says improve DRAM performance and enable higher-layer-count HBM. Management expects a sizable increase in DRAM revenues during the second half of 2026, keeping memory-related process spending central to the company's growth.

Applied Materials now expects advanced packaging revenues to grow more than 70% in 2026, up from its prior outlook of more than 50%. The company is extending its portfolio across HBM and 3D chiplet stacking with Nokota VMax 2 plating, Opta Quad CMP and two new eBeam systems for metrology and defect analysis. The article notes that the benefits depend on sustained customer capital spending, since memory remains a cyclical industry. The article states that Applied Materials' broad portfolio positions it to capture a larger share of customer spending while keeping competitors like Lam Research and Camtek at bay. Lam Research competes across deposition and etch technologies, including advanced atomic layer deposition systems, while Camtek focuses on inspection, metrology, advanced packaging and high-performance computing applications.

Applied Materials shares have climbed 44.2% year to date, outperforming the Zacks Computer and Technology sector and the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry, which appreciated 7% and 8.1% respectively. The stock trades at a price-to-sales multiple of 6.38X, above the industry's 3.01X, and carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Applied Materials' fiscal 2026 earnings indicates year-over-year growth of 42.4%, and the estimates have been revised upward in the past seven days. The article frames the memory demand trend as a likely tailwind for the company in 2026 and beyond, provided customer capital spending holds up.

stories.Headline: IEC proposes Total Contribution framework to assess AI data center sustainability
stories.Summary:
The International Electrotechnical Commission proposed a broader way to judge the sustainability of AI data centers, according to a report announced on November 17, 2026. The IEC issued its Clean Green Data Centres Strategic Position Paper and Leadership Briefing. The framework is called “Total Contribution.” It considers a facility’s environmental footprint alongside its relationship with the electricity grid, economic productivity and public services. The central idea is that a data center should be assessed as part of a wider system.

The IEC established a Strategic Standards Group on Data Centres to develop consistent metrics, reporting protocols and assurance mechanisms. The announcement does not establish a completed global scoring formula or a binding requirement that every data center adopt zero-water cooling. Power Usage Effectiveness measures total facility energy divided by the energy used by IT equipment. A PUE of 1.2 means the facility consumes 20% more energy than its IT equipment alone. The IEC already publishes ISO/IEC 30134-2:2026, which defines PUE and its measurement, calculation and reporting.

The IEC organizes the proposed framework around four connected dimensions. Energy and grid integration covers demand response, support for grid resilience, and the integration of on-site or new renewable generation. Environmental and resource stewardship covers energy consumption, water use, carbon emissions, circularity, advanced cooling and waste heat recovery. Economic and digital productivity covers the relationship between resource consumption and contributions such as AI-enabled productivity, digital transformation and skilled employment. Societal and regional resilience covers support for healthcare, communications, government and other critical services, together with regional development.

In an earlier IEC contribution to ITU’s AI for Good platform, the organization described the forthcoming paper as a way to identify sustainability and safety gaps in standardization. The IEA’s Powering Artificial Intelligence report says active management of computing loads remains rare. Many operators serve third parties and have limited visibility into or control over the work running inside their facilities. The IEA identifies standardized information exchange across computing customers, infrastructure providers and electricity networks as important to unlocking flexibility. The IEC’s announcement highlights liquid and immersion cooling, direct-current power distribution and power quality for AI infrastructure as areas for standards development.

The U.S. Department of Energy’s data center water-efficiency guidance illustrates a liquid-cooled system that ultimately transfers heat to a cooling tower. Liquid cooling does not by itself establish that a facility consumes no water. A closed equipment loop can coexist with evaporative heat rejection elsewhere in the system. The IEC emphasized treating data centers as active participants in energy systems and examining cooling, water use, electronic waste and lifecycle emissions. A large facility with an excellent PUE can still place substantial demand on a constrained grid.

The next phase will determine how the proposed framework becomes consistent reporting and assurance that operators, utilities and policymakers can use. The report’s ambition is to make those relationships visible. Turning that ambition into comparable, verifiable outcomes is the work ahead. The difficult next step is making the four dimensions comparable. A credible assessment needs to show where impacts occur, who receives the benefits and how claims are measured.

stories.Headline: TrendForce predicts HBM4 memory prices will rise to between $3 and $5.50 per gigabit in 2027
stories.Summary:
TrendForce forecast memory price changes during its Roadshow Korea in Seoul on November 18, 2026. The firm predicted that sixth generation HBM4 memory prices will rise significantly next year. These costs will increase from $2.05 per gigabit in 2026 to a new range. The expected 2027 price band is between $3 and $5.50 per gigabit. This represents a price gain of about 46% to 168%.

HBM4E prices should exceed $5 per gigabit with terms set in early 2027. General DRAM contract prices will rise 10% to 15% in late 2026. These gains narrow to 0% to 5% by the second half of 2027. HBM will use 30% of DRAM wafer input in 2027, up from 23%. HBM4 doubled the interface to 2,048 bits, according to the provided reports.

TrendForce stated that 8-high HBM stacks carry a 10% to 20% per-gigabit premium. They explained that base die costs do not shrink as DRAM layers increase. SK hynix CEO Kwak Noh-jung told Reuters that 2027 would be the worst supply year. Micron said 75% of fiscal 2027 volume is committed at prices above 2026 levels. Samsung reportedly seeks a mid-to-high $4 range per gigabit for HBM4.

GPU and ASIC makers are considering less HBM per device because supply is scarce. IDC projects PC shipments will fall 11.3% in 2026 with no relief through 2027. A June 25 class action alleges HBM is a pretext to restrict older chips. This lawsuit was filed in the Northern District of California under the Sherman Act. Cloud giants face higher memory costs, which Nvidia uses to justify server price hikes.

HBM bits consume three to four times the wafer area of conventional DRAM bits. One 12-high HBM4 stack from Micron holds 36 GB, which equals 288 gigabits. Nvidia's Vera Rubin accelerator uses eight such stacks for a total of 2,304 gigabits. China's CXMT and YMTC appear on the Pentagon's Section 1260H list of military companies. YMTC has been on the U.S. Entity List since December 2022.

New DRAM capacity will begin ramping in the second half of 2027. Substantial output contributions from this new capacity are not expected until 2028. NAND supply sufficiency is forecast to turn positive in 2027 as new capacity arrives. Enterprise SSD price growth is expected to accelerate in the fourth quarter of 2026. The articles leave open whether Samsung will confirm individual 2027 contract price terms.

stories.Headline: AMD data center revenue jumps 97% as Google Cloud deploys Epyc chips for TPU systems
stories.Summary:
The Motley Fool published an article on November 15, 2026, by Harsh Chauhan, arguing that Advanced Micro Devices could be the best artificial intelligence stock to buy amid a sell-off. The PHLX Semiconductor Sector index had declined 12% over the past three months, and AMD was caught up in that vortex with significant volatility. Concerns about the sustainability of artificial intelligence infrastructure spending, which has been key to the semiconductor sector's growth, drove the weakness. AMD's stock fell $51.24, or 8.75%, to $534.06 as of 4:00 PM ET on 11/13/26 on the NASDAQ. The article said the recent weakness opened a great opportunity for investors to buy a top stock at an attractive valuation.

AMD's data center revenue jumped 97% year over year in Q3 to $8.5 billion, driven by tremendous demand for its Epyc server central processing units from hyperscalers and AI companies. Alphabet's Google Cloud division expanded its partnership with AMD to deploy its 5th-generation Epyc server CPUs, security fabric, and x86 software to power its cloud Tensor Processing Unit systems. AMD Epyc will serve as the foundation for Google's TPUs, allowing users to run inference applications. Google Cloud reported a backlog of $561 billion at the end of the third quarter, and the tech giant expects to recognize half of that backlog in the next two years. AMD expects revenue to increase by more than 80% in 2027, fueled by healthy growth in the data center business, where it sees the server CPU total addressable market jump to $220 billion by 2030.

The article's author, Harsh Chauhan, wrote that he would not be surprised to see AMD embark on a stunning long-term rally. He said AMD is emerging as one of the most important players in the AI chip ecosystem. He noted that AMD has partnerships with major hyperscalers and AI companies, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta Platforms, Microsoft, and others, in the data center segment. He wrote that these customers should ensure solid long-term revenue growth for AMD, which is precisely what analysts are expecting. Chauhan disclosed that he has no position in any of the stocks mentioned.

The Motley Fool has positions in and recommends Advanced Micro Devices, Alphabet, Meta Platforms, and Microsoft. The article said the $52.2 billion revenue estimate for 2026 points to a 51% jump over last year, and the forecast for 2027 and 2028 is also quite solid. Analysts expect AMD's EPS to grow by nearly 70% annually over the long run, and AMD trades at 33 times forward earnings. Assuming AMD clocks even 50% earnings growth in 2029 and 2030, its EPS could reach $57.53 by the end of the decade, using 2028's projected EPS of $25.57 as the base. A price-to-earnings ratio of 20 at that time, in line with the tech-focused Nasdaq-100 index's forward P/E, would send AMD's shares to $1,150 in just over four years, twice AMD's current price.

The article noted that the past few months haven't been pretty for semiconductor stocks, as evidenced by the 12% decline in the PHLX Semiconductor Sector index over the past three months. It said AMD's data center segment has incredible room for growth and that Alphabet is poised to spend aggressively on its cloud computing infrastructure. The article stated that AMD is therefore going to be a direct beneficiary of Alphabet's enormous spending. It said AMD is well-positioned to capitalize on the massive server CPU opportunity. The article added that AMD's revenue growth will filter down to the bottom line as well.

The article said opportunistic investors should capitalize on the recent weakness in the semiconductor sector and buy the stock for long-term gains. It said the Motley Fool Stock Advisor analyst team just identified what they believe are the 10 best stocks for investors to buy now, and Advanced Micro Devices wasn't one of them. The article cited Netflix making that list on December 17, 2004, when $1,000 invested would now be worth $335,171. It also cited Nvidia making the list on April 15, 2005, when $1,000 invested would now be worth $1,000,640. The article said Stock Advisor's total average return is 823%, compared to 208% for the S&P 500, with returns as of November 15, 2026.

stories.Headline: Linq raises $90 million led by Andreessen Horowitz to build AI agent infrastructure
stories.Summary:
Linq, an infrastructure platform for AI agents based in San Francisco, announced on November 18, 2026 that it has raised $90 million in new funding led by Andreessen Horowitz, with continued participation from TQ Ventures, Mucker Capital, and Abstract, and new participation from Anthos and Left Lane Capital. Ben Horowitz, cofounder and general partner at Andreessen Horowitz, will join Linq's board of directors. The company was founded by Elliott Potter, who serves as CEO, Patrick Sullivan, who serves as CTO, and Jared Mattsson, who serves as President. Linq said its messaging product has already processed more than 1 billion messages, and it counts DoorDash, Town, Tomo, and hundreds of other companies as providers. The funding will support continued investment in messaging and the expansion of Linq's product lineup through its own software, hardware infrastructure, and strategic partnerships.

Linq's computer use offering gives agents access to physical computing infrastructure to interact with software and complete tasks, and HD Calling for Agents adds voice calling to the platform. As an Apple Messaging Service Provider, Linq can help more enterprises launch and scale customer-facing agents on the same channel. The company cited Cloudflare reporting that more than half of internet traffic is no longer human, with AI agent requests on its network up more than 1,700% in a year. Horowitz said agents will communicate and get work done just like people do, and that Linq gives agents the infrastructure to do both at scale. Potter said clicking through five screens to make a payment will become two words to an agent, pay rent, and that Linq helps developers build customer-facing agents that use human tools to do human work.

Aryan Shah, Head of AI research at DoorDash, said the best AI experiences fit naturally into people's lives, and that Linq gives DoorDash the messaging infrastructure to bring ordering into a familiar conversation so customers can go from deciding what they want to placing an order in one thread. Linq describes itself as the platform for building AI agents, bringing together messaging and an expanding set of tools for interacting with the world, helping developers spend less time assembling infrastructure and more time building products. The company said messaging was its first product and remains a core part of its growing AI infrastructure platform. The announcement framed the shift as one in which people will describe what they need and agents will get it done, following the internet giving every business a website and the iPhone giving every business an app. Companies can learn more at linqapp.com.

stories.Headline: Redbox joins NVIDIA Inception to speed AI analysis of menstrual blood data for health and drug discovery
stories.Summary:
Redbox Co., Ltd., the company behind the bio-intelligence business of the NPO Red Box Japan, announced on November 19, 2026, that it had joined the NVIDIA Inception Program, a global startup support program run by NVIDIA Corporation for companies working on advanced technologies such as AI and data science. The announcement said the participation would let the company use NVIDIA's ecosystem to speed up research and development that analyzes biological data, including menstrual blood, with AI. Redbox said it aims to build the data it has accumulated into a foundation for extending healthy life expectancy by ten years, and to use it in ways that also help drug discovery research. The program gives participating startups access to NVIDIA's technical knowledge and training, preferential treatment for hardware and software, and networks with investors and partner companies.

Redbox works on bio-intelligence research and development that comprehensively analyzes biological data, including menstrual blood, starting from support for access to sanitary products. The company said menstruation is a valuable source of information that periodically reflects conditions inside a woman's body, and that large-scale data processing and the use of AI technology are essential to analyze such data at a high level and help each person understand her own health. Through the participation, Redbox said it will build a data analysis infrastructure using GPUs and set up a structure to develop and verify AI models more efficiently. Under the NVIDIA ecosystem, the company plans to build foundation data for extending healthy life expectancy by ten years by analyzing biological data obtained continuously along the menstrual cycle with AI, so that changes in the body and signs of future health risks can be captured.

Redbox also plans to combine its real-world data with AI drug discovery, a field in which the use of AI for protein structure prediction and molecular design has advanced rapidly and shown the potential to greatly shorten the time and cost of finding drug candidates. The company said that improving the accuracy of such AI models and connecting them to medicines that reach actual patients requires biological data obtained in daily life, and that it accumulates data gained continuously along the menstrual cycle as its own real-world data. By combining this data with AI drug discovery technology, Redbox aims to contribute to the search for drug targets and the development of new treatments and medicines in the field of women's health, where research data has been insufficient. It said it will also use the same data and AI analysis technology in supplement development, reading nutritional trends linked to the menstrual cycle and changes in physical condition and developing supplements based on scientific evidence for each person's condition.

Representative Ryoichi Oguma said the company will use the Inception Program to further accelerate the bio-intelligence research and development built on its own real-world data, including menstrual blood, and the analysis of that data. He said Redbox will act not merely as a provider of data and technology but as a partner that creates practical value in both society and business together with research institutions, pharmaceutical companies and partner companies. He said the company will work on a foundation model of multimodal AI that integrates biological data, physical condition records and life logs, a data infrastructure in a secure sovereign environment that takes privacy into account, and a user experience that lets each person understand her own body and turn that understanding into action. Through these efforts, he said, Redbox aims to contribute to AI drug discovery and supplement development and to realize a society that extends healthy life expectancy by ten years.

REDBOX BIO is a next-generation bio-intelligence service that combines and analyzes three kinds of biological data: menstrual blood, blood and facial stratum corneum, or ceramide, to understand each person's body from multiple angles. By continuously accumulating and learning biomarkers such as proteins, metabolites, hormone rhythms and skin lipids, it aims to provide personalized health management in which understanding of one's body deepens as data increases, rather than ending with a single test. The service is set to cover a wide range from athletes' conditioning to beauty, daily performance and longevity, and a women-only model called Model X is scheduled to be provided in 2027. Redbox said it will continue to deepen cooperation with companies, local governments, educational institutions and research institutions, and to use NVIDIA's ecosystem while advancing the building of a data foundation for extending healthy life expectancy, AI drug discovery and supplement development, as well as healthcare services that let each person understand her own body and manage her health proactively.

stories.Headline: Okta Korea's Hwang Kyu-eon says AI agents drive record enterprise revenue and a push into banking
stories.Summary:
Okta expanded its enterprise business in South Korea recently to address rising hacking threats and the spread of artificial intelligence agents. Hwang Kyu-eon, the country manager of Okta Korea, discussed these developments on November 19 at a press briefing. This event took place ahead of the Oktane on the Road Seoul conference held at Hotel Eliena in Seoul's Gangnam district. The company is seeing a surge in demand for unified security solutions as corporations manage more accounts and access privileges. This growth has led to the highest revenue recorded since the Korean unit was first established.

The company plans to focus on winning commercial banks and other financial sector clients starting in the next year. Okta already provides security solutions to some financial firms and has applied its technology to an internet only bank's internal network. To support this expansion, the company intends to add finance specialists to its team during the coming year. The business requires the easing of regulatory constraints regarding the use of software as a service within internal financial networks. These specific changes are necessary because current rules limit how the company can apply its software in those environments.

Hwang Kyu-eon stated that domestic enterprise revenue overtook the commercial segment starting last year as large corporations adopted the solutions. He noted that domestic revenue grew by double digits this year, which is a rate that outpaces the company's global growth. Hwang explained that a few departments at large companies typically use the solution first before expanding it across the organization. He argued that stitching together individual security solutions creates fragmented visibility, which becomes a security threat for the company. He also mentioned that the company must now monitor abnormal behavior after login because attackers often hijack sessions.

Large corporations and financial firms are affected by the need to manage identities and credentials that serve as primary attack paths. Companies find it difficult to manage accounts consistently when they operate multiple separate security solutions across their different internal systems. For example, access privileges may remain on some systems even after an employee leaves the company or changes their department. This lack of coordination means that abnormal behavior detected on one system might not trigger an immediate block on others. Consequently, systems that can quickly trace an intruder's actions and cut off access have become more important for these firms.

The growth is driven by three shifts, including the addition of AI agents to employees and existing corporate systems. These AI agents increase the number of accounts and access privileges that a company must manage to remain secure. In April of this year, Okta launched Okta for AI Agents to detect unidentified agents and manage their activity. In September, the company launched the Blueprint Alliance with Zscaler, CrowdStrike, and Amazon Web Services to share security warning signs. This alliance allows participating global firms to coordinate responses, such as blocking access, across their linked security systems.

Okta Korea will use the Oktane on the Road Seoul event to present its unified security strategy for the AI era. The company will discuss specific solutions to the security challenges that companies face as they multiply their AI agents. They will continue to target the financial sector while hoping for regulatory changes to allow broader software as a service use. The articles leave open whether the Korean government will actually ease the regulatory constraints on financial internal networks. It remains unclear how many new commercial banks will adopt the technology in the coming year.

stories.Headline: Anthropic raises 81.3 billion dollars in record IPO as employees debate AI safety pace
stories.Summary:
The artificial intelligence company Anthropic completed a record breaking initial public offering on Wednesday, November 18, 2026. This financial event raised more than 81.3 billion dollars due to strong demand for AI technology. The company sold over 956 million shares at a price of 83 dollars per share. Certain stockholders also sold more than 23 million shares to reach the final total. Shares began trading publicly on Thursday on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT.

This offering exceeded the original prospectus target of 825 million shares priced between 70 and 78 dollars. The company raised approximately 79.4 billion dollars through the offering, which surpassed the 75 billion dollar haul of SpaceX earlier this year. Anthropic intends to use this new cash as a priority to purchase more compute power. This investment aims to help the company reach recursive self improvement before its rivals do. Such a breakthrough involves current AI models autonomously building the next generation of technology.

Chief executive Dario Amodei participated in a high energy investor roadshow featuring music by producer Fred Again. However, employees known as Ants expressed muted enthusiasm and concerns about the speed of AI development. Co founder Jack Clark and the AI Futures Project now anticipate superhuman AI researchers arriving in 2027. These individuals are debating how leading labs can cooperate to slow model development for safety. They worry that models capable of building their own successors might eventually escape human control.

The listing remained oversubscribed despite general market volatility and growing concerns regarding a possible AI bubble. Many employees are preoccupied with recent rogue agent episodes that have made the industry feel more dangerous. They believe the most difficult part of their work is only just beginning. The company has transitioned from a scrappy start up into one of the most valuable firms globally. Future efforts will focus on the race toward autonomous AI development and safety.

stories.Headline: Microsoft launches Cobalt 200 AI servers as agent workloads demand far more computing
stories.Summary:
Microsoft formally launched servers equipped with the Cobalt 200 on November 17, which is an in-house central processing unit for artificial intelligence. This move follows the development of the Maia custom processor series intended to replace graphics processing units from Nvidia and AMD. The company is responding to a surge in demand for central processing units as the market shifts from chatbots to autonomous agents. These agents act as assistants that carry out tasks on their own rather than just generating text.

This transition requires significantly more infrastructure and processing capacity because agent-based workloads operate autonomously to generate outputs. Alistair Speirs, the general manager of Azure infrastructure at Microsoft, noted that developers can consume up to 3,000 times more computing resources than existing chatbots or the generative Copilot. He explained that this level of capacity cannot be built immediately because it would require several times the size of existing data centers. Even utilizing every high-performance chip in the world would not make such a scale achievable right now.

Alistair Speirs stated that the shift toward agentic AI makes inference more important, which increases the standing of central processing units. While graphics processing units were central to the generative AI era due to machine learning, the new era relies more on the brain-like functions of the CPU. Other companies have also entered this space, with users turning to personal agents like Anthropic's Claude Duet, OpenAI's Dots, and Meta's Muse. These tools have been used in earnest by various companies since last year.

stories.Headline: MangoBoost and PFN sign AI inference infrastructure agreement and plan AI Token Factory proof of concept
stories.Summary:
MangoBoost and Preferred Networks, also known as PFN, signed a memorandum of understanding on November 18 to collaborate on artificial intelligence inference infrastructure technologies. The two companies intend to conduct a proof of concept for a next-generation architecture called the AI Token Factory. This partnership aims to increase AI inference throughput and reduce latency to improve overall system utilization. An official signing ceremony for this agreement will take place at the SC26 supercomputing conference in Chicago between November 15 and November 20.

The proposed heterogeneous computing system combines MangoBoost data processing units and storage solutions with PFN MN-Core AI inference processors and AMD graphics processing units. AMD GPUs will manage the prefill stage for processing input instructions, while PFN chips will handle the decode stage to generate tokens. MangoBoost will provide key-value cache pooling storage and prefill-decode disaggregation solutions to optimize data transfers and memory management. These specialized data processing units are designed to handle communications, security processing, and storage input and output within the AI infrastructure.

Jangwoo Kim, the CEO of MangoBoost, and Takahiro Ogura, a division head at PFN, are leading this collaborative effort to optimize computing resources and networking. The companies stated that they will first validate the new architecture within a simulation environment to test its effectiveness. Once samples of the MN-Core L1000 chip are available, the partners will expand their testing to include performance validation on actual hardware. They also plan to consider publishing a joint research paper based on the results of these evaluations.

stories.Headline: Apacer wins Taiwan Excellence Award for BiCLO AI accelerator powered by DEEPX chips
stories.Summary:
The Taiwanese company Apacer developed an edge artificial intelligence accelerator card called BiCLO that won a 2027 Taiwan Excellence Award. This achievement was announced by the fabless semiconductor company DEEPX on November 18, 2026, regarding the recognized hardware. The award winning device utilizes specialized neural processing units to enhance computing capabilities at the edge of a network. This specific recognition comes from a comprehensive evaluation of research, design, quality, and marketing conducted by the Ministry of Economic Affairs in Taiwan. The BiCLO accelerator card incorporates two DX-M1M neural processing units and utilizes a standard PCI Express interface for connectivity.

Each individual chip provides 25 trillion operations per second of AI computing performance while utilizing 2GB of SRAM. The total system delivers 50 TOPS of computing performance while maintaining a low power consumption of approximately 10 watts. Because each chip consumes about 5 watts, the device can process dozens of video streams, such as CCTV feeds, without any latency. This architecture allows for real-time processing and storage at the edge to reduce the risk of leaking information to external cloud servers. DEEPX is the entity responsible for developing the neural processing units that power the award winning BiCLO accelerator card.

The company stated that the hardware is designed to perform inference on multiple video streams simultaneously to improve efficiency. They highlighted that the technology is particularly useful for applications in smart cities, transportation systems, and various manufacturing facilities. By keeping data processing local, the system avoids the security vulnerabilities associated with transmitting sensitive information over a network. The company believes this approach provides a more secure alternative to traditional cloud based AI processing. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Supergate signs MOU with FPT Semiconductor to cooperate on AI chips and packaging in Vietnam
stories.Summary:
South Korean fabless semiconductor company Supergate signed a memorandum of understanding with Vietnam's FPT Semiconductor on November 18 to cooperate in the artificial intelligence semiconductor business. This partnership was established in connection with the Vietnam, Korea AI and Semiconductor Summit 2026, which took place in Hanoi on November 12. The two companies intend to explore various cooperation opportunities involving semiconductor testing and packaging, cloud services, and vision AI solutions. They will initially focus on handling the testing and packaging of Supergate products within Vietnam.

The agreement requires the companies to jointly explore the local development and commercialization of Supergate's AI system-on-module products. These embedded computing modules integrate processors, memory, and power management onto a single compact circuit board. The partners will also discuss engineering cooperation regarding software integration and AI chip design at the Offshore Development Center of FPT. Furthermore, they will evaluate the technical feasibility of deploying the Tess C100 data center chip developed by Supergate into the cloud infrastructure of FPT.

Employees from both Supergate and FPT will work together at the same location to facilitate this collaboration. The companies will conduct joint testing of AI chips, cloud platforms, and system-on-modules while verifying interoperability and API integration. They also plan to consider joint sales, customer acquisition, and cross-marketing efforts to expand their respective markets. Specific implementation terms and business areas will be determined through separate agreements and subsequent discussions between the two parties.

stories.Headline: Samsung Electro-Mechanics expands Nvidia partnership to add AI capacitors
stories.Summary:
Samsung Electro-Mechanics announced on November 18, 2026, that it is expanding its existing partnership with Nvidia to include multilayer ceramic capacitors. This new cooperation follows a strategic agreement made one month prior to supply package substrates for artificial intelligence chips. The company intends to provide high-reliability capacitors that stabilize voltage for AI accelerators and other high-performance semiconductors. These components will be produced alongside substrates for data center networking systems and high-performance computing platforms.

The agreement requires the expansion of dedicated production infrastructure at the Sejong and Busan plants in South Korea. Nvidia is currently considering providing additional financial support to fund these facility upgrades. Samsung Electro-Mechanics aims to establish a full-scale mass production system by 2029 to meet global demand. The technical focus will involve improving production line efficiency, maintaining quality control, and supporting ultra-fine circuit patterns.

President and CEO Chang Duck-hyun stated that the company will combine its fine-pattern substrate technology with high-reliability capacitor capabilities. He expressed the goal of becoming a total solutions provider that meets the performance and quality requirements of Nvidia. Debora Shoquist, the executive vice president of operations at Nvidia, noted that global supply chain collaboration is essential for AI infrastructure. She added that this cooperation supports the expanded production of next-generation accelerated computing platforms.

stories.Headline: AMD MI455X GPU outperforms Nvidia Vera Rubin by 30 percent in token throughput benchmarks
stories.Summary:
AMD disclosed the artificial intelligence computing performance of its latest Instinct server graphics processing units on November 12. The company revealed that the MI455X GPU, which is used in the Helios system, achieved a throughput of 21,333 tokens per second per GPU. This result was recorded while running the DeepSeek-R1 model during an offline AI inference benchmark conducted by MLPerf. This performance was 30 percent higher than the results released on November 11 for the Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 server rack.

The Helios system houses 72 Instinct MI455X GPUs with a combined 31 terabytes of HBM4 capacity and memory bandwidth reaching 1.7 petabytes per second. Its scale-up bandwidth reaches 260 terabytes per second, while the MI455X offers up to 20 percent higher high-bandwidth memory bandwidth than the Rubin GPU. AMD also introduced the cost-optimized MI450X with 288 gigabytes of HBM4 memory per GPU and the MI430X for scientific research. The MI430X features 432 gigabytes of HBM4 memory, a maximum memory bandwidth of 23.3 terabytes per second, and native support for 64-bit double-precision floating-point calculations.

AMD representatives stated that the inference performance advantage of the MI455X stems from differences in system data bandwidth. They noted that the GPU-to-GPU scale-up bandwidth is higher than that of the Nvidia Vera Rubin. Regarding the MI430X, the company explained that the accuracy of many precision simulations and scientific calculations depends on native hardware FP64 computing performance. To support this claim, AMD analyzed 47 workloads across 11 different scientific computing applications and benchmarks.

stories.Headline: Sources expect Anthropic to allocate under 20% of its IPO shares to retail investors
stories.Summary:
Sources expect Anthropic's allocation of shares for retail investors in its blockbuster initial public offering to fall below 20 percent, according to the Financial Times. Retail buyers have historically received between 5 percent and 10 percent of the shares in large initial public offerings. The report, published on 19 November 2026, cites people described as sources for the expected allocation figure. The article itself sits behind a subscription paywall, so the full details of the offering are not available in the text provided.

The expected allocation matters because it would set the share of the offering that ordinary investors could buy rather than institutions. The historical range of 5 percent to 10 percent for large listings gives a benchmark against which the expected Anthropic figure can be compared. The report does not give the total size of the offering, the price of the shares or the date on which trading would begin. It also does not name the banks or advisers working on the transaction.

The sources cited by the Financial Times are responsible for the expected allocation figure, and the article attributes the expectation to them rather than to Anthropic itself. The report does not include any statement from Anthropic or from any underwriter about how the shares would be divided. No named executive or official is quoted in the available text. The article carries no comment from the company on the expected retail share.

The context is that retail investors have historically received a small slice of large initial public offerings, at 5 percent to 10 percent of the shares. The report does not say what happens next, such as when the allocation would be confirmed or when the shares would list. It also does not say whether the expected figure could change before the offering is completed. More detail may emerge as the transaction proceeds.

stories.Headline: SK Hynix orders HBM4 packaging equipment for Cheongju lines targeting 2027 output
stories.Summary:
South Korea's SK Hynix is preparing to expand its HBM4 production capacity by ordering new back-end equipment. The company began coordinating these purchase orders with its suppliers around November 15, 2026. This expansion focuses on adding new lines for packaging and testing. The company aims to have these new production lines fully operational in the first half of 2027. Some specific equipment items are requested for delivery by the first quarter of next year.

The expansion uses the Cheongju P&T6 fab in North Chungcheong Province, which was formerly called the M8 facility. This site was designated as an HBM production base in 2025, with lines built since early 2026. The company is procuring back-end process equipment for bonding, dicing, cutting, and inspection. Full capacity at this facility could add more than 20,000 HBM wafers per month. This move allows the company to secure more HBM4 output than originally planned.

An SK Hynix official stated the company continues placing equipment orders according to its plans. The official added that the company will respond to market expansion without any disruption. During a third-quarter earnings briefing, the company said DRAM and HBM volumes are sold out through 2029. These statements reflect a judgment that demand for high-bandwidth memory remains solid. The company believes this demand persists despite recent uncertainty in the AI semiconductor industry.

Equipment makers expect to benefit from these large-scale orders as HBM market growth begins in earnest. Industry insiders note that alternative demand sources like AMD and Broadcom remain strong for these chips. The expansion is aided by Nvidia lowering the HBM4 bandwidth target for its Vera Rubin chip. This decision reduced the process burden on manufacturers by adopting a speed that is easier to implement. These changes affect the supply chain strategy for next-generation AI semiconductor components.

The AI industry recently faced uncertainty after Jensen Huang resigned as the chief executive officer of Nvidia. Nvidia appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as the interim CEO to lead the company. The company stated it will maintain existing product development schedules and all current customer contracts. This background explains why the market is monitoring the new management's investment and procurement plans. The industry is watching for a new supply chain strategy from the interim leadership.

The market is watching Nvidia's quarterly earnings announcement scheduled for November 17 to see new procurement plans. This event may reveal if the new management changes its investment or supply chain strategy. Such changes remain a variable in future negotiations regarding the supply of HBM4 memory. The articles leave open whether the interim CEO will alter existing semiconductor procurement strategies. It remains unclear how the successor selection process will impact long-term AI chip investments.

stories.Headline: InMobi launches AI platform to manage advertising campaigns for small businesses
stories.Summary:
On November 18, 2026, InMobi launched a platform called InMobi Accelerate to help small and medium businesses. This new tool uses seven AI agents to plan, build, launch and measure advertising campaigns for users. The company released the announcement from San Mateo, California, at 7:00 AM Eastern time on that day. It targets small firms and the agencies that serve them to manage ads from one single dashboard. The platform is available at accelerate.inmobi.com and InMobi states that it is free to start.

The tool manages ads on Google Ads, Meta Ads, Microsoft Advertising, TikTok Ads and ChatGPT Ads. Seven agents act as a business analyst, audience strategist, media planner, copywriter, creative designer, launch engineer and optimizer. It uses a first-party pixel and universal conversion tracking to report a single figure called True ROAS. This data feeds Mobius, a decisioning system unveiled on October 5 that processes 25 trillion daily predictions. The system evaluates over 200 billion advertising opportunities each day to forecast options against desired advertiser outcomes.

Rohit Dosi, the VP and GM of InMobi Accelerate, said that AI agents change the economics of expertise. He stated that growing businesses should run disciplined programs without hiring seven specialists and agencies should take more clients. InMobi claims that assembling reports from different platforms into one picture is slow work that is difficult to get right. The company says the platform allows businesses to grow without standing up a large in-house marketing function. They describe Accelerate as a self-serve agentic AI advertising platform for planning and measuring campaigns.

InMobi says that 70 percent or more of 800 US small advertisers run campaigns on two or more platforms. A survey by NewtonX in May 2026 found that only 4 percent can launch a campaign the same day. Another StackAdapt survey of 885 senior marketers found that only 7 percent run fully unified measurement across their brands. Many advertisers are affected by single-publisher attribution, where multiple platforms claim the same sale for one single conversion. This structure creates silos that 42 percent of senior marketers say waste over a fifth of programmatic budgets.

The platform was introduced at Glance Forward in New York to examine how AI changes how consumers buy products. OpenAI opened ChatGPT Ads Manager to all US businesses on May 5 and expanded to 89 countries by October 21. Over 100,000 advertisers have run campaigns on ChatGPT since its launch, which includes cost-per-click bidding for all users. InMobi's Mobius system previously reached 8.6 million Grocery Outlet shoppers over a 12-day campaign to prove its scale. The company also plans an integration with Glance, which it describes as an AI-powered personal shopping tool.

Users must approve every plan, creative asset and budget before any advertising goes live on the connected platforms. Continuous optimization only runs if the advertiser authorizes it and sets specific parameters for the AI to follow. The articles leave open which specific parameters can be set, if budget caps exist, or if changes are logged. It is unclear how sales are credited when multiple platforms touch them or which lookback windows the system applies. The announcement does not name an independent auditor or measurement partner to verify the reported True ROAS figures.
