stories.Headline: Nvidia shares rise after third quarter results and revenue forecast beat analyst estimates
stories.Summary:
Nvidia shares rose 3 percent in premarket trading on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, after the company reported strong third-quarter results. The chipmaker saw its quarterly revenue and profit more than double compared to the previous year, which helped ease investor concerns regarding leadership turmoil. This positive financial news also lifted the sentiment for other artificial intelligence stocks as investors weighed the ongoing demand for infrastructure. For the third quarter of fiscal 2027, Nvidia reported revenue of 115.8 billion dollars and a net profit of 65.3 billion dollars. These figures represent a significant increase from the 57 billion dollars in revenue and 31.9 billion dollars in profit recorded a year earlier.

The company issued a fourth-quarter revenue forecast of approximately 130 billion dollars, which exceeded the 125.3 billion dollars expected by analysts. Additionally, the firm projected a gross margin of about 71.5 percent to signal continued business strength. The financial announcement occurred as chief executive Jensen Huang resigned immediately following allegations regarding personal relationships with a woman suspected of having links to China. The board unanimously accepted his resignation and appointed chief financial officer Colette Kress as the interim chief executive, while Harvey Jones became the first board chairman. Kress attempted to reassure the market by stating that business operations would continue as usual despite the transition.

The company has since hired Heidrick and Struggles to help find a permanent replacement for the chief executive role. This leadership change happens while Nvidia remains central to the global investment cycle for artificial intelligence technology. Other related stocks like AMD, Broadcom, and Micron also gained value, while infrastructure firms such as CoreWeave and Nebius saw their shares rise. Investors are now monitoring a potential initial public offering for Anthropic, which could be valued at 1.4 trillion dollars. This upcoming listing will serve as another test of whether high valuations in the sector are supported by long-term demand.

stories.Headline: Meta spends 78 cents of each cash dollar on AI as stock falls 21% from its high
stories.Summary:
Meta closed at $616.38 on Wednesday, 21% below its highest close of the past year of $777.59, reached on Sep 24, Trefis reported on November 19th, 2026. Meta’s ads business keeps growing, and analysts expect earnings of $34.14 a share next year, up from $29.09 this year. The size of its AI bill is holding the stock back, and unlike Amazon, Microsoft or Alphabet, Meta has no cloud business to rent that computing power to others. Meta is one of five tests for the AI trade in the Trefis series, each with a date to watch. The series starts with What 1 Big Trigger Could Make Nvidia Stock Jump By Dec 31?

Meta’s capital spending was $104.4 billion over the last year, up 66%, on data centers, servers and other long-lasting assets. It took 78 cents of every dollar of cash Meta’s business brought in, and two years ago it took 37 cents. All of it has to pay off through ads, and Meta can earn it back only one way. Amazon, Microsoft and Alphabet build data centers partly to rent them to other companies, and when AI demand is strong, that rent shows up as cloud sales. Meta builds for its own apps, and its payoff has to come from better ad targeting and new products, which takes longer to show and is harder to measure.

Meta trades at 18.1 times the earnings analysts expect next year, close to Alphabet at 18.8 times. What is missing is proof that the bill will stop growing faster than the business. Meta is already 21% below its high while investors wait for that proof. For every dollar its benchmark lost, the Trefis High Quality (HQ) Portfolio lost about 81 cents on average, holding 30 quality stocks in equal weight. The source is Trefis, using Morningstar data, with each row covering the four quarters to September.

Dec 9 brings the Fed, and a rate hike is widely expected, which makes spending that pays off years from now harder to justify. Late January brings Meta’s next report, expected then, and two numbers to watch are the 2027 spending plan and growth in ad sales. If spending rises less than ads, the worry should ease, and if spending jumps again while ad growth stays flat, the worry should deepen. Early February brings Alphabet and Amazon, whose spending plans set the tone for all of big tech, and their ad businesses are also the closest match to Meta’s.

Alphabet’s side is in Why Is Alphabet Stock Down 30%? If Meta is a large part of what you own, one company’s spending choice decides a lot of your result, which is a good reason to think now about how and when you would sell. If Meta is a big part of your wealth, so are its risk and its tax bill. Our partner advisory firm offers a free 30-minute strategy review covering a floor under losses and a lower-tax way out.

The article is for education, not a recommendation to buy or sell. For questions about the article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com. In Trefis’s view, the gap between spending growth and ad growth will decide where the stock goes. The article leaves open what Meta’s 2027 spending plan will be and how much ad sales will grow.

It leaves open what the Fed will do on Dec 9 beyond the widely expected rate hike. It leaves open what Alphabet and Amazon will plan for spending in early February. It leaves open how and when a holder would sell. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Malaysia exceeds economic growth forecasts as AI demand surges despite US chip license risks
stories.Summary:
Malaysia's economy expanded by 5.5 percent during the third quarter ending in September, which exceeded the initial 5.3 percent estimate from the statistics department. Bank Negara Malaysia reported that growth surged to 6.9 percent in September alone, driven by strong domestic spending and demand for artificial intelligence. This performance contributed to a 5.6 percent growth rate for the first three quarters of 2026, surpassing the government's revised annual forecast of 4.8 to 5.3 percent. The current economic momentum requires careful monitoring of new US Commerce Department rules released on November 16, which mandate licenses for buyers of advanced AI chips. These restrictions target data center operators in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia, and Brazil to prevent US adversaries from accessing offshore computing power.

Governor Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour expects growth to remain above 5 percent in 2026 and believes data center investment will stay strong until 2028. He noted that Chinese companies account for only 13 percent of the 120 data center firms in the country. Governor Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour stated that the economy is well positioned for continued momentum into 2027, though he warned of several downside risks. He identified the re-escalation of conflict in the Middle East, lower commodity production, and disappointing returns from AI as potential threats to growth. While he acknowledged that geopolitical tensions make the impact of US chip rules difficult to gauge, he maintained that the technology upcycle should be sustained.

He also mentioned that businesses have successfully adapted to supply disruptions despite facing higher operational costs. The broader context includes Malaysia's status as a net energy exporter, which has shielded the nation from high fuel prices that affected the Philippines and Thailand. Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has introduced higher minimum wages for 2027 and additional cash aid to help citizens manage cost of living pressures. Meanwhile, economists suggest the central bank may raise its benchmark rate by 25 basis points in the first quarter of 2027 to address building price pressures. The central bank will continue monitoring global developments to ensure the domestic foreign exchange market functions in an orderly manner.

stories.Headline: Anthropic launches Nasdaq IPO to raise 3.5 billion dollars from Japanese investors
stories.Summary:
The artificial intelligence company Anthropic is launching its initial public offering on the Nasdaq stock exchange during the current week of November 18, 2026. This major financial event is occurring as the firm seeks to help humanity navigate a safe path through the evolving age of artificial intelligence. Several prominent AI laboratories across Asia are watching this debut closely to see if it provides a successful roadmap for their own market entries. These regional firms hope that the American listing will protect them from financial instability as they prepare for their own public debuts. The listing process involves a significant amount of capital, as Anthropic aims to raise up to 3.5 billion dollars from investors based in Japan.

This massive influx of funding comes at a time when the broader investment landscape for technology startups has become increasingly selective. The success of this offering could lead to higher valuations and new listings for several Asian companies, including Upstage in South Korea and Sakana in Japan. Additionally, the move may spark similar public offerings for Chinese firms such as Moonshot and DeepSeek. The leadership at Anthropic has stated that their primary goal is to assist humankind in charting a safe course through the era of artificial intelligence.

While the company reports explosive growth in its filing, it also acknowledges the staggering costs and inherent risks associated with developing advanced AI models. Meanwhile, other industry players like TSMC have already earmarked up to 1 billion dollars to purchase shares in both Anthropic and OpenAI. These strategic investments highlight the intense competition and high financial stakes currently defining the global artificial intelligence sector. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Singapore agrees to help US monitor AI chip use and block export control evasion
stories.Summary:
Prime Minister Lawrence Wong announced on November 17 that Singapore can facilitate American checks on the use of artificial intelligence chips within the city-state. This statement followed the November 16 announcement by the United States regarding new export controls on advanced semiconductor chips used for training AI models. These restrictions target five countries, including Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, and Brazil, because the US Department of Commerce views them as having a higher risk of diversion. The American government aims to curb China's access to this technology through overseas data centres, especially after reports of a relationship between Nvidia leader Jensen Huang and Alice Huang.

The new rules require a license to export these advanced chips to the listed countries, which may impact transshipment volumes. Prime Minister Wong noted that while Singapore accounted for 22 percent of Nvidia's global chip revenue in 2025, only 1 percent of those chips were actually used locally. To maintain trusted access to US technology, Singapore and the US agreed on November 17 to study practical arrangements for legitimate users. This cooperation follows a June 2025 on-site review at Megaspeed by the US Bureau of Industry and Security, which occurred after a February 2025 probe by Singapore Customs and the Singapore Police Force.

Prime Minister Wong stated that the government will take clear and firm action against any businesses that use the Republic to breach laws or circumvent export controls. He emphasized the need to uphold the rule of law and maintain the reputation of Singapore as a trusted business hub. Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong echoed these sentiments on November 18, asserting that the state does not condone companies using their association with Singapore to flout international laws. Additionally, Minister Josephine Teo and US Undersecretary Jeffrey Kessler discussed the importance of clear rules to support legitimate commercial activity during a meeting on November 18.

stories.Headline: Hyundai names Park to lead vehicle platform and 42dot, adds Ma, Kim and three technical recruits
stories.Summary:
On January 13, 2026, Hyundai Motor Group named Dr. Minwoo Park as Head of the Advanced Vehicle Platform Division and CEO of 42dot, according to Hyundai's own announcement. Jeremy Ma was appointed head of Hyundai Motor Group's Silicon Valley office inside the AVP Division and concurrently serves as head of 42dot SV. Kim Dong-uk joined as Senior Executive Director after working at Tesla. 42dot recruited three named specialists: Angelo Corsaro as Senior Research Fellow, Kim Jae-young as Gleo AI Model Group Lead, and Chao Fang as SV VLA Team Lead. Follow-up reports came from outlets including BigGo Finance and Financial News.

The available record does not show that three 42dot recruits were all executives, and it does not show that all three came from Apple and NVIDIA. Park worked at NVIDIA as a vice president and led development and commercialization of autonomous-driving perception technology. Ma previously worked at Apple and NVIDIA among other organizations. Fang previously worked as a principal engineer in NVIDIA's autonomous-driving division, where he contributed to autonomous-driving foundation models and to end-to-end perception deployment. The record does not give hiring dates, pay, a headcount target, a budget or a new office address.

Hyundai's announcement said Park led development and commercialization of autonomous-driving perception technology at NVIDIA. The record describes Park's appointment as putting one person in charge of both the group's vehicle-platform engineering and its dedicated software company. Ma's dual title links the parent group's Silicon Valley presence and the software company's local team under one manager. The record says Fang will lead vision-language-action research for autonomous driving. Hyundai did not disclose Park's compensation, and no reliable source gives one.

The record says three of the six confirmed names trace back to NVIDIA, making the chipmaker the single largest talent source in the group's build-out. The record says the roles skew toward model work: perception, VLA research and an AI model group. The record says the Silicon Valley units are the physical expression of a bet that driving-AI research should sit close to where frontier models are trained. The record says the three 42dot recruits' titles read as senior technical roles, not as C-suite hires. The record says nothing found ties any of the three 42dot recruits to Apple.

The record says talent is the scarcest input in AI right now. The record refers to NVIDIA's own leadership drama, described as the Huang exit, as having already shaken the field. The record says a carmaker recruiting from the chip and compute giant's autonomous-driving ranks is buying know-how that took years to build elsewhere. The record says classic autonomy stacks split the job into separate modules for perception, prediction and planning, while VLA-style systems fold more of that pipeline into one learned model. The record says proponents say VLA handles rare situations more gracefully and skeptics worry about verifying behavior no engineer wrote down as a rule.

The record says reports tied to the latest news describe the Silicon Valley organization as expanding. The record says the leadership structure is already in place, which it calls usually the first signal that a regional hub is meant to last. The record says it leaves blank anything the available results do not establish, including hiring dates and pay. The record says it does not give a headcount target, a budget or a new office address. The record says the story is real, but the tidy three-executives-from-two-giants framing overstates it.

stories.Headline: Researchers find thousands of uncensored AI models on major hosting platforms
stories.Summary:
Researchers from Nanyang Technological University in Singapore and University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign analyzed 22,096 uncensored large language models. These researchers identified these models on five major hosting platforms to evaluate their safety and potential for producing harmful content. The study was led by Zilong Lin, who is an assistant professor of computer science at the University of Missouri-Kansas City. This team examined how these unrestrained models are shared and redistributed across the open source AI community. The resulting paper is titled Characterizing the Ecosystem of Open-Source Uncensored Large Language Models: Supply Chain, Governance, and Risks.

The study found uncensored models on US platforms Hugging Face, Kaggle, and John Snow Labs, and China platforms OpenCSG and ModelScope. These models are deployed through GitHub projects, various applications, and model routing platforms such as the service known as Open Router. The researchers noted that the number of these models rose from 100 per month in May 2023 to over 1,000 now. One specific model, dolphin-2.9.1-yi-1.5-34b, has more than 53 million downloads, including 4.8 million downloads in the last month alone. Only about 13 percent of the identified uncensored models carried any warnings regarding moderation for the users.

Zilong Lin stated that these platforms enable the sharing of artifacts, but safety alignment is difficult to assess from model files. He explained that evaluating safety requires deploying models and testing responses, which involves substantial financial and computational costs for researchers. Lin noted that models travel more easily than the information needed to assess risks, creating a significant supply chain problem. He mentioned that his team responsibly disclosed these findings to Open Router, ModelScope, OpenCSG, Kaggle, John Snow Labs, and Hugging Face. OpenCSG responded by saying the research is meaningful and supports the development of a safe and trustworthy LLM ecosystem.

The GAO found that Gemini, ChatGPT, Grok, and Claude can be coaxed to provide information for planning a terror attack. Generative AI helped enable a January 2025 Las Vegas hotel explosive device attack and a February 2026 British Columbia mass shooting. Users of certain apps may not know they are using uncensored models that lack content filtering or refusal safeguards. These models can be misused to assist with malware development or provide guidance about illegal, malicious, or manipulative activities. Twenty-seven models with 136,000 downloads showed threat indicators, including signatures associated with malware or unsafe deserialization mechanisms.

The researchers found that users apply techniques like toxic training or de-aligned training to datasets to remove refusal behavior. Examples of such models include WizardLM-7B-Uncensored and toxicqa-Llama2-13B, while Daredevil-8B-abliterated uses a newer technique called refusal-direction ablation or abliteration. This abliteration technique appeared in 2024 and quickly gained popularity, leading to a growing ecosystem of public tools within two years. Some uncensored models have legitimate uses, such as when Hugging Face used GLM-5.2 from Z.ai to analyze an infrastructure hack. Many of these uncensored models violate the licensing terms of the original models on which they were based.

Lin expects that greater verification, auditability, and transparency of models will help address the risks posed by these uncensored systems. He pointed to the Colorado AI Act and the EU AI Act, which emphasize AI documentation and the use of model cards. The researchers evaluated text output only, leaving the issues of illegal text-to-image generation, such as CSAM, beyond their study scope. It remains difficult to predict if abliteration tools will face legal challenges similar to those faced by cryptographic code in the 1990s. The articles leave open how platforms will handle the gap between model distribution and the preservation of security threat indicators.

stories.Headline: President Lee calls for thorough crackdown against AI-assisted cheating during CSAT
stories.Summary:
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung called on officials Tuesday to thoroughly prepare anti-cheating measures for the nationwide college entrance exam set to take place this week, describing cheating as a grave crime that undermines social trust. Lee made the remarks during an emergency meeting to inspect the country's readiness for the College Scholastic Ability Test, also known in Korean as Suneung, scheduled for Thursday, following widespread concerns over cheating using artificial intelligence. He said during a video meeting held from Manila, as he wrapped up his visit to the city for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit, that the Suneung is a symbol of fairness and a ladder of opportunity in our society. Lee added that the government must take strict action against those who engage in misconduct, adhering to a zero-tolerance policy, while asking officials to come up with response measures against AI-assisted cheating. He said such misconduct could be repeated due to the development of technology and related devices.

In a subsequent social media post, Lee said the government plans to offer a reward of over 100 million won, or about US$74,805, per case to those who report instances of cheating involving advanced gadgets, should the case be confirmed. He wrote on X, formerly known as Twitter, that people should not ruin their life by needlessly gambling on a stroke of luck and should give it up, both for themselves and everyone else. South Korea has been rocked by the recent confession by the top scorer of this year's certified tax accountant exam that he cheated with the help of AI and digital devices. The incident deepened worries that such a method could be used in the upcoming CSAT, prompting the government to announce a series of measures to prevent the exam from being undermined by AI-assisted cheating.

Anti-cheating measures announced earlier Tuesday include physically checking all glasses worn by test takers, covering buttons on their clothes with stickers and blocking Wi-Fi networks inside and near the test sites. The government also warned that test takers caught cheating will be banned from the CSAT for the next 10 years, while facing criminal punishment. The exam is scheduled for Thursday, and the emergency meeting was held to inspect the country's readiness for it. Lee made his remarks from Manila, where he was wrapping up his visit for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit.

stories.Headline: A 34-year-old man confesses to using a hidden camera and generative AI to top Korea's tax accountant exam
stories.Summary:
A 34-year-old man surnamed Han confessed to cheating his way to first place on this year's tax accountant exam, the top scorer, after photographing questions with a miniature camera, sending them to a generative AI program and reading answers off a smartphone. The confession came last weekend, and the exam was this year's tax accountant exam. A 26-year-old woman had spent more than three years trying to become a corrections officer, paying her way between attempts with contract jobs and factory shifts, and said this year is her last try. She said many people put years into these exams in earnest and that trying to get it the easy way with AI tramples on every one of them. She said cheaters should never be given another chance at the exam.

Most Koreans' exams begin at 18 with the College Scholastic Ability Test, a one-day exam held only once a year, so a bad day means waiting a full year to try again. Of the 551,864 people registered for Thursday's exam, 196,473 have already finished high school, the most in 23 years, according to the Korea Institute for Curriculum and Evaluation, which runs the test. More than 12.3 million people in Korea, a country of about 51 million, hold at least one national technical qualification earned through exams run by the Human Resources Development Service of Korea, according to the 2026 statistical yearbook published by the Ministry of Employment and Labor and HRDK. Professional licenses for tax accountants, real estate agents, appraisers and customs brokers are each governed by its own law, and opening a real estate brokerage requires a licensed real estate agent, while even the management office of a larger apartment complex must be headed by a licensed housing manager. Most of these exams, at least in the first round, are multiple choice.

Police say Han attached his camera to a roll of correction tape, and the government has ordered stickers placed over every button on CSAT takers' clothing. On Wednesday, the Education Ministry also barred test-takers from bringing their own computer-marking pens, correction tape, erasers and pencil lead, leaving black pencils as the only writing tools they may bring. On Wednesday, the ruling Democratic Party introduced a bill that would extend the ban to up to 10 years and apply it to this year's CSAT. Under current law, a CSAT taker caught cheating has that year's results invalidated and is barred from taking the exam the following year, but after serving that penalty is free to take the test again. Park Nam-gi, a professor emeritus of education at Gwangju National University of Education, said that to stop them the potential loss has to be made much bigger, with tough rules like a five-year ban.

Cho Sang-sik, a professor of education at Dongguk University, said that because a single sitting decides who passes and who fails, the written exam works like a lottery, and people stake everything on it, which leads them to reckless crimes. Koo Jeong-woo, a sociology professor at Sungkyunkwan University, said that when the fairness of an exam is called into question, people react very sensitively and feel it as a crisis and failure of the national system. On Tuesday, student councils from 15 universities, including Seoul National, Korea and Yonsei universities and KAIST, issued a joint statement titled, "Does effort really never betray you?" Kim, an 18-year-old high school senior, wakes at 7 a.m., studies at school until 9 p.m.

and then at home until midnight, eats every meal at school to save time, sees friends once a month at most and gave up the acoustic guitar long ago. A 34-year-old quit a corporate job after growing anxious about how much longer they could last in the private sector, now lives off savings and studies nearly every waking hour for the customs officer exam, aiming to pass next year. Korea is the world's second-largest market for ChatGPT subscribers, behind only the United States, a country with more than six times its population, according to Microsoft's "Global AI Adoption in 2025" report. Miniature cameras, some no bigger than a fingernail, sell online for 20,000 to 100,000 won, or $15 to $75, and are stocked at Yongsan Electronics Market, a cluster of electronics stores in Yongsan District, central Seoul, several local outlets have reported.

Merchants at Yongsan said inquiries about such cameras had been rising for three to four years, and that since last year some customers had openly asked for devices built for cheating, according to local reports. Police nationwide recorded 7,800 cases of illegal filming last year, up nearly 18 percent from two years earlier, according to the National Police Agency, and nearly nine in 10 victims were women. In the United States, occupational licenses are largely set state by state, and in Germany, vocational exams are run by chambers of commerce and industry. Kim, the high school senior, will walk into a test site on Thursday morning and said that at school all they hear in the hallways, in the bathroom and in the cafeteria is what are we going to do about AI cheating.

A 22-year-old who used to manage a cafe started studying for the grade 9 civil service exam three months ago, still working morning shifts there and leaning on family when money runs short, and said the cheating news felt like being hit hard on the back of the head. Kim Min-jae, 19, who earned a high school equivalency diploma and is sitting the CSAT for the second time, said being judged only by the CSAT felt fairer. An 18-year-old sitting the CSAT for the first time hopes to become a veterinarian and said the CSAT result is basically the result of my life itself. The 26-year-old hoping to become a corrections officer said she hopes to work to help rehabilitate prisoners one day.

Articles.Title: 'People trusted the system': Why an AI cheating scandal has shaken Korea to its core

stories.Headline: KAIST president Bae opens Innovate Korea forum in a robotic suit as 5,000 gather for human-centered AI
stories.Summary:
Innovate Korea 2026 opened on Tuesday at KAIST's Ryu Keun-chul Sports Complex in Daejeon, marking the annual technology and innovation forum's 10th anniversary with a program built around human-centered artificial intelligence. KAIST President Bae Choong-sik opened the forum wearing an Iron Man-inspired robotic suit developed with the university's researchers and students. He was joined by Kim Seung-hwan, a researcher with lower-body paralysis who demonstrated a wearable walking robot built by a KAIST team led by professor Kong Kyoung-chul. The event, jointly hosted by Herald Media Group, KAIST and the National Research Council of Science and Technology, drew some 5,000 attendees, including students, researchers, industry executives and government officials. It was held under the theme "NEXT 10 Years, You Are the Protagonist: Beyond AI, Humanity First."

During a special anniversary discussion moderated by television personality Park Kyung-lim, Herald Media Group CEO and publisher Choi Jin-young stressed the importance of preserving human values amid rapid technological change. He said technology may pave the way, but ultimately it is people who walk that path, and he called for empathy, reflection and critical thinking in the AI era. Bae identified physical AI, which enables intelligent systems to interact with the real world, as a key opportunity for South Korea over the next decade, citing the country's strengths in manufacturing and robotics. Bae said the goal is to use technology to help people move more freely and pursue the lives they want.

A subsequent panel discussion brought together Ha Jung-woo, vice chair of the National AI Strategy Committee, and Hong Won-hwa, chair of the National Research Foundation of Korea. It also included Jin Yo-han, head of LG CNS' AI Center, and Yoon Kuk-jin, dean of KAIST's AI graduate school. The speakers discussed the country's ambition to become one of the world's top three AI powers, alongside challenges involving talent development, industrial adoption and equitable access to technology. The forum concluded with performances by musical stars Kim Junsu, Cha Ji-yeon, Jung Sun-ah, Ivy and Park Kang-hyun, accompanied by an orchestra led by music director Kim Moon-jung, and singer Kwon Eun-bi also took the stage.

stories.Headline: AI cheating crackdown sparks online mockery
stories.Summary:
Prime Minister Han Seong-sook announced tougher measures on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, to prevent AI-assisted cheating during the College Scholastic Ability Test. These heightened security protocols were implemented for the exam held on Thursday, November 20, 2026, which was taken by 551,864 students. The government introduced these strict rules to stop students from using miniature cameras and other AI-enabled devices to cheat. The new requirements force all test-takers to place their glasses on desks for inspection to detect smart glasses. Supervisors must check collars and buttons for hidden devices, and students are required to roll up both sleeves.

Officials will place stickers over every button on a student's clothing and replace any that fall off. The ministry also provided approved writing tools to further deter the use of unauthorized electronic equipment. Prime Minister Han Seong-sook is responsible for these measures, which the government claims are necessary to ensure exam fairness. However, online critics have mocked the plan, calling the button stickers ridiculous and questioning if the inspections are practical. Some commenters suggested that the government should provide standardized clothing or disposable aprons to avoid these tedious checks.

Others argued that the jokes stem from a lack of real solutions to the problem of AI cheating. The crackdown follows reports of AI-assisted cheating tools being sold on Telegram and a tax exam top scorer allegedly testing devices. Satirical AI images have since spread online, depicting students in swimsuits and diving helmets to mock the security. Some images show electronics stores in the Yongsan district claiming credit for students' admissions to Seoul National University. These memes suggest that sophisticated devices could eventually make private academies irrelevant for academic success.

Articles.Title: AI cheating crackdown sparks online mockery

stories.Headline: South Korean students swap thick glasses for rimless frames as proctors screen for AI smart glasses at the 2027 exam
stories.Summary:
Students preparing for the College Scholastic Ability Test on Thursday are replacing their thick glasses with rimless or thin designs. This sudden trend emerged after the government announced that proctors would inspect every test-taker for AI-powered smart glasses. Many students fear that ordinary eyewear might be mistaken for cheating devices, which could disrupt their concentration during the exam. This anxiety grew following a confession on Sunday by the top scorer of this year's tax accountant certification exam. That individual admitted to using electronic devices and artificial intelligence to cheat during the professional certification test.

The new security measures require proctors to check glasses before each session to prevent the use of concealed electronic devices. The government has also supplied approved writing tools and button-cover stickers to stop the use of miniature cameras. According to industry data, sales of rimless glasses on the Musinsa platform rose 56 percent from Sunday to Monday. Gold-rimmed glasses saw a 40 percent increase during that same period compared to November 8 and 9. The prime minister stated that anyone caught cheating could be barred from taking the exam for up to 10 years.

A representative of the Korean Optometric Association noted that shops see five or six students daily switching their frames. This official explained that students usually avoid changing glasses before exams but are doing so now to avoid suspicion. One parent mentioned buying new glasses for their son because thick black frames might look like smart glasses to proctors. Other students have turned to online communities to ask if their current eyewear looks like a cheating device. Some test-takers have decided to wear contact lenses instead of glasses to avoid any potential issues with the examiners.

These heightened security checks were implemented as 551,864 students sat for the 2027 College Scholastic Ability Test nationwide. Officials are focusing on phones, smart glasses, and other AI-enabled devices to maintain the integrity of the entrance exam. Police are also investigating other cases, including a missing person who allegedly cheated on a law school admission test. While officials reported no confirmed cheating with miniature cameras, the government remains vigilant against high-tech fraud. The overall atmosphere reflects a growing tension between students and the strict new anti-cheating protocols.

stories.Summary:

stories.Headline: Lee Jin-woo skips pledged Suneung livestream as police probe AI cheating claims
stories.Summary:
Lee Jin-woo, the top scorer on this year's Legal Education Eligibility Test, failed to appear for a livestream he had pledged to hold on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026, at the Daechi IDA Admissions Research Institute in Gangnam-gu, Seoul, where he was scheduled to arrive by 8:40 a.m. The 32-year-old first-year dentistry student at Seoul National University had planned to solve the Korean-language section of Thursday's Suneung exam in real time. Instructors from Megastudy and Daesung MyMac, as well as reporters, were to be present for the livestream. Lee failed to appear and could not be reached despite repeated attempts to contact him. An official at Daechi IDA said his phone was turned off and he had not responded to KakaoTalk messages, and that they had been trying to reach him since the previous day.

Lee had planned to answer 56 questions in just 65 minutes, covering both elective subjects, Speech and Writing as well as Language and Media, while the Korean-language section normally allows 80 minutes for 45 questions. The livestream was to run on his Instagram account from 9:30 a.m. to 12:20 p.m. Thursday at the Daechi IDA institute in Gangnam-gu, Seoul. Lee earned perfect scores in both the reading comprehension and logical reasoning sections of the LEET, administered in July for admission to law schools in 2027.

The LEET was introduced in 2008 as the country transitioned from the traditional bar examination system to a law school system, and it assesses applicants' reading comprehension, logical reasoning and aptitude for legal studies rather than their knowledge of law, and also includes an essay-writing section that individual law schools may consider. Lee was not the first person to achieve a perfect score on the LEET, as a legal professional who ranked first nationwide in the 2013 exam also earned full marks, news reports said. Lee explained that he misinterpreted the questions' requirements after losing concentration toward the end of the exam. He told a local news outlet that the livestream was intended to quickly verify his abilities using newly released exam questions that could not have been leaked in advance. He had also faced allegations of falsifying his past Suneung score reports, and the reports he posted on social media for the exams he took in 2012, 2017, 2023 and 2025 all bore his current name, Lee Jin-woo, which he adopted after legally changing his name.

He had previously used a different name while attending Korea University before enrolling at Seoul National University, raising questions about whether the reports had been altered. An official from the Korea Institute for Curriculum and Evaluation, which administers the exam, told Newsis that score reports generally retain the name used at the time of registration unless formally changed through administrative procedures. Questions about Lee's performance arose after he showed his exam booklet in an interview with YouTuber Mimiminu, known for content on college entrance exam preparation, and viewers noticed that Lee had corrected his answers to questions 25 through 29, with his original choices matching the correct answers to questions 24 through 28, fueling speculation that he had mistakenly shifted answers copied from an outside source. Some speculated that he may have mistakenly shifted the answers by one question while copying them from an external source, possibly AI, and the fact that the corrections appeared on the test booklet itself, rather than on the answer sheet where such mistakes typically occur, fueled further suspicions.

The controversy gained momentum following a separate case in which the highest scorer on this year's national tax accountant qualification exam admitted to using AI to obtain answers during the tests. Lee faced similar allegations over his Suneung results, in which he got just one question wrong, and a person claiming to have tutored Lee just days before last year's college entrance exam said he lacked even basic high school-level knowledge of biology. His reported Suneung scores show a dramatic improvement over the years: in 2012, in his first Suneung, he received grades of 6 to 8 across subjects on a nine-grade scale with 1 being the highest and 9 the lowest, in his second exam in 2017 he scored 7 in Korean language, 1 in math and 4 in English with grades of 2 to 3 in the remaining subjects, by 2023 his grades had improved to grades of 1 or 2 in major subjects, and for last year's exam he earned the top grade of 1 in every subject. Police have launched an investigation into Lee over allegations of cheating on the LEET and last year's Suneung, following a criminal complaint filed Wednesday by Bang Min-woo of Min Law Firm and Park Eun-sun of Reason Law Office on charges including obstruction of business.

Nearly 552,000 students registered for the final exam under the current system, and parents braved freezing temperatures outside a Seoul testing center on the tense Suneung morning. President Lee Jae Myung on Tuesday ordered additional measures to curb AI-assisted cheating during Thursday's college entrance exam, with a proposed reward of at least 100 million won, or $75,000, for tips. A separate report addressed why phones across Korea blared emergency alerts Thursday, even on silent. The articles leave open whether Lee will reschedule the livestream and what the police investigation will find.

stories.Headline: AI accelerators push designers to adopt vertical power delivery as currents near kiloamperes
stories.Summary:
The articles report that AI accelerators and GPUs now consume thousands of amperes at increasingly low voltages, pushing a shift to vertical power delivery that moves regulation closer to loads, as described in a November 19, 2026 semiengineering.com article. A 600W GPU running near 0.7 V forces current to rise to 1,000 amps and beyond, compounding resistive losses and voltage droop across the power delivery network. Multi-chiplet constructions compound these issues by further increasing current density and signal congestion. Designers are turning to vertical power delivery networks that relocate voltage regulator modules from the device periphery to the PCB landside, inside the accelerator package, or inside the silicon interposer. The vertical PDN trend began nearly a decade ago with backside power delivery networks on the wafer backside, enabling fine-tuned power delivery directly to transistors while reducing IR drop across tens of on-chip interconnect levels.

The articles state that backside PDNs are being extended with on-die decoupling capacitors formed in deep trenches as part of the BPDN. Recent changes inside packages, interposers, substrates, and across data center racks are becoming just as important, alongside compact passive devices like high-performance inductors. The changes involve system co-design of the PDN, interposer, power management ICs, integrated voltage regulators, DC-DC converters, capacitors, and other passives, alongside custom HPC, memory devices, and interconnects. Intel Foundry's 18A was the first to move backside wafer processing in leading-edge high-volume manufacturing, and Samsung and TSMC plan to implement backside PDNs at future advanced nodes starting next year. ASE, Marvell, Empower, and others are moving voltage regulation closer to the processor, and integration of compact passive components is becoming a key differentiator in high-density power delivery.

Nir Sever, senior director of business development at proteanTecs, said people in the most advanced semiconductors are moving from discrete PMICs to distributed IVRs placed much closer to the chip, reducing IR drop to the chip's own PDN. He said closed and fast control loops between the chip power management unit and the IVR reduce reaction time to voltage droop events from milliseconds to microseconds, allowing voltage to be tuned accurately with high granularity even on different areas of a chip. Lipen Yuan, senior director of TSMC's Advanced Technology Business Development, said during a 2024 IEDM short course that energy efficiency becomes the most important performance index for AI-infused platforms moving forward. CP Hung, vice president of corporate R&D at ASE, said AI systems are placing unprecedented demands on board-to-chip power delivery, making the final stage of voltage regulation increasingly important. Harrison Chang, vice president of corporate R&D at ASE, said power efficiency is becoming a defining challenge for next-generation AI systems, and that by shortening the high-current transmission path, the company's solution can reduce parasitic routing losses by 50% or more.

Sojan Philips, principal product manager of Redhawk-SC at Synopsys, said the move to multi-die architectures is bringing power integrity to the forefront alongside thermal, stress, and warpage challenges, but the underlying power-delivery problem already existed in advanced single-die designs. He said AI accelerators now operate at currents approaching the kiloampere range, where even milliohm-level resistance in the PDN can result in significant IR drop, and that loss of voltage margin can directly affect performance and power targets, particularly maximum operating frequency and V min. He also said backside power delivery can significantly improve power delivery by reducing IR drop and freeing frontside routing resources for signals, but it does not eliminate power-integrity challenges and changes the thermal landscape, making co-optimization of power integrity and thermal management increasingly important. Alex Kizeev, technical director of signal and power integrity at Amkor's design optimization team, said the OSAT sits where die, substrate or interposer, passives, and board meet, so OSATs are brought in earlier to model the package-level PDN and co-simulate it with the customer's die power data. Kizeev said the best results come from a PDN budget partitioned across the die, package, and board, with foundry and fabless teams owning the on-die PDN including the die power map and bump-map allocation, the substrate supplier defining stackup and via/plane technology, and the OSAT optimizing package-level pieces including stackup choice, via and ball assignment, DCap selection and placement, warpage and reliability, and validation.

The articles state that power delivery is now a significant performance limiter in data center chips, and that power delivery is becoming a system-level co-design challenge, expanding simulation needs and the role of OSATs. A simple illustration shows power efficiency dropping as the industry scales from a 1kW GPU to a 5kW GPU, with losses from the voltage regulator itself staying constant at around 13%, resistive losses jumping from 8% to 31%, and voltage droop rising from 17% to 31%. With lateral power delivery, power integrity becomes increasingly difficult to maintain as compute loads rise, and the low supply voltage of 0.7-0.9V means multiple kiloamp levels of current are needed to meet the high-power needs of modern GPUs. Fast workload transients tend to magnify voltage droop, so designers apply voltage guardbands that further increase power consumption and reduce system efficiency. For next-generation data centers built to meet AI demands, 800V DC power delivery is starting to replace traditional AC power distribution, coexisting with multiple distributed regulators located much closer to individual loads.

The articles state that next-generation PDNs begin at 800V DC and are stepped down in stages using DC-to-DC converters to 48V, 12V, and then 0.7V, for instance, with one of the most critical junctures at the point of load where integrated voltage regulators supply the AI multi-chiplet package. By limiting the number of power conversions, system-level efficiency can improve while reducing thermal cooling requirements. The voltage regulator module can be positioned underneath the PCB, a logical first step commonly referred to as vertical power delivery, while moving voltage regulation inside the main processor package and below the SoC is called integrated power delivery, and integrating voltage regulator components into the interposer itself is called fully integrated power delivery. The approach companies take depends on the company's expertise, its partners, and the complexity of the system involved. ASE is offering a range of power delivery capabilities to enable PCB backside integration, which considers the limited space inside computer trays, and its PowerSiP options can include double-sided connected capacitors sandwiched between coreless substrates, substrateless designs, solder-free cap array modules with exposed terminals for embedded substrate or PCB solutions, high-aspect-ratio 4:1 copper pin integration for lower packaging impedance, and high-density active and passive component integration using single- or double-sided molding.

stories.Headline: Korean teachers doubt proctors can detect AI cheating as students seek tougher CSAT checks
stories.Summary:
South Korean teachers and students voiced concern ahead of Thursday’s College Scholastic Ability Test that proctors may not be able to detect AI-assisted cheating, The Korea Times reported on Nov. 17, 2026. The anxiety followed a top scorer’s admission on Sunday that he used a miniature camera and generative AI to cheat on a national tax accountant licensing exam. The confession reversed his earlier denials, which came after public scrutiny over his unusually high marks. Amid the alarm, the government is pursuing measures including blocking access to public Wi-Fi at CSAT sites. The CSAT is so high-stakes in Korea that even air traffic is halted during its English listening section.

Huh Jin-man, 53, a high school teacher of 25 years who will proctor the CSAT on Thursday, said a full Wi-Fi shutdown still leaves a loophole because smartphones can connect via 5G and other networks. He said being trained does not mean teachers can spot AI tools right away, and that many scenarios and variables leave them wondering how it will turn out. He said teachers should still check students even if it may not always be possible, because the hard work of the honest majority must not go to waste. He expects screening to tighten in future exams but said how students are tested or evaluated will have to change, with some skeptics calling the current CSAT meaningless. Another teacher in his 60s, identified only by his surname Jung, said the news talks about pea-sized cameras and asked how anyone could possibly detect them.

Jung said the main worry for proctors is how to respond at all, citing supervising female students as an example, and that a proctor can do little without a student’s cooperation, while forcing a search could land the proctor in trouble. Paek Young-sun, 38, an elementary school teacher of 12 years, said stopping students on suspicion of cheating brings claims that teachers ruined their CSAT, and teachers have even been sued over that, while ignoring a student who seems to be cheating brings blame for lax supervision. Kim Tae-hoon, a senior at Donong High School in Namyangju, Gyeonggi Province, said that with no surefire fix like an electromagnetic pulse to disable devices, it all comes down to proctors and mistakes will happen. He said it would be unfair for those who studied hard to lose out to someone with AI. His friend Lee Soo-hyun wondered how many people have already cheated using AI in recent years without getting caught.

Another senior who spoke on condition of anonymity said education authorities are acting irresponsibly by pushing ahead without effective countermeasures. He warned that the spotlight on AI glasses may lead proctors to scrutinize only eyeglasses and similar wearables, pushing cheaters toward other tiny devices. He said even a full internet and Wi-Fi shutdown does little against on-device AI, which runs on a built-in chip without a network, so belongings should be inspected more thoroughly even if check-in starts earlier, and test sites need detectors that can pick up internal circuitry and metal. He said some may worry about cost and staffing, but that is a price worth paying for a fair exam.

stories.Headline: AI Digital forecasts AI agents will take over media buying decisions in 2027
stories.Summary:
A new forecast from the media consultancy AI Digital predicts that artificial intelligence agents will increasingly take control of media buying decisions in 2027, shifting campaign execution, optimization and budget allocation from humans to automated systems. The company’s Media Trends 2027 report, released on November 19, 2026, outlines nine predictions for the coming year, including changes in how advertising is purchased, measured and evaluated. While the report does not specifically examine audio advertising, several of its forecasts have implications for radio and podcast companies seeking to remain competitive as advertisers embrace automation. The report says the shift could intensify pressure on audio companies to demonstrate advertising effectiveness, improve measurement and prove their value against competing digital platforms.

The report cites research from the Interactive Advertising Bureau showing that 82% of respondents familiar with agentic AI ad buying already use or are likely to use it for budget allocation, pacing and optimization. Another 84% report current or potential use for planning and buying recommendations, while 93% say the same for performance analysis. Those figures combine adoption and intended use among 161 respondents, rather than measuring how widely the technology has already been deployed. AI Digital also predicts that creative performance will play a greater role in determining how advertising dollars are distributed, with advertisers increasingly testing creative executions and using performance data to guide subsequent spending. Another prediction centers on measurement, with marketers expected to make greater progress connecting brand awareness campaigns with actual sales and reducing their reliance on traditional measures of exposure and engagement.

AI Digital CEO Stephen Magli said more media decisions in 2027 will run through an AI system before they reach a customer, and that an agent will chase a cheaper acquisition cost all day even if those customers were going to buy anyway. He said the agent only knows what you told it to care about, and that the company built the guide so marketers can act on each of these changes while 2027 plans are still being written. For audio ad sellers, the potential shift raises questions about how automated buying systems will evaluate audio against other media, and demonstrating measurable campaign performance could become even more important. Audio companies may face greater pressure to demonstrate which executions produce results and how those outcomes compare with other advertising formats, which could strengthen the importance of attribution studies, sales-lift research and other tools designed to demonstrate advertising effectiveness.

The report also forecasts changes in brand safety practices that could have implications for news and talk programming, with advertisers expected to move away from keyword-based blocking toward systems that evaluate the broader context of content. It cites an Integral Ad Science audit in which keyword blocking flagged 54% of Reuters news stories online that had already passed the company’s brand standards, illustrating how broad keyword restrictions can exclude otherwise acceptable advertising environments. AI Digital says a shift toward contextual evaluation could potentially benefit news and political podcasts whose discussions of sensitive subjects might otherwise trigger advertising exclusions. The report also predicts political advertising will retreat from 2026 levels, although demand could still be robust in some markets where state and local elections fill the calendar.

stories.Headline: Retailers remove Contixo AI toy after it gives children graphic descriptions of violence
stories.Summary:
Several major retailers recently removed listings for the Contixo AI Pixie-Paw after reports surfaced about its disturbing behavior. This plush cat with video screens for eyes was marketed to children as young as 3 years old for safe roleplay and learning. NBC News reporters discovered that the toy provided graphic descriptions of executions and gang rape when asked about historical atrocities. These troubling discoveries occurred shortly before the Black Friday shopping season in November 2026. The removal of the product from Target, Walmart, Macy's, and Amazon follows a pattern of failures in AI toys.

Other tested chatbots switched languages unexpectedly or misspelled simple words like apple despite being marketed for preschoolers and children with autism. A report from the consumer safety group PIRG last year indicated that some AI toys engaged in sexual talk with young children. Some of these devices also promoted Chinese government talking points by claiming that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China. Katie Notopoulos of Business Insider warned parents against buying these companions because children cannot easily distinguish chatbots from real beings.

She noted that the Grok rocket doll from Curio, which launched in December 2023, suffered from clunky latency and limited utility. Notopoulos also mentioned the $800 Moxie robot, which became useless after the company ran out of money and shut down its technical support. She argued that the risks of emotional attachment and technical failure outweigh any potential academic or social benefits. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Morgan Stanley's Simkowitz says AI buildout has enough capital but power supply constrains growth
stories.Summary:
Morgan Stanley Co-President Dan Simkowitz said on November 19, 2026 that the firm sees enough capital to finance the artificial intelligence buildout. He spoke with Magdalena Stoklosa, Morgan Stanley's director of Asia research, at the 25th anniversary of the firm's Asia summit. Simkowitz warned that demand for AI funding could raise financing costs for other borrowers. He also said power supply remains a constraint on the buildout. The article was published by MarketBeat and appeared on Yahoo Finance.

Morgan Stanley estimates more than $1 trillion in equity will be raised for the AI ecosystem by the end of 2028. Simkowitz said the total had already surpassed $800 billion after the day's activity. AI-related financing has expanded beyond traditional unsecured debt to structures backed by lease payments, chips and guarantees on the residual value of chips. He pointed to the role of private credit and insurance capital in funding the buildout. Morgan Stanley's research team sees power as the principal bottleneck, reflecting insufficient investment in U.S. power generation and grid efficiency.

Simkowitz said the AI market can have all kinds of periods of excess and misallocation of capital. He characterized conditions as reasonably normal for now, given the volume of capital being absorbed and the pace of change. He said Morgan Stanley was the lead bookrunner and sole stabilization agent for Anthropic's offering, and declined to discuss further details, citing legal constraints. He said corporate mergers and acquisitions are very, very busy. He attributed the pickup partly to companies executing strategies after several years of subdued deal volumes, favorable access to credit and a potential regulatory window that he said could end in January 2029.

Simkowitz said AI tools were first used inside Morgan Stanley to improve financial-adviser productivity and are now deployed in software coding, cybersecurity, research, investment management and investment banking. He said the firm expects to write off a fair amount of existing software in the current quarter because of newer AI tools, without specifying an amount. He said the wealth business has grown from roughly 3 million households eight years ago to 21 million, while the financial-adviser count has stayed relatively flat. He put assets under management in the business at approximately $8.5 trillion, up from roughly $3 trillion.

He said retail clients have remained engaged in equity markets and have been seeking higher yields. Simkowitz said private equity firms are interested in buying assets but have been selling less than he expected. He said pressure from investors and employees could encourage more sales over time. He said the market for initial public offerings remains accessible, although the bar is high for companies without substantial scale or growth.

He described the development of Asian equity markets as a significant opportunity, pointing to corporate-governance reforms in Japan and efforts to deepen capital markets elsewhere in the region. He said Morgan Stanley's long-standing relationship with Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, which he said holds more than a 20% stake in the firm, supports its goal of becoming Japan's leading securities firm, where it currently ranks second. Simkowitz said Morgan Stanley plans to keep investing in Asian wealth management, alongside opportunities in U.S. investment banking, fixed income and commodities. He cited the firm's stock-plan administration business as a way to reach potential clients in wealth management.

The article says the firm will continue to look for opportunities to replace legacy software. The article does not give the amount of the software write-off or further details of the Anthropic offering. The article does not say when the power bottleneck might ease. More to follow.

stories.Headline: AI-Led Development Made Features Cheap. Your Users Still Can't Find Them.
stories.Summary:
Tanya Donska wrote in a Hackernoon article published on November 19th, 2026, about a client who built a real-time co-editing feature, similar to Google Docs but for their data workflows, because users kept asking for it. The build took three months and cost close to 100,000 US dollars, yet six months later only 8% of users had touched the feature. People kept requesting it even after it went live, filing about 47 requests a month through ideas or GitHub issues, and most of those people were paying customers on different plans, while the power users stayed almost silent. The feature sat in Settings, then Workspace, then Collaboration, behind a toggle called "Enable real-time editing", with nothing in onboarding. The founder explained that it was a premium feature and they did not want to confuse free users by showing it if they could not use it, even though 64% of their users were on paid plans.

Donska tracked the feature for about 20 to 25 days and found that 8% of users found the toggle in Settings by accident, 12% asked and were told where it was, and 3% read the changelog, while the other 77% never found it. She changed three things, none of which was a redesign: onboarding got one line of about 10 seconds saying users could collaborate in real time by clicking any document to invite teammates, a small prompt appeared when a document was opened alone asking whether the user was working solo and suggesting inviting teammates, and the toggle moved out of Settings to become a Collaboration button in the header of every document. Within 30 days, 81% of users had found it, usage on paid plans rose from 8% to 47%, and requests fell from 47 a month to 11. Nothing in the feature itself changed, and Donska wrote that three months of engineering were saved by a button and one sentence.

Donska described how such features now get built: a person sees a request on X.com for a similar product, asks the opinion of 25 to 40 people who say it is a nice idea, and then builds it in two or three weeks of what she called a vibe-coded experience costing around 10 grand, at a cost to their health and mental well-being. She said nobody in that process asks where the feature goes, so it goes to Settings, and she argued that a feature more than two clicks away signals what she called vibe-coded work that would not help users at all. She listed four problems: paid features are either hidden or pushed for payment on the first settings panel without a trial, Settings becomes a dump for time zones, notifications, passwords and every feature the team could not place, launches rely on changelogs that only 3% read instead of websites and emails, and landing pages promise too much and do too little because no designer or planning meeting asks where people will actually see the feature. She advised reading last month's requests before opening Claude Code for the next feature and counting how many ask for something already built, and she wrote that AI will build a feature by Thursday but has no idea where to put it.

Articles.Title: AI-Led Development Made Features Cheap. Your Users Still Can't Find Them.

stories.Headline: Tony Fadell becomes Smartex chairman as it launches AI fabric inspection for H&M
stories.Summary:
Tony Fadell, the co-designer of the iPod, iPhone and Nest doorbell, is coming aboard as chairman of Smartex, a company launching a physical AI product for fabric quality checks, Fortune reported on November 19, 2026. Fadell has invested roughly $10 million in Smartex, which has been working with him on the product. The product can perform fabric quality checks continuously, at three times the speed of a human. H&M, also an investor in Smartex, is one of its launch customers. Max Easton, CEO of Smartex, spoke to Fortune at Web Summit in Lisbon this year.

Smartex is rolling out two new products, Smartex Inspect and Smartex IQ. Smartex Inspect is a physical AI camera system that attaches to existing textile machinery to monitor the quality of material as it goes by. Smartex IQ generates intelligence from the supply chain data that comes from Smartex's suite of products. Smartex has about 65 employees, revenues in the low millions annually, and has installed 800 of its older monitoring systems at clients in 10 different countries. The company's valuation four years ago was $55 million, and Easton declined to give an updated number.

Fadell said fabric inspection is very, very technical and highly prone to human error. He said it is all subjective depending on whether it is in the morning or the afternoon or on Friday afternoon, and there is no Pantone color for quality inspection. He said that if you walked into a mill or a garment facility 50 years ago and walk into it today, it is almost exactly the same, same processes, same equipment, same everything. He said it has not been upgraded in any way, and they might have email, and in some cases they do not even have Wi-Fi. Fadell said this is something he has been investing in for a decade now, because he believes in very, very applied AI in the physical world, but you have got to make it really easy for the customers to use.

Easton said most of the work is done by hand, and checking the quality of the fabric will be performed by a worker holding a handful of color swatches, watching a roll of cloth go by all day. He said workers are looking for simple physical defects like holes, needles, the wrong yarn, something that would be noticeable in a garment. He said that if you go to any kind of fashion supply chain, whether it is fabric production or garment production, most people are just kind of amazed by how chaotic it is. Easton said companies are at the mercy of independent operators in multiple foreign countries and have zero visibility, even when the product arrives, and they do not know when it is going to arrive. He said that for any player in the apparel chain, 50% of their cost-base is fabric, but because the product is so variable in quality, a company like H&M will typically over-order about 5% more fabric than they need.

Easton said that globally at H&M that is like 2.5 billion meters of fabric every single year, just in case, and at $4 a meter that adds up to $10 billion in fabric costs. Easton reckons Smartex might save H&M $100 million annually simply by reducing its waste. Fadell said there are four things that H&M cares about: price, speed, quality and sustainability. He said a lot of times they commit to making this garment and pre-sell it online, but they cannot deliver it because the fabric shows up at the garment house and they cannot make the garment because the fabric is wrong in some way. Fadell said reducing waste means better margins.

The fashion business thrives on the conceit that it is modern, on-trend and all about what is happening right now, but behind the scenes, in the textile mills and garment factories that supply major brands, is an industry that runs much as it did in the 1970s. Its supply chains are splintered, chaotic and based in warehouses that are so old-fashioned they may not even be on the internet, according to Easton. For most brands, there is no such thing as a white T-shirt, and it needs to be exactly the right shade of white, which might be a brilliant white or a creamier off-white. Because the work is inspected by humans, fashion brands can never be quite sure that the quality of the fabric they are buying is going to be consistent, or even match what they ordered. The challenge is not as simple as pointing a camera at a textile processor and sending it to a computer, and the system has to take account of changes in lighting, the speed at which the fabric is moving and small variations in color, and calibrate all that against a client's own standards.

Smartex has a library of 50 billion images of fabric to do that calibration. The articles do not say when Smartex Inspect and Smartex IQ will become available or what they will cost. The articles do not say how many of the new products H&M will install or where. The articles do not give an updated valuation for Smartex. The articles do not say what share of Smartex Fadell's roughly $10 million investment bought.

stories.Headline: Microsoft unveils partner incentives and AI agent tools at Ignite 2026
stories.Summary:
Microsoft used its Ignite 2026 conference to place partners at the centre of what it calls a Frontier Transformation era, highlighting a projected US$31 trillion AI market by 2030, according to ARN. To help drive partner-led AI growth, the company unveiled a raft of new incentives, specialisations and go-to-market programs. Microsoft chief partner officer and VP for global channel partner sales Nicole Dezen said partners are increasingly looking beyond internal productivity improvements and focusing on AI as a revenue-generating opportunity. According to figures Dezen cited from IDC, the AI market is expected to grow 4.5 times by 2030, while 47 per cent of partners surveyed expect new revenue streams to rank among their top three AI priorities over the next year.

New investments were revealed across the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program, including expanded partner benefits packages featuring Microsoft 365 Copilot Business licences, additional Dragon Copilot licences, Azure credits and Copilot Studio capacity. Microsoft is also introducing a new Agentic Partner Capability Score aimed at recognising partners building and deploying AI agents, while expanding the Partner Skilling Hub with dedicated frontier learning journeys focused on AI transformation engagements. Dezen pointed to Microsoft's own research as evidence that deeper AI adoption within partner organisations translates into stronger business outcomes, citing the Microsoft AI Partner Economics Value Indicator Study finding that partners with high AI maturity generate 67 per cent more partner revenue per dollar of Microsoft AI revenue than those with low AI maturity. The company also unveiled a new Frontier Partner specialisation designed to recognise partners capable of designing, deploying, securing and governing AI agents across Microsoft's technology stack.

Alongside the partner program updates, Microsoft revealed product announcements spanning Copilot, Azure, Fabric and security technologies, with a key theme being the evolution of Copilot beyond conversational AI into a platform for delegated work and business process automation. Among the headline technology announcements was Microsoft IQ, a new enterprise context management platform designed to combine organisational data, knowledge, skills and tools through more than 350 third-party connectors. On the infrastructure front, Microsoft announced Azure Cobalt 200 virtual machines, which it claims deliver up to 50 per cent better performance than the previous generation, while outlining new opportunities for application and database modernisation through Azure Catalyst, Azure HorizonDB and updates to Azure Database services. Microsoft also introduced Agent 365, an observability platform for managing AI estates across Copilot deployments, agents, models and third-party AI services, and expanded governance and risk management capabilities through Microsoft Entra Suite and Dynamic Agent Risk.

In the commercial channel, Microsoft is doubling down on co-sell motions and marketplace-led growth, reporting a 70 per cent increase in co-sell eligible solutions sold through Microsoft Marketplace this fiscal year and introducing new programs including Sales Recommender and Partner Center for Sales. IDC data cited by Dezen suggests those efforts could pay off, with sell-focused partners generating nearly three times the economic value of build-focused partners. Managed services are also emerging as a key growth area, with 60 per cent of partners in IDC's survey reporting that managed services led to additional engagements with existing customers more than half the time. Dezen said partners remain central to translating AI innovation into business outcomes, telling them they are the market makers and that every customer transformation creates new opportunity.

Articles.Title: Microsoft pitches $31T AI opportunity as partners push beyond productivity gains

stories.Headline: Microsoft lets businesses customize its AI models with their own data via Licensed Weights
stories.Summary:
Microsoft announced Licensed Weights during the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, November 18, 2026, with CEO Satya Nadella presenting several new models from Microsoft AI, the company’s internal lab. The initiative lets customers customize Microsoft’s frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure, according to the company. Mustafa Suleyman, the CEO of Microsoft AI, described the arrangement on stage as a selective approach to open-weight AI that sits between fully proprietary models and fully downloadable ones. Interested companies will need to go through their Microsoft account representatives to get started with the program.

The approach is meant to appeal to businesses that want affordable AI while keeping control over their intellectual property, and Microsoft said it would use customers’ information to train its models only if they agreed. Suleyman said customers control who can access the customized model and that their data and adaptations stay entirely theirs, with Microsoft working through Frontier Company to deliver the model and embed it in their products and agents. He also remarked that no one wants to pour their IQ into someone else’s model, a nod to an argument Palantir CEO Alex Karp has made repeatedly. The announcement came alongside MAI Code 2, a coding model that Suleyman said delivers 98% of the performance of GPT 6.1 Sol at just 40% of the cost, and 5% of the cost against Opus 5.5 on four widely used benchmarks for everyday enterprise coding tasks. Microsoft also released its image editing model MAI Image 2.7 on Tuesday, which the article says now leads its category on Artificial Analysis while beating Nano Banana Pro and several GPT image models on price and quality.

Microsoft’s own models do not necessarily compete with OpenAI and Anthropic yet, but the company has legacy sway with countless businesses, and the article says Licensed Weights could strike a balance among major tech companies. Western labs including Thinking Machines and Mistral are releasing more competitive open-weight models, though Anthropic and OpenAI still hold the overwhelming majority of the enterprise AI market. Licensed Weights is not an open-weight family of models, but it diversifies the open-versus-closed debate somewhat and differentiates Microsoft’s offering from those of OpenAI and Anthropic. The article frames the initiative as a smart pairing with Microsoft’s goal of balancing price and performance, and it positions the company for organizations seeking a blend of return-on-investment tools, customization, security controls and capability.
